sentences.zh: 文成五王、獻文六王、孝文六王

translations.literal: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, and Xiaowen's Six Sons
translations.idiomatic: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, and Xiaowen's Six Sons

sentences.zh: 安樂王長樂，皇興四年，封建昌王，後改封安樂王。

translations.literal: Prince of Anle Chang Le, in the fourth year of Huangxing was enfeoffed Prince of Changchang; later he was reassigned Prince of Anle.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Le, Prince of Anle, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changchang in the fourth year of Huangxing and later reassigned as Prince of Anle.

sentences.zh: 長樂性凝重，獻文器愛之。

translations.literal: Chang Le's nature was grave and steady; Xianwen prized and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Steady and grave by nature, Chang Le was a favorite of Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 承明元年，拜太尉，出為定州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chengming he was appointed Grand Commandant and sent out as Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming he became Grand Commandant and went out as Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 頓辱衣冠，多不奉法，百姓詣闕訟之，孝文罰杖三十。

translations.literal: He humiliated officials and many did not obey the law; the people went to the palace to sue him, and Xiaowen punished him with thirty strokes of the staff.
translations.idiomatic: He abused officials and flouted the law until commoners petitioned at court; Xiaowen had him beaten thirty strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 貪暴彌甚，以罪徵詣京師。

translations.literal: His greed and violence grew worse, and he was summoned to the capital on criminal charge.
translations.idiomatic: His greed and cruelty deepened until he was summoned to the capital on criminal charge.

sentences.zh: 後謀不軌，事發，賜死於家，葬以王禮，諡曰厲。

translations.literal: Later he plotted rebellion; when the affair broke he was ordered to die at home, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous name Stern.
translations.idiomatic: He later plotted treason; when it was exposed he was ordered to die at home, buried with princely rites, and posthumously named Stern.

sentences.zh: 子詮，字搜賢，襲。

translations.literal: His son Quan, styled Souxian, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan, styled Souxian, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為涼州刺史。

translations.literal: At the start of Xuanwu's reign he was made Governor of Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanwu's reign he was made Governor of Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 在州貪穢，政以賄成。

translations.literal: In the province he was greedy and corrupt; government was bought with bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was greedy and corrupt; government ran on bribes.

sentences.zh: 後除定州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was removed and made Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 及京兆王愉之反，詐言國變。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Quan falsely announced that the state was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, rebelled, Quan spread word that the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 在北州鎮，咸疑朝廷有舋，遣使觀詮動靜。

translations.literal: The garrisons of the northern provinces all suspected trouble at court and sent envoys to watch Quan's movements.
translations.idiomatic: Northern garrison commanders suspected upheaval at court and sent men to watch Quan.

sentences.zh: 詮具以狀告，州鎮帖然。

translations.literal: Quan reported the full situation, and the provinces and garrisons settled down.
translations.idiomatic: Quan reported the facts in full, and the provinces and garrisons calmed.

sentences.zh: 愉奔信都，詮以李平、高殖等四面攻燒，愉突門而出。

translations.literal: Yu fled to Xin Du; Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides and set fires; Yu burst through a gate and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu fled to Xin Du; Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides with fire until Yu broke out through a gate and escaped.

sentences.zh: 尋除侍中，兼以首告之功，除尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Palace Attendant, and for his role in the first report he was also made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant and, for leading the first report, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰武康。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous name was Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Wukang.

sentences.zh: 子鑒，字長文，襲。

translations.literal: His son Jian, styled Changwen, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jian, styled Changwen, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後除相州刺史、北討大都督，討葛榮。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign to attack Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign against Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 仍兼尚書左僕射、北道行台尚書令，與都督裴衍共攻信都。

translations.literal: He also held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left, Northern Route Mobile Office Director of the Masters of Writing, and with Commander Pei Yan jointly besieged Xin Du.
translations.idiomatic: He also held the vice directorship on the left, directed the Northern Route mobile office, and with Commander Pei Yan besieged Xin Du.

sentences.zh: 鑒既庸才，見天下多事，遂謀反，降附葛榮。

translations.literal: Jian was a mediocrity; seeing the realm in turmoil he plotted rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre in talent, Jian saw the realm in chaos and plotted rebellion, surrendering to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 都督源子邕與裴衍合圍鑒，斬首傳洛，詔改姓元氏。

translations.literal: Commander Yuan Ziyong and Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian, beheaded him, and sent the head to Luoyang; an edict changed his surname to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Yuan Ziyong and Pei Yan besieged him, beheaded him, and sent the head to Luoyang; an edict changed his clan name to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，許復本族，又特復鑒王爵，贈司空。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign his original clan was restored, and Jian's princely title was specially restored with posthumous gift of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign his clan was restored and Jian's princely title specially revived with posthumous rank as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 鑒弟斌之，字子爽，性險無行。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang, was treacherous and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang, was treacherous and without principle.

sentences.zh: 及與鑒反，敗，遂奔葛榮。

translations.literal: When he rebelled with Jian and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When he joined Jian's rebellion and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 榮滅，得還。

translations.literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: After Ge Rong's destruction he returned.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝時，封潁川郡王，委以腹心之任。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan and entrusted with duties of intimate trust.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was made Prince of Yingchuan and given duties of intimate trust.

sentences.zh: 帝入關，斌之奔梁。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered Guanzhong, Binzhi fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered Guanzhong, Binzhi fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，還長安，位尚書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he returned to Chang'an and held Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he returned to Chang'an as Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 薨，贈太尉，諡武襄。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant, posthumous name Wuxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant and name Wuxiang.

sentences.zh: 廣川王略，延興二年封，位中都大官。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangchuan Lue, enfeoffed in the second year of Yanxing, held the office of Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan, Lue, enfeoffed in the second year of Yanxing, was Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.

sentences.zh: 性明敏，鞫獄稱平。

translations.literal: Clear and sharp by nature, in judging cases he was called fair.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and sharp by nature, he was known for fair judgments.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，薨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taihe.

sentences.zh: 諡曰莊。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 子諧，字仲和，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 十九年，薨。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「古者大臣之喪，有三臨之禮，此蓋三公已上。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In antiquity at the death of great ministers there was the rite of three visits—this applied to those of rank Three Excellencies and above.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "In antiquity great ministers received three imperial visits at death—this was for those of Three Excellencies rank and above.

sentences.zh: 自漢已降，多無此禮。

translations.literal: From Han downward many lacked this rite.
translations.idiomatic: From Han onward the rite was often neglected.

sentences.zh: 庶仰遵古典，哀感從情。

translations.literal: We wish to follow the ancient model in spirit and let grief move with feeling.
translations.idiomatic: We wish to follow the ancient model and let grief answer feeling.

sentences.zh: 雖以尊降伏，私痛寧爽。

translations.literal: Though rank requires restraint, private pain may not be denied.
translations.idiomatic: Though rank demands restraint, private pain should not be denied.

sentences.zh: 欲令親王有期親者為之三臨，大功親者為之再臨，小功緦麻為之一臨。

translations.literal: We wish princes with close kin in the first degree of mourning to make three visits, those in the second degree two visits, and those in the third and fifth degrees one visit.
translations.idiomatic: Princes with first-degree mourning kin should make three visits, second-degree kin two, third- and fifth-degree kin one.

sentences.zh: 廣川王于朕大功，必欲再臨者，欲於大斂日親臨盡哀，成服之後，緦衰而吊。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangchuan bears to Us mourning of the second degree; if he must have two visits, We wish to visit in person at the great encoffining to exhaust grief, and after assuming mourning garments to attend in fifth-degree hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan is second-degree kin to Us; for two visits We would attend the great encoffining in person, then after assuming garments attend in fifth-degree hemp.

sentences.zh: 既殯之緦麻，理在無疑。

translations.literal: Once the coffin is set, fifth-degree hemp is surely without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: After the coffin is sealed, fifth-degree hemp is surely proper.

sentences.zh: 大斂之臨，當否如何？

translations.literal: As to the visit at great encoffining—is it fitting?
translations.idiomatic: Is the visit at great encoffining fitting?

sentences.zh: 為須撫柩於始喪？

translations.literal: Must one stroke the bier at the first mourning?
translations.idiomatic: Must one stroke the bier at first mourning?

sentences.zh: 為應盡哀於闔柩？

translations.literal: Or should grief be exhausted at closing the coffin?
translations.idiomatic: Or exhaust grief only when the coffin is closed?

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎崔光、宋弁、通直常侍劉芳、典命下大夫李元凱、中書侍郎高聰等議曰：「三臨之事，乃自古禮。

translations.literal: Huangmen Attendant Cui Guang, Song Bian, Regular Attendant Liu Fang, Lower Grandee of Orders Li Yuankai, Secretariat Attendant Gao Cong, and others deliberated: "The three visits are indeed ancient rite.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, Song Bian, Liu Fang, Li Yuankai, Gao Cong, and others said: "Three visits are ancient rite.

sentences.zh: 爰及漢、魏，行之者稀；

translations.literal: Down through Han and Wei few practiced it;
translations.idiomatic: Through Han and Wei few practiced it;

sentences.zh: 陛下方遵前軌。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now follows the former track.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty now follows the former path.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為若期親三臨，大功宜再。

translations.literal: We deem that for first-degree kin three visits, for second-degree kin two are fitting.
translations.idiomatic: For first-degree kin three visits, for second-degree kin two.

sentences.zh: 始喪之初，哀之至極，既以情降，宜從始喪。

translations.literal: At the start of mourning grief is utmost; since feeling lowers rank, one should follow the start of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: At first mourning grief is utmost; since feeling tempers rank, follow the start of mourning.

sentences.zh: 大斂之臨，伏如聖旨。

translations.literal: As to the visit at great encoffining, we submit to the sacred intent.
translations.idiomatic: The visit at great encoffining we submit to Your Majesty's intent.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「魏、晉已來，親臨多闕，至於戚臣，必於東堂哭之。

translations.literal: An edict said: "From Wei and Jin onward personal visits were often lacking; for kin and ministers they were sure to weep in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, emperors often skipped personal visits; for kin and ministers they wept in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 頃大司馬安定王薨，朕既臨之後，受慰東堂。

translations.literal: Recently when Grand Marshal the Prince of Anding died, after We visited him We received condolences in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal the Prince of Anding died, We visited him then received condolences in the Eastern Hall.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，應更哭不？

translations.literal: For today's affair—should We weep again?
translations.idiomatic: For today—should We weep again?

sentences.zh: 」光等議曰：「東堂之哭，蓋以不臨之故。

translations.literal: Guang and others said: "Weeping in the Eastern Hall was because of not visiting in person.
translations.idiomatic: They said: "Eastern Hall weeping was for lack of personal visit.

sentences.zh: 今陛下躬親撫視，群臣從駕，臣等議，以為不宜復哭。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally attends; ministers follow the carriage—we deem further weeping unfitting.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty attends in person and ministers follow—we deem further weeping unfitting.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「若大司馬戚尊位重，必哭於東堂。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank, he must be wept for in the Eastern Hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank, Eastern Hall weeping is required.

sentences.zh: 而廣川既是諸王之子，又年位尚幼，卿等議之，朕無異焉。

translations.literal: But the Prince of Guangchuan is a king's son and still young in years and rank—as you deliberate, We have no objection.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan is a king's son and young in years and rank—as you see fit, We agree.

sentences.zh: 」諧將大斂，帝素委貌深衣哭之，入室哀慟，撫屍而出。

translations.literal: When Xie was about to be greatly encoffined, the emperor in plain dress and deep garments wept; entering the chamber he wailed bitterly, stroked the corpse, and went out.
translations.idiomatic: At Xie's great encoffining the emperor wore plain dress and deep garments, entered wailing, stroked the corpse, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 琛字曇寶，幼敏慧，孝文愛之。

translations.literal: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever and perceptive as a child; Xiaowen loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever and perceptive as a boy; Xiaowen loved him.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，拜定州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Xuanwu he was made Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he was made Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 琛妃，宣武舅女，高皇后妹。

translations.literal: Chen's consort was Xuanwu's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was Xuanwu's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.

sentences.zh: 琛憑恃內外，在州貪婪。

translations.literal: Relying on inside and outside connections, in the province he was greedy.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on court and family ties, he was greedy in office.

sentences.zh: 及還朝，靈太后詔曰：「琛在定州，唯不將中山宮來，自餘無所不致，何可敘用！

translations.literal: On returning to court Empress Ling said: "In Ding Province Chen brought everything except the Zhongshan palace—how can he be employed!
translations.idiomatic: On return Empress Ling said: "In Ding he took everything but the Zhongshan palace—how employ him?

sentences.zh: 」由是廢於家。

translations.literal: Because of this he was dismissed to his home.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to his home.

sentences.zh: 琛以明帝始學，獻金字《孝經》。

translations.literal: When Mingdi first studied, Chen presented a gold-letter Classic of Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingdi began studies Chen presented a gold-letter Classic of Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 又無方自達，乃與劉騰為養息，賂騰金寶巨萬計。

translations.literal: Unable to advance by his own means, he made Liu Teng his adoptive son and bribed Teng with gold and jewels in sums of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to advance on his own, he made Liu Teng his adoptive father and bribed him with gold and jewels beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 騰為言，乃得兼都官尚書。

translations.literal: Teng spoke for him and he obtained concurrent Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Teng spoke for him and he gained concurrent Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 出為秦州刺史，在州聚斂，百姓籲嗟。

translations.literal: Sent out as Governor of Qin Province, in the province he amassed wealth and the people groaned.
translations.idiomatic: As Governor of Qin he amassed wealth until the people groaned.

sentences.zh: 東益、南秦二州氐反，詔琛為行台，仍充都督，還攝州事。

translations.literal: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict made Chen mobile-office commander and also acting commander, returning to hold provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, he was made mobile-office commander and acting commander, resuming provincial duties.

sentences.zh: 既總軍省，求欲無厭。

translations.literal: Holding both army and province, his desires knew no limit.
translations.idiomatic: Commanding army and province, his appetites knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 進討氐、羌，大被摧破。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Di and Qiang, he inflicted great defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Di and Qiang he inflicted great defeats.

sentences.zh: 內恃劉騰，無所畏憚。

translations.literal: Within he relied on Liu Teng and feared nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Within he relied on Liu Teng and feared nothing.

sentences.zh: 為中尉彈糾，會赦，除名。

translations.literal: The Commandant of Justice impeached him; an amnesty came and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice impeached him; amnesty struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 尋復王爵。

translations.literal: Soon his princely title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his princely title was restored.

sentences.zh: 後討鮮于修禮，敗，免官爵。

translations.literal: Later attacking Xianyu Xiuli he was defeated and stripped of office and title.
translations.idiomatic: Later, attacking Xianyu Xiuli, he was defeated and stripped of office and title.

sentences.zh: 後討汾晉胡、蜀，卒於軍，追復王爵。

translations.literal: Later attacking Hu of Fen and Jin and Shu, he died in the army; posthumously his princely title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Hu of Fen and Jin and Shu, he died in the army; his princely title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 安豐王猛字季烈，太和五年封，加侍中。

translations.literal: Prince of Anfeng Meng, styled Jilie, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Anfeng, Meng, styled Jilie, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮都大將、營州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as Grand General of the Garrison Capital and Governor of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand General of the Garrison Capital and Governor of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 猛寬仁雄毅，甚有威略，戎夷畏愛之。

translations.literal: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with great authority and strategy; the barbarians feared and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, he had great authority; barbarians feared and loved him.

sentences.zh: 薨于州，贈太尉，諡曰匡。

translations.literal: He died in the province; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant, posthumous name Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant and name Kuang.

sentences.zh: 子延明襲。

translations.literal: His son Yanming succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanming inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，授太中大夫。

translations.literal: Under Xuanwu he was made Grand Palace Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he was made Grand Palace Grandee.

sentences.zh: 延昌初，歲大饑，延明乃減家財以拯賓客數十人，並贍其家。

translations.literal: At the start of Yan Chang, in a year of great famine, Yanming reduced family wealth to save several dozen guests and support their households.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yan Chang, a year of famine, he spent family wealth to save dozens of guests and their households.

sentences.zh: 至明帝初，為豫州刺史，甚有政績。

translations.literal: By the start of Mingdi he was Governor of Yu Province with marked achievements in government.
translations.idiomatic: By Mingdi's accession he was Governor of Yu Province with marked achievements.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attendant of the Yellow Gate within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 延明既博極群書，兼有文藻，鳩集圖籍萬有餘卷。

translations.literal: Yanming had mastered the classics and also literary talent; he gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of books and maps.
translations.idiomatic: He had mastered the classics and literary talent, gathering more than ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 性清儉，不營產業。

translations.literal: His nature was pure and frugal; he did not pursue estates.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and frugal, he did not pursue estates.

sentences.zh: 與中山王熙及弟臨淮王彧等並以文學令望，有名於世。

translations.literal: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his younger brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu he shared literary renown famous in the age.
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu he shared literary fame.

sentences.zh: 雖風流造次不及熙、彧，而稽古淳篤過之。

translations.literal: Though in casual elegance he did not match Xi and Yu, in classical learning and solid virtue he surpassed them.
translations.idiomatic: In casual elegance he fell short of Xi and Yu; in classical learning and solid virtue he surpassed them.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中，詔與侍中崔光撰定服制。

translations.literal: Promoted to Palace Attendant, an edict ordered him with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to fix mourning garments.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Attendant, he was ordered with Cui Guang to fix mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 後兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Later he also held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.
translations.idiomatic: He later held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.

sentences.zh: 以延明博識多聞，敕監金石事。

translations.literal: Because Yanming was broadly learned, he was ordered to supervise metal and stone affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his broad learning he was ordered to supervise metal and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 及元法僧反，詔為東道行台、徐州大都督，節度諸軍事。

translations.literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, an edict made him Eastern Route mobile office, Grand Commander of Xu Province, directing all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled he was made Eastern Route mobile office and Grand Commander of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 與都督臨淮王彧、尚書李憲等討法僧。

translations.literal: With Commander the Prince of Linhuai Yu and Master of Writing Li Xian he attacked Faseng.
translations.idiomatic: With the Prince of Linhuai Yu and Li Xian he attacked Faseng.

sentences.zh: 梁遣其豫章王綜鎮徐州。

translations.literal: Liang sent the Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent the Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 延明先牧徐方，甚得人譽；

translations.literal: Yanming had earlier governed Xu region and won great praise of the people;
translations.idiomatic: Yanming had earlier governed Xu and won the people's praise;

sentences.zh: 招懷舊土，遠近歸之。

translations.literal: he won over the old territory and the distant and near submitted.
translations.idiomatic: he won back the old territory until distant and near submitted.

sentences.zh: 綜既降，延明因以軍乘之。

translations.literal: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed on with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong surrendered, Yanming pressed the army forward.

sentences.zh: 復東南之境，至宿、豫而還。

translations.literal: He recovered the southeastern borderlands, reaching Su and Yu, then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered the southeast to Su and Yu, then returned.

sentences.zh: 遷都督，徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted Commander and Governor of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander and Governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 頻經師旅，人物雕弊。

translations.literal: Repeated campaigns had worn the land and people.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated campaigns had ravaged land and people.

sentences.zh: 延明招攜新故，人悉安業，百姓咸附。

translations.literal: Yanming won over old and new inhabitants until all were settled and the people attached.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming won over old and new until all were settled and the people attached.

sentences.zh: 莊帝時，兼大司馬。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Zhuang he also held Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Zhuang he also held Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，延明受顥委寄。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received Hao's trust.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, Yanming received his trust.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，奔梁，死於江南。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated he fled to Liang and died south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao was defeated he fled to Liang and died south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 莊帝末，喪還。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Zhuang's reign his coffin was returned.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhuang's reign his coffin returned.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，贈太保，王如故，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaowu he was posthumously made Grand Guardian, princely title as before, posthumous name Wensuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession he was posthumously Grand Guardian with princely title unchanged and name Wensuan.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦讚頌銘誄三百餘篇。

translations.literal: Works composed: more than three hundred pieces of poetry, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges.
translations.idiomatic: He composed more than three hundred poems, fu, encomia, hymns, inscriptions, and dirges.

sentences.zh: 又撰《五經宗略》、《詩禮別義》；

translations.literal: He also compiled Overview of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites;
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled Overview of the Five Classics and Separate Meanings of the Odes and Rites;

sentences.zh: 注《帝王世紀》及《列仙傳》。

translations.literal: annotated Records of Emperors and Kings and Lives of Immortals.
translations.idiomatic: annotated Records of Emperors and Kings and Lives of Immortals.

sentences.zh: 又以河間人信都芳工算圖。

translations.literal: He also took Xin Dufang of Hejian, skilled in calculation and diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: He also employed Xin Dufang of Hejian, skilled in calculation and diagrams.

sentences.zh: 又集《器准》九篇，芳別為之注，皆行於世矣。

translations.literal: He gathered nine chapters of Standards of Implements; Fang wrote a separate commentary—both circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered nine chapters of Standards of Implements with Fang's commentary—both circulated.

sentences.zh: 孫長儒，孝靜時襲祖爵。

translations.literal: His grandson Changru, under Emperor Xiaojing, inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Changru inherited under Emperor Xiaojing.

sentences.zh: 獻文皇帝七男：思皇后生孝文皇帝；

translations.literal: Emperor Xianwen had seven sons: the Reflective Empress bore Emperor Xiaowen;
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen had seven sons: the Reflective Empress bore Xiaowen;

sentences.zh: 封昭儀生咸陽王禧；

translations.literal: Consort Feng the Worthy bore the Prince of Xianyang Xi;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Feng the Worthy bore the Prince of Xianyang, Xi;

sentences.zh: 韓貴人生趙郡靈王幹、高陽文穆王雍；

translations.literal: Consort Han the Worthy bore the Prince of Zhao Commandery the Spiritual Gan and the Prince of Gaoyang the Cultivated and Solemn Yong;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Han bore the Prince of Zhao Commandery the Spiritual Gan and the Prince of Gaoyang the Cultivated Yong;

sentences.zh: 孟椒房生廣陵慧王羽；

translations.literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Guangling the Sagacious Yu;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Meng bore the Prince of Guangling the Sagacious Yu;

sentences.zh: 潘貴人生彭城武宣王勰；

translations.literal: Consort Pan the Worthy bore the Prince of Pengcheng the Martial and Proclaimed Xie;
translations.idiomatic: Consort Pan bore the Prince of Pengcheng the Martial Xie;

sentences.zh: 高椒房生北海王詳。

translations.literal: Consort Gao of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Beihai Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Gao bore the Prince of Beihai Xiang.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧字思永，太和九年封，加侍中、驃騎大將軍、中都大官。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi, styled Siyong, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Xianyang, Xi, styled Siyong, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant, General of Agile Cavalry, and Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.

sentences.zh: 文明太后令皇子皇孫于靜所別置學，選忠信博聞之士為之師傅，以匠成之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming ordered imperial sons and grandsons to a separate school at Jing's place, choosing loyal, trustworthy, and broadly learned men as teachers to shape them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming placed imperial sons in a separate school, choosing loyal and learned teachers to shape them.

sentences.zh: 孝文以諸弟典三都職，謂禧曰：「弟等皆幼年任重，三都折獄，特宜用心。

translations.literal: Xiaowen, because the princes held the three capital judiciaries, told Xi: "You are all young yet bear heavy duty; the three capitals' judging of cases especially demands care.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen told Xi and the others: "You are young yet bear heavy duty; judging in the three capitals especially demands care.

sentences.zh: 夫未能操刀而使割錦，非傷錦之尤，實授刀之責。

translations.literal: To hand one a knife who cannot wield it and bid him cut brocade is not the brocade's chief fault but the fault of him who gave the knife.
translations.idiomatic: Giving a knife to one who cannot wield it and bidding him cut brocade faults not the brocade but the giver.

sentences.zh: 」文明太后亦致誡勖。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming also sent admonitions and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming also sent admonitions.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、開府、冀州刺史，孝文餞於南郊。

translations.literal: Sent out as Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Ji Province; Xiaowen feasted him at the southern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, Opener of the Office, and Governor of Ji; Xiaowen feasted him at the southern suburb.

sentences.zh: 又以濟陽王鬱枉法賜死之事遣告禧，因以誡之。

translations.literal: He also sent word of the affair of the Prince of Jiyang Yu, wrongly executed by law, to admonish Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the wrongful execution of the Prince of Jiyang Yu as further admonition.

sentences.zh: 後禧朝京師，詔以廷尉卿李沖為禧師。

translations.literal: Later when Xi came to the capital, an edict made Director of the Court Li Chong Xi's teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi came to court, Li Chong was made his teacher.

sentences.zh: 時王國舍人應取八族及清修之門，禧取任城王隸戶為之，深為帝責。

translations.literal: At the time a prince's household aide should be taken from the eight clans and families of pure conduct; Xi took retainers of the Prince of Rencheng—deeply rebuked by the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: A prince's aides should come from the eight clans; Xi took the Prince of Rencheng's retainers and was deeply rebuked.

sentences.zh: 帝以諸王婚多猥濫，於是為禧娉故潁川太守隴西李輔女；

translations.literal: Because the princes' marriages were mostly base, he betrothed Xi to the daughter of former Governor of Yingchuan Longxi Li Fu;
translations.idiomatic: Because princely marriages were base, Xi was betrothed to Li Fu's daughter of Yingchuan;

sentences.zh: 河南王幹娉故中散代郡穆明樂女；

translations.literal: the Prince of Henan Gan to the daughter of former Central Scribe of Dai Commandery Mu Mingle;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Henan Gan to Mu Mingle's daughter;

sentences.zh: 廣陵王羽娉驃騎諮議參軍榮陽鄭平城女；

translations.literal: the Prince of Guangling Yu to the daughter of Staff Officer of Agile Cavalry Rongyang Zheng Pingcheng;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Guangling Yu to Zheng Pingcheng's daughter;

sentences.zh: 潁川王雍娉故中書博士范陽盧神寶女；

translations.literal: the Prince of Yingchuan Yong to the daughter of former Doctor of the Secretariat Luyang Lu Shenbao;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Yingchuan Yong to Lu Shenbao's daughter;

sentences.zh: 始平王勰娉廷尉卿隴西李沖女；

translations.literal: the Prince of Shiping Xie to the daughter of Director of the Court Longxi Li Chong;
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Shiping Xie to Li Chong's daughter;

sentences.zh: 北海王詳娉吏部郎中榮陽鄭懿女。

translations.literal: the Prince of Beihai Xiang to the daughter of Bureau Director Rongyang Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Beihai Xiang to Zheng Yi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「冀州人蘇僧瓘等三千人稱禧清明，有惠政，請世胙冀州。

translations.literal: The authorities memorialized: "Three thousand men of Ji Province, led by Su Senguan, call Xi clear and bright with benevolent government, and ask hereditary fief in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Authorities reported: "Three thousand men of Ji, led by Su Senguan, praise Xi's clarity and benevolence and ask hereditary fief in Ji."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「畫野由君，理非下請。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Territory is drawn by the ruler; principle does not allow petition from below.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "Territory is the ruler's to draw; subjects may not petition from below."

sentences.zh: 」入除司州牧。

translations.literal: He entered office as Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He became Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 詔以禧元弟之重，食邑三千戶，自余五王皆食邑二千。

translations.literal: An edict, because Xi was the eldest younger brother, gave him three thousand households; the other five princes each two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi was the eldest younger brother he received three thousand households; the other five princes two thousand each.

sentences.zh: 孝文引見朝臣，詔斷北語，一從正音，禧贊成其事。

translations.literal: Xiaowen received the court ministers and ordered an end to northern speech, all following standard pronunciation; Xi praised and completed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen ordered court to abandon northern speech for standard pronunciation; Xi praised the policy.

sentences.zh: 於是詔：「年三十已上，習性已久，容或不可卒革。

translations.literal: Then an edict: "Those thirty and above, long accustomed, perhaps cannot be suddenly changed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: "Those thirty and above, long accustomed, perhaps cannot change at once.

sentences.zh: 三十已下，見在朝廷之人，語音不聽仍舊。

translations.literal: Those thirty and below now in court—speech must not remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Those thirty and below in court must not keep old speech.

sentences.zh: 若有故為，當降爵黜官。

translations.literal: Whoever deliberately persists shall be lowered in rank and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberate persistence means lowered rank and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 若仍舊俗，恐數世之後，伊洛之下，復成被髮之人。

translations.literal: If old custom remains, I fear that after several generations below Yi and Luo they will again become people with loose hair.
translations.idiomatic: If custom remains, after generations below Yi and Luo they may again become loose-haired barbarians."

sentences.zh: 朕嘗與李沖論此，沖言：'四方之語，竟知誰是；

translations.literal: I once discussed this with Li Chong; Chong said: "Of the speech of the four quarters, who knows which is right?
translations.idiomatic: I once discussed this with Li Chong, who said, "Of the speech of the four quarters, who knows which is right?

sentences.zh: 帝者言之，即為正矣，何必改舊從新。

translations.literal: What the emperor speaks is then orthodox—why must one change the old and follow the new?
translations.idiomatic: What the emperor speaks is orthodox—why change the old for the new?"

sentences.zh: '沖之此言，應合死罪。

translations.literal: Chong's words deserve death in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's words deserved death in principle."

sentences.zh: 」乃謂沖曰：「卿實負社稷。

translations.literal: He then told Chong: "You have truly failed the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He told Chong: "You have failed the altars of soil and grain."

sentences.zh: 」沖免冠陳謝。

translations.literal: Chong removed his cap and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Chong removed his cap and apologized.

sentences.zh: 又責留京之官曰：「昨望見婦女之服，仍為夾領小袖，何為而違前詔？

translations.literal: He also rebuked officials who remained in the capital: "Yesterday I saw women's dress still with overlapping collars and narrow sleeves—why violate the former edict?
translations.idiomatic: He rebuked capital officials: "Yesterday I saw women still in overlapping collars and narrow sleeves—why violate the edict?"

sentences.zh: 」禧對曰：「陛下聖過堯、舜，光化中原。

translations.literal: Xi replied: "Your Majesty's sagacity surpasses Yao and Shun, transforming the central plains.
translations.idiomatic: Xi replied: "Your Majesty surpasses Yao and Shun, transforming the central plains.

sentences.zh: 舛違之罪，實合處刑。

translations.literal: The crime of violation truly deserves punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Violation deserves punishment."

sentences.zh: 」孝文曰：「若朕言非，卿等當奮臂廷論，如何入則順旨，退有不從？

translations.literal: Xiaowen said: "If Our words are wrong, you should debate boldly in court—why in enter flatter the intent and in withdraw not follow?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen said: "If We err, debate in court—why flatter Us in session and disobey in private?

sentences.zh: 昔舜語禹：'汝無面從，退有後言。

translations.literal: In antiquity Shun told Yu: 'Do not agree to my face and afterward speak behind my back.'
translations.idiomatic: Shun told Yu: Do not agree to my face and speak behind my back—is this not you?"

sentences.zh: '卿等之謂乎！」

translations.literal: Is this not what you are!"
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what you mean!"

sentences.zh: 尋以禧長兼太尉公。

translations.literal: Soon Xi was made concurrent Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xi was made concurrent Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 後帝幸禧第，謂司空穆亮、僕射李沖曰：「元弟禧戚連皇極，且長兼太尉，以和飪鼎，朕恆恐君有空授之名，臣貽彼己之刺。

translations.literal: Later the emperor visited Xi's residence and told Minister of Works Mu Liang and Vice Director Li Chong: "Younger brother Xi is kin to the imperial pole and long holds concurrent Grand Commandant to harmonize the cauldron; We always fear the ruler has the name of empty appointment and ministers the wound of failing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Xi's home, the emperor told Mu Liang and Li Chong: "Xi is imperial kin and long concurrent Grand Commandant; We fear empty titles for the ruler and mutual failure for ministers.

sentences.zh: 今幸其宅，徒屈二賓，良以為愧。

translations.literal: Now visiting his house, We have only wronged you two guests—truly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Today We wrong only you two guests—truly ashamed."

sentences.zh: 」帝篤于兄弟，以禧次長，禮遇優隆。

translations.literal: The emperor was deep in brotherly feeling; because Xi was next eldest he treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Deep in brotherly feeling, he treated Xi, next eldest, with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 然亦知其性貪，每加切誡，而終不改操。

translations.literal: Yet he also knew his greedy nature and often admonished him sharply, but in the end he did not change his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yet knowing his greed he often admonished him, without changing his conduct.

sentences.zh: 後加侍中，正太尉。

translations.literal: Later he was made Palace Attendant and regular Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Palace Attendant and regular Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，禧受遺輔政。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Xi received the testamentary regency.
translations.idiomatic: At the emperor's death Xi received testamentary regency.

sentences.zh: 雖為宰輔之首，而潛受賄賂。

translations.literal: Though head among the regents, he secretly received bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Though head regent, he secretly took bribes.

sentences.zh: 姬妾數十，意尚未已，猶欲遠有簡娉，以恣其情。

translations.literal: He had several dozen concubines and was not yet satisfied, still wishing to choose from afar to indulge his desires.
translations.idiomatic: He had dozens of concubines and still wished to choose more from afar.

sentences.zh: 宣武頗惡之。

translations.literal: Xuanwu greatly disliked this.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu greatly disliked this.

sentences.zh: 景明二年春，召禧等入光極殿，詔曰：「恪比纏尪疾，實憑諸父。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Jingming he summoned Xi and others to Guangji Hall and said: "Ke is lately ill and truly relies on his uncles.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Jingming's second year he summoned them to Guangji Hall: "Ke is ill and relies on his uncles.

sentences.zh: 今便親攝百揆。

translations.literal: Now he will personally hold the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: Now he will personally govern.

sentences.zh: 且還府司，當別處分。

translations.literal: Return to your princely offices; separate disposition will follow.
translations.idiomatic: Return to your offices; We will dispose separately."

sentences.zh: 」尋詔進位太保，領太尉。

translations.literal: Soon an edict advanced him to Grand Guardian and head Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was advanced to Grand Guardian and head Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 帝既覽政，禧意不安，遂與其妃兄兼給事黃門侍郎李伯尚謀反。

translations.literal: When the emperor took government, Xi was uneasy and with his consort's brother, Concurrent Attendant of the Yellow Gate Li Boshang, plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took power Xi was uneasy and with Li Boshang, his consort's brother, plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 帝時幸小平，禧在城西小宅。

translations.literal: The emperor was then at Xiaoping; Xi was at a small residence west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Xiaoping; Xi at a small residence west of the city.

sentences.zh: 初欲勒兵直入金墉，眾懷沮異。

translations.literal: At first he wished to lead troops straight into Jincheng; the host was disheartened and divided.
translations.idiomatic: He meant to lead troops into Jincheng; the host wavered and split.

sentences.zh: 禧心因緩，自旦達晡，計不能決。

translations.literal: Xi's heart slackened; from dawn to dusk he could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: His heart slackened; from dawn to dusk he could not decide.

sentences.zh: 遂約不泄而散。

translations.literal: They agreed to disperse without leaking the plot.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to disperse without revealing the plot.

sentences.zh: 直寢符承祖、薛魏孫與禧將害帝。

translations.literal: Duty Attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun with Xi were to harm the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Duty attendants Fu Chengzu and Xue Weisun were to kill the emperor with Xi.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝息於芒山，止浮圖陰下，少時睡臥，魏孫便欲赴廷。

translations.literal: That day the emperor rested on Mang Mountain below the shadow of a pagoda; after a little he slept; Weisun wished to rush the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That day the emperor rested on Mang Mountain beneath a pagoda; Weisun meant to rush the hall.

sentences.zh: 承祖私言于魏孫曰：「吾聞殺天子者身當癩。

translations.literal: Chengzu privately told Weisun: "I hear that whoever kills the Son of Heaven his body will break out in sores.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu whispered: "Whoever kills the Son of Heaven breaks out in sores."

sentences.zh: 」魏孫且止。

translations.literal: Weisun for the moment stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Weisun stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝尋覺悟。

translations.literal: The emperor soon awoke.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon awoke.

sentences.zh: 俄有武興王楊集始出，便馳告。

translations.literal: Presently Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi came out and at once rode to report.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Wuxing Yang Jishi came out and rode to report.

sentences.zh: 而禧意不疑，乃與臣妾向洪池別墅，遣其齋帥劉小苟奉啟，雲檢行田牧。

translations.literal: Xi still did not suspect; he went with concubines toward Hongchi Villa and sent his fast officer Liu Xiaogou with a memorial saying he was inspecting fields and herds.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, still unsuspecting, went with concubines to Hongchi Villa and sent Liu Xiaogou with a memorial claiming to inspect fields.

sentences.zh: 小苟至芒嶺，已逢軍人，怪小苟赤衣，將欲殺害。

translations.literal: Xiaogou reached Mang Ridge and already met soldiers; they wondered at Xiaogou's red dress and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaogou met soldiers on Mang Ridge; they wondered at his red dress and nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 小苟言欲告反，乃緩之。

translations.literal: Xiaogou said he wished to report rebellion, and they spared him.
translations.idiomatic: He said he came to report rebellion and was spared.

sentences.zh: 禧是夜宿于洪池，不知事露。

translations.literal: That night Xi lodged at Hongchi, not knowing the affair was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xi lodged at Hongchi, unaware the plot was exposed.

sentences.zh: 其夜，將士所在追禧，禧自洪池東南走，左右從禧者唯兼防閣尹龍武。

translations.literal: That night soldiers everywhere pursued Xi; Xi fled southeast from Hongchi; of those who followed Xi only Concurrent Guard Yin Longwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers pursued him; he fled southeast from Hongchi with only Yin Longwu.

sentences.zh: 禧憂迫，謂曰：「試作一謎，當思解之，以釋毒悶。

translations.literal: Xi in distress said: "Try to make a riddle; I shall think to solve it and ease this bitter vexation.
translations.idiomatic: In distress Xi said: "Make a riddle—I will solve it to ease this torment."

sentences.zh: 」龍武欻憶舊謎云：「眠則同眠，起則同起，貪如犲狼，贓不入己。

translations.literal: Longwu suddenly recalled an old riddle: "Sleeping we sleep together, rising we rise together, greedy as jackals and wolves, yet booty does not enter oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Longwu recalled: "Sleeping we sleep together, rising we rise together, greedy as jackals and wolves, yet booty never enters oneself."

sentences.zh: 」都不有心於規刺也。

translations.literal: He had no thought of plotting assassination.
translations.idiomatic: He had no thought of assassination.

sentences.zh: 禧亦不以為諷己，因解之曰：「此是眼也。

translations.literal: Xi also did not take it as satire of himself and solved: "This is the eye.
translations.idiomatic: Xi did not take it as satire and said: "The eye."

sentences.zh: 」而龍武謂之是箸。

translations.literal: But Longwu meant chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Longwu meant chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 渡洛水，至柏塢，顧謂龍武曰：「汝可勉心作與太尉公同死計。

translations.literal: Crossing the Luo, at Baiwu he turned to Longwu: "You should steel your heart and make the plan to die with the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: At Baiwu he said: "Steel your heart and die with the Grand Commandant."

sentences.zh: 」龍武曰：「若與殿下同命，雖死猶生。

translations.literal: Longwu said: "If I share fate with Your Highness, though I die I yet live.
translations.idiomatic: Longwu said: "To share Your Highness's fate is to live even in death."

sentences.zh: 」俄而禧被禽，送華林都亭，著千斤鎖格龍武，羽林掌衛之。

translations.literal: Soon Xi was seized and sent to Hualin Postal Pavilion; a thousand-jin lock was put on Longwu and armored guards watched them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xi was seized at Hualin Postal Pavilion; Longwu was chained with a thousand-jin lock under armored guard.

sentences.zh: 時熱甚，禧渴悶垂死，敕斷水漿。

translations.literal: The heat was extreme; Xi thirsted and was near death; an order cut off water and drink.
translations.idiomatic: In extreme heat Xi thirsted near death; orders cut off water.

sentences.zh: 侍中崔光令左右送酪漿升餘，禧一飲而盡。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Cui Guang ordered attendants to send more than a sheng of yogurt; Xi drank it in one draft.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang sent more than a sheng of yogurt; Xi drank it at once.

sentences.zh: 初，孝文觀台宿有逆謀氣，言於禧曰：「玄象變，汝終為逆謀，會無所成，但受惡而已。

translations.literal: Earlier Xiaowen, observing the observatory, saw air of treasonous plotting and told Xi: "The stars change—you will end in treasonous plotting, accomplish nothing, and only receive evil.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xiaowen saw treason in the stars and told Xi: "You will plot treason, accomplish nothing, and only suffer."

sentences.zh: 」至此，果如言。

translations.literal: At this it was indeed as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Now it was as he said.

sentences.zh: 禧臨盡，畏迫喪志，乃與諸妹公主等訣，言及一二愛妾。

translations.literal: At the end Xi, in fear and oppression, lost his will and took leave of his sisters the princesses, speaking of one or two beloved concubines.
translations.idiomatic: At the end, broken by fear, he took leave of princess sisters and named one or two beloved concubines.

sentences.zh: 公主哭且罵之，言：「坐多取此婢輩，貪逐財物，致今日之事，何復囑問此等！

translations.literal: A princess wept and cursed him: "Because you took too many of these maidservants and greedily chased wealth you brought today's affair—why still entrust questions to them!
translations.idiomatic: A princess wept and cursed: "You took too many maids and chased wealth—that brought today—why entrust them now?

sentences.zh: 」禧愧而無言。

translations.literal: Xi was ashamed and speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was ashamed and silent.

sentences.zh: 遂賜死私第，絕其諸子屬籍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to die at his private residence; his sons were struck from the clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to die at home; his sons were struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 禧之諸女，微給資產、奴婢。

translations.literal: Xi's daughters were given a little property and maidservants.
translations.idiomatic: His daughters received a little property and maids.

sentences.zh: 自余家財悉以賚高肇、趙修二家，其餘賜內外百官，逮於流外，多百匹，下至十匹，其積聚若此。

translations.literal: All remaining family wealth was bestowed on the houses of Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the rest given to inner and outer officials, down to those outside the flow, many a hundred bolts, down to ten—his accumulation was such.
translations.idiomatic: Remaining wealth went to Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the rest to officials high and low in bolts from hundreds to tens—such was his hoard.

sentences.zh: 其宮人為之歌曰：「可憐咸陽王，奈何作事誤？

translations.literal: His palace women made a song: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how could you err in your deeds?
translations.idiomatic: Palace women sang: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how err so?

sentences.zh: 金床玉幾不能眠，夜蹋霜與露。

translations.literal: Golden bed and jade couch—you cannot sleep; at night you tread frost and dew.
translations.idiomatic: Golden bed, jade couch—yet no sleep; at night you tread frost and dew.

sentences.zh: 洛水湛湛彌岸長，行人那得度！

translations.literal: The Luo runs deep and the bank is long—how can a traveler cross!
translations.idiomatic: The Luo runs deep, the bank long—how can a traveler cross?

sentences.zh: 」其歌遂流至江表。

translations.literal: The song flowed to the lands south of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: The song flowed south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 北人之在南者，雖富貴，聞弦管奏之，莫不灑泣。

translations.literal: Northerners in the south, though rich and noble, hearing it played on string and pipe—all wept without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Northerners in the south, though rich, hearing strings and pipes—wept without restraint.

sentences.zh: 禧八子。

translations.literal: Xi had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 長子通，字曇和，竊入河內太守陸琇家。

translations.literal: The eldest son Tong, styled Tanhe, secretly entered the home of Interior Governor of Henei Lu Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest Tong, styled Tanhe, secretly entered Governor of Henei Lu Xiu's home.

sentences.zh: 初與通情，既聞禧敗，乃殺之。

translations.literal: At first he was intimate with Tong; hearing of Xi's defeat he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At first intimate with Tong; hearing of Xi's defeat he killed him.

sentences.zh: 通弟翼，字仲和，後會赦，詣闕上書，求葬父。

translations.literal: Tong's younger brother Yi, styled Zhonghe, later met an amnesty and went to court with a memorial asking to bury his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Zhonghe, later gained amnesty and petitioned to bury his father.

sentences.zh: 不許，乃與二弟昌、曄奔梁。

translations.literal: It was not granted; he with two younger brothers Chang and Ye fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Denied, he fled to Liang with Chang and Ye.

sentences.zh: 正光中，詔咸陽、京兆二王諸子並聽附屬籍。

translations.literal: In Zhengguang an edict allowed sons of the Princes of Xianyang and Jingzhao to reattach to the registers.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengguang sons of Xianyang and Jingzhao were allowed to reattach to registers.

sentences.zh: 後復禧王爵，葬以王禮，詔曄弟坦襲。

translations.literal: Later Xi's princely title was restored; burial with princely rites; an edict made Yi's younger brother Tan succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xi's title was restored with princely burial; Yi's brother Tan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 翼與昌，申屠氏出；

translations.literal: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shen Tu;
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shen Tu;

sentences.zh: 曄，李妃所出也。

translations.literal: Ye was born of Consort Li.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was born of Consort Li.

sentences.zh: 翼容貌魁壯，風制可觀，梁武甚重之，封為咸陽王。

translations.literal: Yi's appearance was tall and strong, his bearing admirable; Emperor Wu of Liang greatly valued him and enfeoffed him Prince of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and strong with admirable bearing, Liang Wudi made him Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 翼讓其嫡弟曄，梁武不許。

translations.literal: Yi yielded to his younger brother of the main line Ye; Liang Wudi did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Yi yielded to Ye, the son of the main line; Liang Wudi refused.

sentences.zh: 後為青、冀二州刺史，鎮郁州。

translations.literal: Later he was Governor of Qing and Ji and garrisoned Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later Governor of Qing and Ji, garrisoning Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 翼謀舉州入國，為梁武所殺。

translations.literal: Yi plotted to surrender the province to Wei and was killed by Liang Wudi.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to surrender the province to Wei and Liang Wudi killed him.

sentences.zh: 翼弟樹，字秀和，一家獨立。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Shu, styled Xiuhe, stood alone in the family.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Shu, styled Xiuhe, stood apart in the family.

sentences.zh: 美姿貌，善吐納，兼有將略。

translations.literal: Fine in appearance, skilled in breath regulation, and also with military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Fine in appearance, skilled in breath regulation, with military talent.

sentences.zh: 位宗正卿。

translations.literal: He held Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He held Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 後亦奔梁。

translations.literal: Later he too fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He too fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武尤器之，封為魏郡王，後改封鄴王。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi especially prized him, enfeoffed him Prince of Wei Commandery, later changed to Prince of Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi prized him, made him Prince of Wei Commandery, later Prince of Ye.

sentences.zh: 數為將領，窺覦邊服。

translations.literal: Several times a commander, he watched the borderlands for opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Several times commander, he watched the borders for opportunity.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之害百官也，樹時為郢州刺史，請討榮。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong killed the hundred officials, Shu was then Governor of Ying Province and asked to attack Rong.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered officials, Shu as Governor of Ying asked to attack him.

sentences.zh: 梁武資其士馬，侵擾境上。

translations.literal: Liang Wudi supplied men and horses and he harassed the border.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi supplied troops and he harassed the border.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，御史中尉樊子鵠為行台，率徐州刺史杜德、舍人李昭等討之。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaowu, Commandant of Justice Fan Zihu was mobile office and with Governor of Xu Du De and Attendant Li Zhao attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession Fan Zihu as mobile office with Du De and Li Zhao attacked him.

sentences.zh: 樹城守不下，子鵠使金紫光祿大夫張安期說之。

translations.literal: Shu held the city and would not yield; Zihu sent Golden Grandee Zhang Anqi to persuade him.
translations.idiomatic: Shu held the city; Zihu sent Zhang Anqi to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 樹請委城還南，子鵠許之，殺白馬為盟。

translations.literal: Shu asked to yield the city and return south; Zihu agreed and they killed a white horse in covenant.
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked to yield and return south; Zihu agreed and they swore on a white horse.

sentences.zh: 樹恃誓，不為戰備。

translations.literal: Shu trusted the oath and made no war preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting the oath, he made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 與杜德別，還南。

translations.literal: Parting from Du De he returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Parting from Du De he returned south.

sentences.zh: 德不許，送洛陽，置在景明寺。

translations.literal: De did not permit it and sent him to Luoyang, placed in Jingming Temple.
translations.idiomatic: De refused and sent him to Luoyang, to Jingming Temple.

sentences.zh: 樹年十五奔南，未及富貴。

translations.literal: Shu at fifteen fled south and had not yet reached wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he fled south before wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 每見嵩山雲向南，未嘗不引領歔欷。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw clouds on Mount Song drifting south he never failed to stretch his neck and sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever clouds on Mount Song drifted south he stretched his neck and sighed.

sentences.zh: 初發梁，睹其愛姝玉兒，以金指環與別，樹常著之。

translations.literal: When he first left Liang he saw his beloved Yu'er and gave her a gold finger-ring in parting; Shu always wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Liang he gave his beloved Yu'er a gold ring; he always wore it.

sentences.zh: 寄以還梁，表必還之意。

translations.literal: He sent it back to Liang as a token that he would surely return.
translations.idiomatic: He sent it back to Liang as pledge he would return.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知之，俄而賜死。

translations.literal: Court learned of it and soon ordered him to die.
translations.idiomatic: Court learned and soon ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 未幾，杜德忽得狂病，云：「元樹打我不已。

translations.literal: Before long Du De suddenly took madness and said: "Prince Yuan Shu keeps beating me.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Du De went mad crying: "Yuan Shu keeps beating me."

sentences.zh: 」至死，此驚不絕。

translations.literal: Until death this fright did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Until death the fright did not cease.

sentences.zh: 舍人李昭尋奉使向秦州，至潼關驛，夜夢樹云：「我已訴天帝，待卿至隴，終不相放。

translations.literal: Attendant Li Zhao soon went on mission to Qin Province; at Tong Pass postal station at night he dreamed Shu said: "I have appealed to Heaven; when you reach Long I will not spare you.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao dreamed Shu said: "I have appealed to Heaven; at Long I will not spare you."

sentences.zh: 」昭覺，惡之。

translations.literal: Zhao awoke and hated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao awoke in dread.

sentences.zh: 及至隴口，為賀拔嶽所殺。

translations.literal: When he reached Long Pass he was killed by Heba Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At Long Pass Heba Yue killed him.

sentences.zh: 子鵠尋為達野拔所殺。

translations.literal: Zihu was soon killed by Daye Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Zihu was soon killed by Daye Ba.

sentences.zh: 孝靜時，其子貞自建業求隨聘使崔長謙赴鄴葬樹，梁武許之。

translations.literal: Under Xiaojing his son Zhen from Jiankang asked to follow envoy Cui Changqian to Ye to bury Shu; Liang Wudi permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaojing his son Zhen followed envoy Cui Changqian to Ye to bury Shu; Liang Wudi permitted.

sentences.zh: 詔贈樹太師、司徒、尚書令。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made Shu Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Shu Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 貞既葬，還江南，位太子舍人。

translations.literal: After burial Zhen returned to Jiangnan as Crown Prince's Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After burial Zhen returned to Jiangnan as Crown Prince's Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及侯景南奔，梁武以貞為咸陽王。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing fled south, Liang Wudi made Zhen Prince of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled south, Liang Wudi made Zhen Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 送景，使為魏主。

translations.literal: Sending Jing off, he made Zhen Wei's sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Sending Jing off, he made Zhen sovereign of Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，景反。

translations.literal: Before long Jing rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jing rebelled.

sentences.zh: 曄字世茂，梁封為桑乾王，卒于南。

translations.literal: Ye, styled Shimao, was enfeoffed by Liang as Prince of Sanggan and died in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, styled Shimao, was made Prince of Sanggan by Liang and died in the south.

sentences.zh: 坦一名穆，字延和。

translations.literal: Tan, also named Mu, styled Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Tan, also named Mu, styled Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 傲狠凶粗，因飲醉之際，於洛橋左右頓辱行人，為道路所患。

translations.literal: Proud, fierce, and coarse; in a drunken interval at both sides of Luo Bridge he abused passersby and was a plague on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and coarse; drunk at Luo Bridge he abused passersby and plagued the road.

sentences.zh: 從叔安豐王延明每切責之曰：「汝凶悖性與身而長。

translations.literal: His uncle the Prince of Anfeng Yanming often sharply rebuked him: "Your fierce perversity grows with your body.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Yanming often rebuked him: "Your fierce perversity grows with your body.

sentences.zh: 昔宋有東海王禕，志性凡劣，時人號曰驢王。

translations.literal: In Song there was the Prince of Donghai Yi, of ordinary will and inferior nature—men of the time called him Prince Ass.
translations.idiomatic: In Song the Prince of Donghai Yi was dull—men called him Prince Ass.

sentences.zh: 我熟觀汝所作，亦恐不免驢號。

translations.literal: I have watched closely what you do—you too may not escape the ass's name.
translations.idiomatic: Watching you closely, you may not escape the ass's name."

sentences.zh: 」當時聞者號為「驢王」。

translations.literal: Those who heard at the time called him "Prince Ass."
translations.idiomatic: Hearers called him "Prince Ass."

sentences.zh: 禧誅後，坦兄翼、樹等五人相繼南奔，故坦得承襲。

translations.literal: After Xi was executed, Tan's elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others in succession fled south, so Tan could inherit.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi's execution Yi, Shu, and five others fled south, so Tan inherited.

sentences.zh: 改封敷城王。

translations.literal: He was reassigned Prince of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned Prince of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 永安初，復本封咸陽郡王。

translations.literal: At the start of Yong'an his original enfeoffment as Prince of Xianyang was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an his Xianyang enfeoffment was restored.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 莊帝從容謂曰：「王才非荀、蔡，中歲屢遷，當由少長朕家，故有超授。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang said at ease: "Your talent is not that of Xun or Cai, yet in mid-years you were often promoted—because you grew up in Our house, hence the extraordinary appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said: "Your talent is not Xun or Cai, yet mid-career promotions came because you grew up in Our house."

sentences.zh: 」初，禧死後，諸子貧乏，坦兄弟為彭城王勰所收養，故有此言。

translations.literal: Earlier after Xi's death the sons were poor; Tan and his brothers were taken in by the Prince of Pengcheng Xie—hence this speech.
translations.idiomatic: After Xi's death the sons were poor; Tan and brothers were raised by the Prince of Pengcheng—hence this.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，其兄樹見禽。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiaowu his elder brother Shu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession Shu was captured.

sentences.zh: 坦見樹既長且賢，慮其代己，密勸朝廷以法除之。

translations.literal: Tan saw Shu was elder and worthy and feared he would replace him, and secretly urged court to remove him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Shu elder and worthy, Tan feared replacement and secretly urged court to kill him.

sentences.zh: 樹知之，泣謂坦曰：「我往因家難，不能死亡，寄食江湖，受其爵命。

translations.literal: Shu knew it and wept, telling Tan: "I came before because of family trouble, unable to die, eating in rivers and lakes, accepting their titles.
translations.idiomatic: Shu wept to Tan: "I came from family trouble, unable to die, eating in exile, accepting titles.

sentences.zh: 今者之來，非由義至，求活而已，豈望榮華？

translations.literal: Today's coming is not from righteousness to the end but to seek life—how could I hope for glory?
translations.idiomatic: Today I come not from duty but to live—how hope for glory?

sentences.zh: 汝何肆其猜忌，忘在原之義！

translations.literal: Why do you indulge suspicion and forget the meaning of kin from one belly!
translations.idiomatic: Why indulge suspicion and forget kin from one belly?

sentences.zh: 腰背雖偉，善無可稱。

translations.literal: Your back and waist are indeed grand, yet in goodness there is nothing to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Your back is broad, yet in goodness nothing to praise."

sentences.zh: 」坦作色而去。

translations.literal: Tan changed color and left.
translations.idiomatic: Tan darkened and left.

sentences.zh: 樹死，竟不臨哭。

translations.literal: When Shu died he never came to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu died Tan never mourned.

sentences.zh: 後曆司徒、太尉、太傅，加侍中、太師、錄尚書事、宗師、司州牧。

translations.literal: Later he held Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor, and was made Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Imperial Clan Director, and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He later held Works, Commandant, Tutor, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Recorder, Imperial Clan Director, and Si Governor.

sentences.zh: 雖祿厚位尊，貪求滋甚，賣獄鬻官，不知紀極。

translations.literal: Though salary was thick and rank high, greedy seeking grew worse; he sold judgments and sold offices beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Though richly salaried, greed grew; he sold judgments and offices beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 為御史劾奏，免官，以王歸第。

translations.literal: Impeached by the censor, he was dismissed and returned to his princely residence.
translations.idiomatic: The censor impeached him; he was dismissed to his residence.

sentences.zh: 尋起為特進，出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised Special Grand Master and sent out as Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Special Grand Master and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 專復聚斂，每百姓納賦，除常別先責絹五匹，然後為受。

translations.literal: He again amassed wealth; whenever the people paid tax, besides the regular levy he first exacted five bolts of silk, then accepted payment.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed again; besides regular tax he first exacted five bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 性好畋漁，無日不出。

translations.literal: He loved hunting and fishing and went out every day without fail.
translations.idiomatic: He loved hunting and fished every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 秋冬獵雉兔，春夏捕魚蟹，鷹犬常數百頭。

translations.literal: Autumn and winter he hunted pheasant and hare; spring and summer he caught fish and crab; hawks and dogs often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn and winter pheasant and hare; spring and summer fish and crab; hundreds of hawks and dogs.

sentences.zh: 自言寧三日不食，不能一日不獵。

translations.literal: He said he could go three days without eating but not one day without hunting.
translations.idiomatic: He said he could go three days without food but not one without hunting.

sentences.zh: 入為太傅。

translations.literal: He entered office as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He entered office as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，准例降爵，封新豐縣公，除特進、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At the start of Qi's Tianbao, by precedent his rank was lowered; he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinfeng, made Special Grand Master and Opener of the Office with Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao his rank lowered to Duke of Xinfeng, Special Grand Master, Opener with Equal Honor.

sentences.zh: 坐子世寶與通直散騎侍郎彭貴平因酒醉誹謗，妄說圖讖，有司奏當死。

translations.literal: Because his son Shibao with Regular Attendant Peng Guiping, drunk, slandered and falsely spoke of portents, the authorities memorialized death.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shibao with Peng Guiping, drunk, slandered and spoke portents; authorities sought death.

sentences.zh: 詔並宥之。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned them both.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned both.

sentences.zh: 坦配北營州，死配所。

translations.literal: Tan was assigned to North Ying Province and died in assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was assigned North Ying Province and died there.

sentences.zh: 趙郡王幹字思直，太和九年，封河南王，位大將軍。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan, styled Sizhi, in the ninth year of Taihe was enfeoffed Prince of Henan and held office of Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao Commandery, Gan, styled Sizhi, in Taihe's ninth year was Prince of Henan and Grand General.

sentences.zh: 孝文篤愛諸弟，以幹總戎別道，誡之曰：「司空穆亮年器可師，散騎常侍盧陽烏才堪詢訪，汝其師之。

translations.literal: Xiaowen deeply loved his younger brothers; because Gan commanded armies on a separate route he admonished him: "Minister of Works Mu Liang in years and vessel may be teacher; Regular Attendant Lu Yangwu in talent may be consulted—you should take them as teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen admonished Gan on a separate command: "Mu Liang may teach you; Lu Yangwu may advise—take them as teachers."

sentences.zh: 」遷洛，改封趙郡王。

translations.literal: After moving the capital he was reassigned Prince of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital move he became Prince of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 除都督、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made Commander and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commander and Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 帝親餞於郊，誡曰：「刑獄之理，先哲所難。

translations.literal: The emperor personally feasted him in the suburbs and admonished: "The principle of punishments and prisons is what the sages found hard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted him at the suburbs: "Punishments and prisons are what sages found hard.

sentences.zh: 然既有邦國，得不自勵也！

translations.literal: Yet since there is a state, can one not urge oneself!
translations.idiomatic: Yet with a state, can one not urge oneself?

sentences.zh: 」詔以李憑為長史，唐茂為司馬，盧尚之為諮議參軍，以匡弼之。

translations.literal: An edict made Li Ping Director, Tang Mao Marshal, and Lu Shangzhi Staff Officer to correct and assist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ping, Tang Mao, and Lu Shangzhi were appointed to correct and assist.

sentences.zh: 而憑等諫，幹殊不納。

translations.literal: When Ping and others remonstrated, Gan utterly did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When they remonstrated, Gan utterly refused.

sentences.zh: 州表斬盜馬人，於律過重，而尚書以幹初臨，縱而不劾。

translations.literal: The province memorialized execution of a horse thief—by law excessively heavy—and the Masters of Writing, because Gan had just arrived, indulged and did not impeach.
translations.idiomatic: The province executed a horse thief beyond the law; the Masters of Writing indulged him as newly arrived.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「尚書曲阿朕意，實傷皇度。

translations.literal: An edict said: "The Masters of Writing bent to Our intent—truly it wounds imperial measure.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The Masters of Writing bent to Our intent—truly wounding imperial measure.

sentences.zh: 幹闇於政理，律外重刑，並可推聞。

translations.literal: Gan is dark in governing principle and imposed heavy punishment outside the law—both may be reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Gan is dark in governing and imposed lawless heavy punishment—both should be reported upward."

sentences.zh: 」後轉特進、司州牧。

translations.literal: " Later he was transferred to Special Guardian and Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was made Special Guardian and Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕南討，詔幹都督中外諸軍事，給鼓吹一部，甲士三百人，出入殿門。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south, Gan was ordered to supervise all military affairs within and without, given one set of martial music, three hundred armored soldiers, and permission to enter and leave the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign the emperor made Gan supreme commander of all forces at home and abroad, granted him a full martial band, three hundred armored guards, and the right to pass in and out of the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 幹貪淫不遵政典，御史中尉李彪將糾劾之，會遇幹于尚書下舍，屏左右誡之，而幹悠然不以為意。

translations.literal: Gan was greedy and licentious and did not follow the statutes; Censor-in-Chief Li Biao was about to impeach him. He happened to meet Gan in the subordinate quarters of the Masters of Writing, dismissed attendants, and admonished him—but Gan remained at ease and took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Gan was greedy and licentious and ignored the law. Censor-in-Chief Li Biao was about to impeach him when he met Gan in the Masters of Writing quarters, sent away his attendants, and warned him face to face. Gan remained perfectly unconcerned.

sentences.zh: 彪表彈之。

translations.literal: Biao memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Biao submitted an impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔幹與北海王詳俱隨太子詣行在所。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Gan and Prince of Beihai Xiang to follow the crown prince to the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Gan and Prince of Beihai Xiang to accompany the crown prince to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 及至，密使左右察其意色，無有憂悔，乃親數其過，杖之一百，免所居官，以王還第。

translations.literal: When they arrived, the emperor secretly had attendants observe their expressions; seeing no worry or remorse, he personally enumerated Gan's faults, beat him a hundred strokes, removed him from office, and sent him home as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: On their arrival the emperor secretly had attendants watch their faces. Seeing no sign of worry or remorse, he personally listed Gan's offenses, gave him a hundred strokes of the rod, stripped his offices, and sent him home in princely rank only.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰靈王。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Prince Ling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Prince Ling.

sentences.zh: 陪葬長陵。

translations.literal: He was buried beside Changling.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Changling.

sentences.zh: 子謐襲封。

translations.literal: His son Mi inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 幹妃穆氏表謐及謐母趙等悖禮愆常。

translations.literal: Gan's consort Lady Mu memorialized that Mi and Mi's mother Zhao and others violated ritual and were constantly irregular.
translations.idiomatic: Gan's consort Lady Mu reported that Mi, Mi's mother Zhao, and others had violated ritual and behaved with constant impropriety.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「妾於女君，猶婦人事姑舅；

translations.literal: The edict said: "A concubine toward her lady is like a daughter-in-law toward mother-in-law and father-in-law;
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "A concubine toward her lady is like a daughter-in-law toward her husband's parents;

sentences.zh: 妾子於君母，禮加如子之恭。

translations.literal: a concubine's son toward his lord's mother—ritual adds the respect due a son.
translations.idiomatic: a concubine's son toward his lord's mother should show a son's full respect.

sentences.zh: 何得黷我風猷，可付宗正依禮正罪。

translations.literal: How can you defile my customs? Hand them to the Director of the Imperial Clan for punishment according to ritual."
translations.idiomatic: How dare you defile my house? Hand them to the Director of the Imperial Clan for punishment according to ritual."

sentences.zh: 」謐在母喪，聽聲飲戲，為御史中尉李平所彈。

translations.literal: During his mother's mourning Mi listened to music and drank at games; Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning Mi listened to music and drank at games; Censor-in-Chief Li Ping impeached him.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，復封。

translations.literal: He met an amnesty and was restored to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty followed and his fief was restored.

sentences.zh: 後為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 謐兄諶，字興伯，性平和，位都官尚書。

translations.literal: Mi's elder brother Chen, styled Xingbo, was mild by nature and held the office of Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's elder brother Chen, styled Xingbo, was even-tempered by nature and served as Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮之入洛陽，啟莊帝欲遷都晉陽。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, he petitioned Emperor Zhuangdi to move the capital to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang he asked Emperor Zhuangdi to move the capital to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 帝以問諶，爭之以為不可。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Chen; he argued that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Chen, who argued that it must not be done.

sentences.zh: 榮怒曰：「何關君而固執也！

translations.literal: Rong said in anger: "What business is it of yours to be so stubborn!
translations.idiomatic: Rong said in anger, "What is it to you that you should be so stubborn!

sentences.zh: 且河陰之役，君應之。

translations.literal: Besides, at the massacre at Heyin you had a part in it."
translations.idiomatic: And at the massacre at Heyin you had your share."

sentences.zh: 」諶曰：「天下事天下論之，何以河陰之酷而恐元諶！

translations.literal: Chen said: "The affairs of the realm are discussed by the realm—why should Yuan Chen fear Heyin's cruelty!
translations.idiomatic: Chen said, "The realm's affairs are the realm's to judge—why should Yuan Chen fear the cruelty of Heyin!

sentences.zh: 宗室戚屬，位居常伯，生既無益，死復何損！

translations.literal: As kin of the imperial house, holding the rank of regular supervisor, alive I am of no use, dead of no loss!
translations.idiomatic: I am kin of the imperial house and hold a supervisor's rank—alive I am of little use, dead I am no great loss!

sentences.zh: 正使今日碎首流腸，亦無所懼。

translations.literal: Even if today my head is shattered and my bowels spill, I have nothing to fear."
translations.idiomatic: Even if today my head is smashed and my guts spill out, I have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」榮大怒，欲罪諶。

translations.literal: Rong was greatly enraged and wished to punish Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was furious and meant to punish Chen.

sentences.zh: 其從弟世隆固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Shilong firmly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Shilong remonstrated firmly and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不震悚。

translations.literal: Those who saw it were all shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 諶顏色自若。

translations.literal: Chen's countenance was as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's face did not change.
