sentences.zh: 後數日，帝與榮見宮闕壯麗，列樹成行，乃歎曰：「臣一昨愚志，有遷京之意，今見皇居壯觀，亦何用去河洛而就晉陽。

translations.literal: Some days later the emperor and Rong saw the palace halls magnificent and trees in rows, and sighed: "I the other day in foolish intent had a mind to move the capital; now seeing the imperial residence so grand, what use is there to leave Heluo for Jinyang?
translations.idiomatic: Days later the emperor and Rong saw the palace halls magnificent and trees standing in rows. Rong sighed, "Only yesterday in foolish intent I wished to move the capital; now that I see the imperial residence so grand, what need to leave Heluo for Jinyang?

sentences.zh: 臣熟思元尚書言，深不可奪。

translations.literal: I have thought over Director Yuan's words—they truly cannot be overturned."
translations.idiomatic: I have weighed Director Yuan's words—they truly cannot be overturned."

sentences.zh: 」是以遷都議因罷。

translations.literal: Thus the proposal to move the capital was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal to move the capital was therefore dropped.

sentences.zh: 永安元年，拜尚書左僕射，封魏郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yong'an he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yong'an he was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Prince of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 諶本年長，應襲王封，為其父靈王愛其弟謐，以為世子。

translations.literal: Chen was the elder by years and should have inherited the princely fief, but his father Prince Ling loved his younger brother Mi and made him heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chen was the elder and should have inherited the fief, but his father Prince Ling favored his younger brother Mi and named him heir.

sentences.zh: 莊帝詔復諶封趙郡王。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuangdi ordered Chen's fief as Prince of Zhao commandery restored.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuangdi restored Chen's fief as Prince of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 歷位司空、太保、太尉、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He held in succession the offices of Minister of Works, Grand Guardian, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Minister of Works, Grand Guardian, Grand Commandant, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，拜大司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaojing's reign he was made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡孝懿。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Xiaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Xiaoyi.

sentences.zh: 諶無他才識，歷位雖重，時人忽之。

translations.literal: Chen had no other talent or insight; though his offices were weighty, men of the time slighted him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen had no other talent or insight; though his posts were weighty, his contemporaries thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 謐弟譚，頗強立，少為宗室推敬，卒于秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Tan was quite forceful; in youth he was respected among the imperial kin and died as Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Tan was forceful by nature; in youth the imperial kin respected him, and he died as Governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 譚弟讞，貪暴無禮。

translations.literal: Tan's younger brother Yan was greedy and violent and without ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Tan's younger brother Yan was greedy, violent, and without propriety.

sentences.zh: 位太中大夫，封平鄉男。

translations.literal: He held the office of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was enfeoffed as Baron of Pingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He held the office of Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was enfeoffed Baron of Pingxiang.

sentences.zh: 河陰遇害。

translations.literal: He was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 廣陵王羽字叔翻，太和九年封，加侍中，為外都大官。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangling Yu, styled Shufan, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe, made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangling Yu, styled Shufan, was enfeoffed in the ninth year of Taihe, made Attendant-in-Ordinary, and appointed Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.

sentences.zh: 羽少聰慧，有斷獄之稱。

translations.literal: Yu in youth was clever and had a reputation for deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was clever from youth and had a reputation for judging cases.

sentences.zh: 後罷三都，以羽為大理，典決京師獄訟。

translations.literal: Later the three capitals offices were abolished and Yu was made Director of the Court of Justice, deciding capital lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: When the three capital offices were abolished Yu was made Director of the Court of Justice and decided lawsuits in the capital.

sentences.zh: 遷特進、尚書右僕射，又為太子太保、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Special Guardian and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then made Grand Tutor to the crown prince and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Special Guardian and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, then made Grand Tutor to the crown prince and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 孝文將南討，遣羽持節安撫六鎮。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen was about to campaign south he sent Yu with credentials to pacify the six garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen prepared the southern campaign he sent Yu with credentials to pacify the six frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 發其突騎，夷夏寧悅。

translations.literal: He mobilized their shock cavalry; Chinese and barbarians alike were content.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized their shock cavalry; Chinese and barbarians alike were content.

sentences.zh: 還領廷尉卿。

translations.literal: On his return he took charge of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he took charge of the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 及車駕發，羽與太尉元丕留守。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage set out, Yu and Grand Commandant Yuan Pi remained to guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched south, Yu and Grand Commandant Yuan Pi remained behind as guardians.

sentences.zh: 帝友愛諸弟，及將別，不忍早分，詔羽從至雁門。

translations.literal: The emperor loved his younger brothers dearly; when they were about to part he could not bear to separate early and ordered Yu to follow as far as Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved his younger brothers dearly; unwilling to part too soon, he ordered Yu to accompany him as far as Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 及令羽歸，望其稱效，故賜如意以表心。

translations.literal: When he ordered Yu to return, hoping for his worthy service, he therefore gave him a ruyi scepter to express his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When he sent Yu back, expecting worthy service, he gave him a ruyi scepter as a token of his affection.

sentences.zh: 十八年，羽表辭廷尉，不許。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Yu memorialized to resign the Court of Justice; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Yu asked to resign the Court of Justice; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 羽奏：「外考令文，每歲終，州鎮列牧守績狀。

translations.literal: Yu memorialized: "The statutes on external evaluation require that at year's end provinces and garrisons list the governors' and magistrates' performance.
translations.idiomatic: Yu memorialized, "The statutes on external evaluation require that at year's end provinces and garrisons list governors' and magistrates' performance.

sentences.zh: 及至再考，隨其品第，以彰黜陟。

translations.literal: When the second evaluation comes, according to their grades they are promoted or demoted to show reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the second evaluation they are ranked and promoted or demoted to show reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 雖外有成令，而內令未班。

translations.literal: Though there is a completed statute outside, the inner statute has not been promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Though the outer rule exists, the inner rule has not yet been issued.

sentences.zh: 內外考察，理應同等。

translations.literal: Internal and external examination should in principle be equal.
translations.idiomatic: Internal and external examination ought to be equal in principle.

sentences.zh: 臣輒推准外考，以定京官績行。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to apply the outer evaluation as standard to fix the capital officials' conduct and performance."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant ventures to apply the outer evaluation as standard to fix the conduct and performance of capital officials."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「論考之事，理在不輕，問績之方，應關朕聽。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The matter of evaluation in principle is not light; the method of inquiring into performance should concern my hearing.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Evaluation is no light matter; the method of reviewing performance should reach my ears.

sentences.zh: 輒爾輕發，殊為躁也。

translations.literal: To issue it so lightly is quite rash.
translations.idiomatic: To issue it so lightly is rash indeed.

sentences.zh: 今始維夏，且待至秋。

translations.literal: Now it is barely midsummer—wait until autumn."
translations.idiomatic: It is barely midsummer—wait until autumn."

sentences.zh: 」後孝文臨朝堂考群臣，顧謂羽曰：「上下二等，可為三品，中等但為一品。

translations.literal: Later Xiaowen at the court hall evaluated the ministers and, turning to Yu, said: "The upper and lower grades can be made three grades; the middle grade need only be one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowen evaluated the ministers at court and said to Yu, "The upper and lower grades may be made three grades; the middle grade need only be one.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，上下是黜陟之科，故旌絲發之美；

translations.literal: The reason is that upper and lower are the grades of promotion and demotion, therefore to display the beauty of even a thread's difference;
translations.idiomatic: Upper and lower are the grades of promotion and demotion, and should display even the finest distinction;

sentences.zh: 中等守本，事可大通。」

translations.literal: the middle keeps to the norm—the matter can be broadly applied."
translations.idiomatic: the middle keeps to the norm and can be applied broadly."

sentences.zh: 帝又謂羽曰：「汝功勤之績不聞于朝，阿黨之音頻幹朕聽。

translations.literal: The emperor again said to Yu: "Your merit and diligence are not heard of at court, but the sound of faction reaches my ears again and again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said again to Yu, "Your merit and diligence are not heard of at court, yet reports of faction reach my ears again and again.

sentences.zh: 今黜汝錄尚書、廷尉，但居特進、太保。

translations.literal: Now I demote you from Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Court of Justice, but keep you as Special Guardian and Grand Guardian."
translations.idiomatic: I demote you from Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Court of Justice and leave you only Special Guardian and Grand Guardian."

sentences.zh: 」又謂尚書令陸睿曰：「叔翻在省之初，甚著善稱；

translations.literal: He also said to Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui: "Shufan at first in the Secretariat was very well spoken of;
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui, "Shufan at first in the Secretariat was well spoken of;

sentences.zh: 自近以來，偏頗懈怠。

translations.literal: of late he has been partial and slack.
translations.idiomatic: of late he has grown partial and slack.

sentences.zh: 豈不由卿等隨其邪偽之心？

translations.literal: Is it not because you and the others follow his crooked heart?
translations.idiomatic: Is that not because you follow his crooked inclinations?

sentences.zh: 今奪卿尚書令祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I strip your salary as Director of the Masters of Writing for one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I strip your salary as director for one payment cycle."

sentences.zh: 」謂左僕射元贊曰：「計叔翻之黜，卿應大辟。

translations.literal: He said to Left Vice Director Yuan Zan: "Considering Shufan's demotion, you ought to receive death.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Left Vice Director Yuan Zan, "By Shufan's demotion you ought to receive death.

sentences.zh: 但以咎歸一人，不復相罪。

translations.literal: But because the blame falls on one man, I do not punish you further.
translations.idiomatic: But the blame falls on one man and I will not punish you further.

sentences.zh: 今解卿少師之任，削祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I release you from Junior Preceptor and cut your salary one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I release you from Junior Preceptor and cut your salary one cycle."

sentences.zh: 」詔吏部尚書澄曰：「觀叔父神志驕傲，可解少保。

translations.literal: The edict to Minister of Personnel Shang said: "I see my uncle's spirit proud—he may be released from Junior Guardian."
translations.idiomatic: He edicted Minister of Personnel Shang, "I see my uncle's spirit is proud; release him from Junior Guardian."

sentences.zh: 」又謂長兼尚書于果曰：「卿不能勤謹夙夜，數辭以疾。

translations.literal: He also said to long-concurrent Director Yu Guo: "You are not diligent and careful morning and night, and often plead illness.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to long-concurrent Director Yu Guo, "You are not diligent morning and night and often plead illness.

sentences.zh: 今解卿長兼，可光祿大夫、守尚書，削祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I release you from long-concurrent status; you may be Grand Master for the Palace, acting Director of the Masters of Writing, and I cut your salary one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I release you from long-concurrent status; you may be Grand Master for the Palace and acting director, and I cut your salary one cycle."

sentences.zh: 」又謂守尚書尉羽曰：「卿恭勤。

translations.literal: He also said to acting Director Yu Yu: "You are respectful and diligent.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to acting Director Yu Yu, "You are respectful and diligent.

sentences.zh: 在集書，殊無憂存左史之事。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat you have no worry for the left historiographer's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Secretariat you have no concern for the left historiographer's duties.

sentences.zh: 今降為長兼常侍，亦削祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I demote you to long-concurrent Regular Attendant and also cut your salary one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I demote you to long-concurrent Regular Attendant and cut your salary one cycle."

sentences.zh: 」又謂守尚書盧陽烏曰：「卿在集書，雖非高功，為一省文學之士，常不以左史在意。

translations.literal: He also said to acting Director Lu Yangwu: "In the Secretariat, though not of high merit, you are a literary man of the department and constantly pay no mind to the left historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: He also said to acting Director Lu Yangwu, "In the Secretariat, though not of high merit, you are a literary man of the office and constantly ignore the left historiographer.

sentences.zh: 今降卿長兼王師，守常侍、尚書如故，奪常侍祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I demote you to long-concurrent Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; acting Regular Attendant and Director as before; I strip your Regular Attendant salary one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I demote you to long-concurrent Preceptor to the Heir Apparent; acting Regular Attendant and Director as before; I strip one cycle of Regular Attendant salary."

sentences.zh: 」謂左丞公孫良、右丞乞伏義受曰：「卿等不能正心直言，罪應大辟。

translations.literal: He said to Left Assistant Gongsun Liang and Right Assistant Qifu Yishou: "You do not correct your hearts and speak plainly—your crime deserves death.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Left Assistant Gongsun Liang and Right Assistant Qifu Yishou, "You do not correct your hearts and speak plainly—your crime deserves death.

sentences.zh: 但以事鐘叔翻，故不能別致貶。

translations.literal: But because the affair centers on Shufan, I cannot separately impose demotion.
translations.idiomatic: But because the affair centers on Shufan I cannot separately demote you.

sentences.zh: 二丞可以白衣守本官。

translations.literal: Both assistants may in plain dress keep their original offices.
translations.idiomatic: Both assistants may in plain dress keep their original offices.

sentences.zh: 冠服、祿恤盡皆削奪。

translations.literal: Cap, robes, and salary allowances are all stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Cap, robes, and salary allowances are all stripped.

sentences.zh: 若三年有成，還復本任；

translations.literal: If in three years there is achievement, restore the original posts;
translations.idiomatic: If in three years there is achievement, restore your original posts;

sentences.zh: 如其無成，則永歸南畝。

translations.literal: if there is none, then forever return to the southern fields."
translations.idiomatic: if none, then forever return to the southern fields."

sentences.zh: 」謂散騎常侍元景曰：「卿等自任集書，合省逋墮，致使王言遺滯，起居不修。

translations.literal: He said to Regular Attendant Yuan Jing: "You and the others took charge of the Secretariat yourselves; the whole department fell into neglect, causing imperial words to lag and the record of attendance to go unrepaired.
translations.idiomatic: He said to Regular Attendant Yuan Jing, "You took charge of the Secretariat yourselves; the whole department fell into neglect, imperial words lagged, and the attendance record went unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 今降為中大夫、守常侍，奪祿一周。

translations.literal: Now I demote you to Grand Master of the Palace, acting Regular Attendant, and strip your salary one cycle."
translations.idiomatic: I demote you to Grand Master of the Palace, acting Regular Attendant, and strip your salary one cycle."

sentences.zh: 」又謂諫議大夫李彥：「卿實不稱職，可去諫議，退為元士。

translations.literal: He also said to Remonstrating Master Li Yan: "You truly do not fit the office; you may leave remonstrance and withdraw to gentleman of the Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Remonstrating Master Li Yan, "You truly do not fit the office; leave remonstrance and withdraw to gentleman of the Yuan."

sentences.zh: 」又謂中庶子游肇及中書舍人李平：「識學可觀，可為中第。」

translations.literal: He also said to Palace Aide You Zhao and Secretariat Drafter Li Ping: "Your learning and insight are admirable—you may be middle grade."
translations.idiomatic: He also said to Palace Aide You Zhao and Secretariat Drafter Li Ping, "Your learning and insight are admirable—you may be middle grade."

sentences.zh: 初，孝文引陸睿、元贊等前，曰：「朕為天子，何假中原？

translations.literal: Earlier Xiaowen had summoned Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and the others before him and said: "I am Son of Heaven—why need the Central Plains?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Xiaowen had summoned Lu Rui, Yuan Zan, and the others and said, "I am Son of Heaven—why need the Central Plains?

sentences.zh: 欲令卿等子孫博見多知。

translations.literal: I wish your sons and grandsons to see much and know much.
translations.idiomatic: I wish your sons and grandsons to see much and know much.

sentences.zh: 若永居恆北，遇不好文主，卿等子弟不免面牆也。

translations.literal: If you forever dwell in the far north and meet an unlettered lord, your sons and grandsons will not escape facing the wall."
translations.idiomatic: If you forever dwell in the far north and meet an unlettered lord, your sons and grandsons will not escape ignorance."

sentences.zh: 」陸睿對曰：「實如明詔。

translations.literal: Lu Rui replied: "It is truly as the clear edict says.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rui replied, "It is truly as the clear edict says.

sentences.zh: 金氏若不入仕漢朝，七葉知名，亦不可得也。

translations.literal: If the Jin clan had not entered office in the Han dynasty, seven generations of fame would also have been unobtainable."
translations.idiomatic: If the Jin clan had not entered office under the Han, seven generations of fame would never have been possible."

sentences.zh: 」帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 帝幸羽第，與諸弟言曰：「朕親受人訟，知廣陵之明瞭。

translations.literal: The emperor visited Yu's residence and said to his younger brothers: "I personally receive lawsuits and know Guangling's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Yu's residence and told his younger brothers, "I personally hear lawsuits and know how clear Guangling is.

sentences.zh: 」咸陽王禧曰：「臣年為廣陵兄，明為廣陵弟。

translations.literal: Prince of Xianyang Xi said: "By years I am Guangling's elder brother; by clarity I am Guangling's younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Xi said, "By years I am Guangling's elder brother; by clarity I am Guangling's younger brother."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：我為汝兄，汝為羽昆，汝復何恨！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: I am your elder brother, you are Yu's peers—what more do you resent!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I am your elder brother; you are Yu's peers—what more do you resent!"

sentences.zh: 」車駕南伐，除開府、青州刺史。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage campaigned south, he was made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: " On the southern campaign he was made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 詔羽曰：「海服之寄，故唯宗良。

translations.literal: The edict to Yu said: "The charge of the coastal regions—therefore only a worthy of the clan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict to Yu said, "The coastal charge belongs only to a worthy of the clan.

sentences.zh: 唯酒唯田，可不誡歟！

translations.literal: Only wine, only fields—can you not be warned!
translations.idiomatic: Only wine, only fields—will you not take warning!"

sentences.zh: 」宣武即位，遷司州牧。

translations.literal: When Xuanwu took the throne, Yu was transferred to Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne Yu was transferred to Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 及帝覽政，引入內，面授司徒。

translations.literal: When the emperor took charge of government he was brought inside and personally invested as Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took charge of government Yu was brought inside and personally invested as Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 請為司空，乃許之。

translations.literal: He asked to be Minister of Works and it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be Minister of Works and it was granted.

sentences.zh: 羽先淫員外郎馮俊興妻，夜私遊。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu had debauched the wife of the Extraordinary Attendant Feng Junxing and went out at night in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yu had debauched the wife of Extraordinary Attendant Feng Junxing and went out at night in secret.

sentences.zh: 為俊興所擊，積日秘匿，薨於府。

translations.literal: Junxing struck him; for many days he kept it secret, and he died in his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Junxing struck him; for many days he kept it hidden, and he died in his residence.

sentences.zh: 宣武親臨哀，贈司徒，諡曰慧。

translations.literal: Xuanwu personally came to mourn; he was posthumously made Minister of Education with posthumous title Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu came in person to mourn; he was posthumously made Minister of Education with the posthumous title Hui.

sentences.zh: 子恭襲，是為節閔帝。

translations.literal: His son Gong inherited—this was Emperor Jiemin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gong inherited—this was Emperor Jiemin.

sentences.zh: 恭兄欣，字慶樂，性粗率，好鷹犬。

translations.literal: Gong's elder brother Xin, styled Qingle, was coarse by nature and fond of hawks and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Gong's elder brother Xin, styled Qingle, was coarse by nature and fond of hawks and dogs.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，封沛郡王，後封淮陽王。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei commandery, later Prince of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was enfeoffed Prince of Pei commandery, later Prince of Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，加太師、開府，復封廣陵王，太傅、司州牧，尋除大司馬。

translations.literal: Under Xiaowu he was made Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, again enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Sizhou, then soon removed as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was made Grand Preceptor and Commander-in-Chief, again enfeoffed Prince of Guangling, Grand Tutor, and Governor of Sizhou, then soon made Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 孝武入關中，欣投托人使達長安，為太傅、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Xiaowu entered Guanzhong, Xin entrusted an envoy to reach Chang'an and was made Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong Xin sent an envoy to reach Chang'an and was made Grand Tutor and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 欣于中興宗室，禮遇最隆，自廣平諸王，悉居其下。

translations.literal: Among the imperial kin of the Zhongxing era Xin received the most honored treatment; from Prince of Guangping and the other princes, all were below him.
translations.idiomatic: Among the imperial kin of the Zhongxing restoration Xin received the highest honors; from Prince of Guangping downward all ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 又為大宗師，進大塚宰、中軍大都督。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand Clan Master, promoted to Grand Steward of the Tomb, and Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Clan Master, promoted Grand Steward of the Tomb, and Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 大統中，為柱國大將軍、太傅。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he was Pillar of State, Grand General, and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era he was Pillar of State, Grand General, and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂欣曰：「王三為太傅，再為太師，自古人臣，示聞此例。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said to Xin: "You have thrice been Grand Tutor and twice Grand Preceptor—from antiquity among subjects, I have never heard this example."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said to Xin, "You have thrice been Grand Tutor and twice Grand Preceptor—from antiquity among subjects I have never heard such an example."

sentences.zh: 」欣遜謝而已。

translations.literal: Xin declined with apologies only.
translations.idiomatic: Xin declined with apologies only.

sentences.zh: 後拜司徒。

translations.literal: Later he was made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 恭帝初，遷大丞相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gongdi's reign he was transferred to Grand Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gongdi's reign he was transferred to Grand Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 薨，諡曰容。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Rong.

sentences.zh: 欣好營產業，多所樹藝，京師名果皆出其園。

translations.literal: Xin loved to build estates and planted much; the capital's famous fruits all came from his gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Xin loved to build estates and planted widely; the capital's famous fruits all came from his gardens.

sentences.zh: 所汲引及寮佐咸非長者，為世所鄙。

translations.literal: Those he brought in and his staff were none of them men of stature; the age despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those he brought in and his staff were none of them men of stature, and the age despised him.

sentences.zh: 高陽王雍字思穆，少俶儻不恆。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, styled Simu, in youth was unconventional and unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yong, styled Simu, in youth was unconventional and unsteady.

sentences.zh: 孝文曰：'吾亦未能測此兒之深淺，然觀其任真率素，或年器晚成。

translations.literal: Xiaowen said: 'I also cannot measure this boy's depth; yet seeing him sincere and plain by nature, perhaps in years and capacity he will mature late.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "I too cannot measure this boy's depth; yet seeing him sincere and plain by nature, perhaps in years and capacity he will mature late.

sentences.zh: 」太和九年，封潁川王。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: " In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 或說雍待士以營聲譽，雍曰：「吾天子之子，位為諸王，用聲名何為？

translations.literal: Some said Yong treated scholars to build reputation; Yong said: "I am the Son of Heaven's son, rank among princes—what use is reputation?
translations.idiomatic: Some said Yong cultivated scholars to build reputation; Yong said, "I am the Son of Heaven's son and rank among princes—what use is reputation?

sentences.zh: 」改封高陽。

translations.literal: " He was changed to Prince of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was changed to Prince of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 後為相州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 帝誡曰：「為牧之道，亦易亦難。

translations.literal: The emperor admonished him: "The way of governing is both easy and hard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admonished him, "Governing is both easy and hard.

sentences.zh: 其身正，不令而行，故便是易；

translations.literal: If the person is upright, without giving orders things are done—therefore it is easy;
translations.idiomatic: If the person is upright, without giving orders things are done—therefore it is easy;

sentences.zh: 其身不正，雖令不從，故曰是難。

translations.literal: if the person is not upright, though orders are given they are not followed—therefore it is said to be hard."
translations.idiomatic: if the person is not upright, though orders are given they are not followed—therefore it is hard."

sentences.zh: 」宣武初，遷冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu he was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was transferred to Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 雍在二州，微有聲稱，入拜司州牧。

translations.literal: In the two provinces Yong had slight reputation; he entered court as Governor of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the two provinces Yong had some reputation; he entered court as Governor of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝時幸雍第，皆盡家人禮。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Yong's residence, all used family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Yong's residence they used full family ritual.

sentences.zh: 遷司空，轉太尉，加侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works, then Grand Commandant, and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Works, then Grand Commandant, and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 尋除太保，領太尉、侍中如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Grand Guardian, retaining Grand Commandant and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Guardian, retaining Grand Commandant and Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，詔雍入居太極西柏堂，諮決大政，給親信二十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign an edict ordered Yong to dwell in the Western Cypress Hall of Taiji, consult on great affairs, and gave him twenty trusted men.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign an edict ordered Yong to dwell in the Western Cypress Hall of Taiji, consult on great affairs, and gave him twenty trusted men.

sentences.zh: 又詔雍為宗師，進太傅、侍中，領太尉公，別敕將作營國子學寺，給雍居之。

translations.literal: Another edict made Yong Grand Clan Master, promoted to Grand Tutor and Attendant-in-Ordinary, retaining Grand Commandant; a separate edict had the Directorate of Works build the National University temple for Yong to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict made Yong Grand Clan Master and promoted him to Grand Tutor and Attendant-in-Ordinary while retaining Grand Commandant; a separate edict had the Directorate of Works build the National University temple for his residence.

sentences.zh: 領軍于忠擅權專恣，僕射郭祚勸雍出之，忠矯詔殺祚及尚書裴植，廢雍以王歸第。

translations.literal: Commander of the Palace Guards Yu Zhong seized power and acted as he pleased; Vice Director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him; Zhong forged an edict and killed Zuo and Director of the Masters of Writing Pei Zhi, deposed Yong and sent him home as a prince.
translations.idiomatic: Commander of the Palace Guards Yu Zhong seized power and acted as he pleased; Vice Director Guo Zuo urged Yong to remove him; Zhong forged an edict and killed Zuo and Director Pei Zhi, deposed Yong, and sent him home as a prince.

sentences.zh: 朝有大事，使黃門就諮訪之。

translations.literal: When the court had great affairs they sent the Yellow Gate to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court had great affairs they sent the Yellow Gate to consult him.

sentences.zh: 忠尋復矯詔將殺雍，以問侍中崔光，拒之乃止。

translations.literal: Zhong soon again forged an edict intending to kill Yong; he asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, who refused—and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong soon forged another edict intending to kill Yong; he asked Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang, who refused, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 未幾，靈太后臨朝，出忠為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long Empress Dowager Ling held court and sent Zhong out as Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Empress Dowager Ling held court and sent Zhong out as Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 雍表暴忠罪，陳己不能匡正，請返私門。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized exposing Zhong's crimes and stating that he himself could not correct them, asking to return to private life.
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized exposing Zhong's crimes, confessing that he could not correct them, and asking to return to private life.

sentences.zh: 靈太后感忠保護之勳，不問其罪。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling was moved by Zhong's merit in protecting her and did not inquire into his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling was moved by Zhong's merit in protecting her and did not inquire into his crimes.

sentences.zh: 除雍侍中、太師，領司州牧。

translations.literal: Yong was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Preceptor and took charge of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Preceptor and took charge of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍表請王公已下賤妾悉不聽用織成錦繡、金玉珠璣，違者以違旨論；

translations.literal: Yong memorialized asking that from princes and dukes downward concubines of low rank all be forbidden woven brocade, gold, jade, and pearls—violators to be judged by violating the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Yong memorialized that from princes and dukes downward all low-rank concubines be forbidden woven brocade, gold, jade, and pearls—violators judged by violating the edict;

sentences.zh: 奴婢悉不得衣綾錦纈，止於縵繒而已；

translations.literal: slave girls must not wear damask or brocade patterns, only plain silk;
translations.idiomatic: slave girls must not wear patterned damask or brocade, only plain silk;

sentences.zh: 奴則布服，並不得以金銀為釵帶，犯者鞭一百。

translations.literal: male slaves only cloth garments, and none may use gold or silver for hairpins and belts—violators receive a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: male slaves only cloth garments, and none may use gold or silver for hairpins and belts—violators receive a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 太后從之，而不能久也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager followed it, but could not keep it long.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager agreed, but could not keep it long.

sentences.zh: 詔雍乘步挽出入掖門，又以本官錄尚書事，朝晡侍講。

translations.literal: An edict allowed Yong to ride a drawn carriage in and out of the side gates, and with his original office to record the Masters of Writing; morning and evening he attended lectures.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed Yong to ride a drawn carriage through the side gates and, with his original office, to record the Masters of Writing; morning and evening he attended lectures.

sentences.zh: 明帝覽政，詔雍乘車出入大司馬門，進位丞相。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took charge of government an edict allowed Yong to ride in and out of the Grand Marshal Gate and promoted him to Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took charge of government an edict allowed Yong to ride through the Grand Marshal Gate and promoted him to Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 又詔依齊郡順王簡太和故事，朝訖引坐，特優拜伏之禮。

translations.literal: Another edict followed the Taihe precedent of Prince Jian of Qi commandery Shun: after court, he was invited to sit and received special bowing and prostration.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict followed the Taihe precedent of Prince Jian of Qi commandery Shun: after court he was invited to sit and received special bowing and prostration.

sentences.zh: 總攝內外，與元叉同決庶政。

translations.literal: He oversaw internal and external affairs and with Yuan Cha jointly decided ordinary government.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw internal and external affairs and with Yuan Cha jointly decided ordinary government.

sentences.zh: 歲祿粟至四萬石，伎侍盈房，榮貴之盛，昆弟莫及。

translations.literal: Annual salary grain reached forty thousand piculs; performing girls filled the rooms; splendor and honor such that his brothers could not match.
translations.idiomatic: Annual salary grain reached forty thousand piculs; performing girls filled his rooms; splendor and honor his brothers could not match.

sentences.zh: 元妃盧氏薨後，更納博陵崔顯妹，欲以為妃。

translations.literal: After his primary consort the Lu clan died, he took as consort the younger sister of Boling Cui Xian and wished to make her consort.
translations.idiomatic: After his primary consort Lady Lu died he took as consort the younger sister of Boling Cui Xian and wished to make her his princess consort.

sentences.zh: 宣武初以崔顯世號東崔，地寒望劣，難之，久乃聽許。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu, because Cui Xian's house was called Eastern Cui in the age, of low land and weak standing, it was difficult; only after long delay was permission granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, because Cui Xian's house was called Eastern Cui in the age and was of low land and weak standing, the match was resisted; only after long delay was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 延昌已後，疏棄崔氏，別房幽禁，僅給衣食而已。

translations.literal: After Yan-chang he neglected the Cui clan, kept her in a separate chamber under close guard, giving only food and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan-chang he neglected the Cui clan, kept her in a separate chamber under close guard, giving only food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 未幾，崔暴薨，多雲雍毆殺也。

translations.literal: Before long Lady Cui died violently; many said Yong beat her to death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lady Cui died violently; many said Yong beat her to death.

sentences.zh: 靈太后許賜其女伎，未及送之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling had granted him her female performers but had not yet sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling had granted him her female performers but had not yet sent them.

sentences.zh: 雍遣其閹豎丁鵝，自至宮內，料簡四人，冒以還第。

translations.literal: Yong sent his eunuch Ding E in person to the inner palace, selected four on his own authority, and took them back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent his eunuch Ding E in person to the inner palace, selected four on his own authority, and took them back to his residence.

sentences.zh: 太后責其專擅，追停之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager reproached his usurpation and halted it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager reproached his usurpation and halted it.

sentences.zh: 孝莊初，于河陰遇害。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaozhuang he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaozhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、相國，諡文穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-axe and Chancellor; posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-axe and Chancellor with the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 雍識懷短淺，又無學業，雖位居朝首，不為時情所推。

translations.literal: Yong's insight was shallow and he had no learning; though he stood at the head of court, he was not pushed by the mood of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's insight was shallow and he had no learning; though he stood at the head of court, the mood of the time did not favor him.

sentences.zh: 自熙平以後，朝政褫落。

translations.literal: From Xiping onward court government fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: From the Xiping era onward court government fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 及清河王懌之死，元叉專政，天下大責歸焉。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died, Yuan Cha monopolized government; the realm's great blame fell on him.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi died, Yuan Cha monopolized government and the realm's great blame fell on Yong.

sentences.zh: 嫡之泰，字昌，頗有時譽，位太常卿，與雍同時遇害。

translations.literal: His eldest son Tai, styled Chang, had some reputation in the time and held the office of Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was killed with Yong at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Tai, styled Chang, had some reputation in the time and served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was killed with Yong at the same time.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉公、高陽王，諡曰文。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Commandant and Prince of Gaoyang; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Commandant and Prince of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子斌襲。

translations.literal: His son Bin inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin inherited.

sentences.zh: 斌字善集，歷位侍中、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Bin, styled Shanji, held in succession Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Bin, styled Shanji, served in turn as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 斌美儀貌，性寬和，居官重慎，頗為齊文襄愛賞。

translations.literal: Bin had handsome bearing and a mild nature; in office he was very cautious and was quite favored by Qi Emperor Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was handsome and mild; in office he was very cautious and was quite favored by Qi Emperor Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，准例降爵為高陽縣公，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was reduced to Duke of Gaoyang county and he was made Grand Master for the Palace with Glory Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao, by precedent his rank was reduced to Duke of Gaoyang county and he was made Grand Master for the Palace with Glory Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 二年，從文宣討契丹還，至白狼河，以罪賜死。

translations.literal: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Wenxuan, at the White Wolf River he was sentenced to death for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, returning from campaigning against the Khitan with Emperor Wenxuan, at the White Wolf River he was sentenced to death for a crime.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰字彥和，少而歧嶷，姿性不群。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, styled Yanhe, from youth was precocious; in disposition he was unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie, styled Yanhe, was precocious from youth and unlike others in disposition.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，封始平王，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed Prince of Shiping and made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 勰生而母潘氏卒，其年獻文崩。

translations.literal: Xie was born and his mother Lady Pan died; that year Xianwen died.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was born and his mother Lady Pan died; that year Emperor Xianwen died.

sentences.zh: 及有所知，啟求追服，文明太后不許。

translations.literal: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning; Empress Dowager Wenming did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to understanding he petitioned to observe mourning for her; Empress Dowager Wenming did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 乃毀容憔悴，心喪三年，不參吉慶。

translations.literal: He therefore ruined his appearance in grief, observed heart-mourning three years, and did not take part in auspicious celebrations.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wasted his appearance in grief, observed heart-mourning for three years, and took no part in auspicious celebrations.

sentences.zh: 孝文大奇之。

translations.literal: Xiaowen marveled greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen marveled greatly.

sentences.zh: 敏而耽學，雅好屬文。

translations.literal: Quick and devoted to learning, he elegantly loved composing literature.
translations.idiomatic: Quick and devoted to learning, he elegantly loved composing literature.

sentences.zh: 長直禁內，參決軍國大政，萬機之事無不預焉。

translations.literal: On long duty inside the forbidden quarters he took part in deciding great military and civil affairs; of the myriad tasks none did not involve him.
translations.idiomatic: On long duty inside the forbidden quarters he took part in deciding great military and civil affairs; none of the myriad tasks passed without him.

sentences.zh: 及車駕南伐，領宗子軍，宿衛左右。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage campaigned south he took charge of the imperial clan army and guarded close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign he took charge of the imperial clan army and guarded close at hand.

sentences.zh: 轉中書令，侍中如故，改封彭城王。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before, and changed to Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before, and changed to Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 帝升金墉城，顧見堂後桐竹，曰：「凰皇非梧桐不棲，非竹實不食。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the Jincheng ramparts, looked back and saw behind the hall paulownia and bamboo, and said: "The phoenix will not perch except on the paulownia, will not eat except bamboo fruit.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the Jincheng ramparts, looked back, and saw paulownia and bamboo behind the hall. He said, "The phoenix will not perch except on paulownia and will not eat except bamboo fruit.

sentences.zh: 今梧竹並茂，詎能降凰乎？

translations.literal: Now paulownia and bamboo are both lush—can the phoenix descend?
translations.idiomatic: Now paulownia and bamboo are both lush—can the phoenix descend?

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：「凰皇應德而來，豈桐竹能降？

translations.literal: " Xie said: "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how can paulownia and bamboo make it descend?
translations.idiomatic: " Xie said, "The phoenix comes in response to virtue—how can paulownia and bamboo make it descend?

sentences.zh: 」帝笑曰：「朕亦未望降之。

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed and said: "I also did not expect it to descend."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed and said, "I also did not expect it to descend."

sentences.zh: 」後宴侍臣於清徽堂。

translations.literal: Later he feasted the attending ministers at the Clear Splendor Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later he feasted the attending ministers at the Clear Splendor Hall.

sentences.zh: 日晏，移于流化池芳林下。

translations.literal: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant trees at the Transforming Flow Pool.
translations.idiomatic: The day grew late; they moved to beneath the fragrant trees at the Transforming Flow Pool.

sentences.zh: 帝仰觀桐葉之茂，曰：「'其桐其椅，其實離離。

translations.literal: The emperor looked up at the paulownia leaves lush and said: "'Its paulownia, its chair-tree, its fruit hangs thick.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked up at the lush paulownia leaves and said, "'Its paulownia, its chair-tree, its fruit hangs thick.

sentences.zh: 愷悌君子，莫不令儀。

translations.literal: The gracious gentleman—none is not admirable.'
translations.idiomatic: The gracious gentleman—none is not admirable.'

sentences.zh: '今林下諸賢，足敷歌詠。

translations.literal: Now the worthies beneath the trees are enough to fill song and praise."
translations.idiomatic: Now the worthies beneath the trees are enough to fill song and praise."

sentences.zh: 」遂令黃門侍郎崔光讀暮春群臣應制詩。

translations.literal: He then ordered Secretariat Attendant Cui Guang to read the ministers' responsive poems for late spring.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Secretariat Attendant Cui Guang to read the ministers' responsive poems for late spring.

sentences.zh: 至勰詩，帝乃為改一字，曰：「昔祁奚舉子，天下謂之至公。

translations.literal: When they came to Xie's poem the emperor altered one character and said: "In the past Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to Xie's poem the emperor altered one character and said, "In the past Qi Xi recommended his son and the realm called it utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 今見勰詩，始知中令之舉非私也。

translations.literal: Now seeing Xie's poem I know the Director's recommendation was not private."
translations.idiomatic: Now seeing Xie's poem I know the director's recommendation was not private."

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：「臣露此拙，方見聖朝之私，賴蒙神筆賜刊，得有令譽。

translations.literal: Xie said: "Your servant shows this clumsy piece and thereby sees the holy court's favor; relying on the divine brush's correction I have worthy reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "Your servant shows this clumsy piece and thereby sees the holy court's favor; relying on the divine brush's correction I have worthy reputation."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「雖琱琢一字，猶是玉之本體。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Though one character is carved and polished, it is still the jade's original substance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Though one character is carved and polished, it is still the jade's original substance."

sentences.zh: 」勰曰：'《詩》三百，一言可蔽。

translations.literal: Xie said: 'The three hundred pieces of the Odes—a single phrase can cover them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "The three hundred pieces of the Odes—a single phrase can cover them.

sentences.zh: 今陛下賜刊一字，足以價等連城。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty bestows the correction of one character—it is enough to equal a linked city in value."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty bestows the correction of one character—it is enough to equal a city in value."

sentences.zh: 」勰表解侍中，詔曰：「蟬貂之美，待汝而光。

translations.literal: Xie memorialized to resign Attendant-in-Ordinary; the edict said: "The beauty of the cicada-fur cap awaits you to shine.
translations.idiomatic: Xie memorialized to resign Attendant-in-Ordinary; the edict said, "The beauty of the cicada-fur cap awaits you to shine.

sentences.zh: 人乏之秋，何容方退。

translations.literal: In a season when men are scarce, how can you withdraw now?
translations.idiomatic: In a season when men are scarce, how can you withdraw now?

sentences.zh: 」後從幸代都，次於上黨之銅鞮山，路傍有大松樹十數根。

translations.literal: " Later he followed the emperor to the northern capital; they halted at the Tongdi Mountains in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he followed the emperor to the northern capital; they halted at the Tongdi Mountains in Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 時帝進傘，遂住而賦詩，令示勰曰：「吾作詩雖不七步，亦不言遠。

translations.literal: Beside the road were more than ten great pine trees; at the time the emperor advanced his parasol, stopped, and composed a poem, ordering it shown to Xie: "My composing, though not in seven paces, is not said to be far.
translations.idiomatic: Beside the road stood more than ten great pines; the emperor advanced his parasol, stopped, and composed a poem, ordering it shown to Xie: "My composing, though not in seven paces, is not said to be far.

sentences.zh: 汝可作之，比至吾間，令就也。

translations.literal: You may compose one; by the time you reach my side, finish it.
translations.idiomatic: You may compose one; by the time you reach my side, finish it.

sentences.zh: 」時勰去帝十步，遂且行且作，未至帝所而就。

translations.literal: " At the time Xie was ten paces from the emperor; he then walked and composed, and before reaching the emperor's place he finished.
translations.idiomatic: " Xie was ten paces from the emperor; he walked and composed, and before reaching the emperor's place he finished.

sentences.zh: 詩曰：「問松林，松林經幾冬？

translations.literal: The poem said: "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has the pine grove known?
translations.idiomatic: The poem said, "I ask the pine grove—how many winters has the pine grove known?

sentences.zh: 山川何如昔？

translations.literal: How are mountains and rivers compared to the past?
translations.idiomatic: How are mountains and rivers compared to the past?

sentences.zh: 風雲與古同？

translations.literal: Wind and clouds the same as of old?
translations.idiomatic: Wind and clouds the same as of old?

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑曰：「汝此亦調責吾耳！

translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly and said: "Your piece also teases me!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed greatly and said, "Your piece also teases me!

sentences.zh: 」詔贈勰所生母潘氏為彭城國太妃。

translations.literal: " An edict enfeoffed Xie's birth mother Lady Pan as Grand Consort of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict enfeoffed Xie's birth mother Lady Pan as Grand Consort of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 又除中書監，侍中如故。

translations.literal: He was again made Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.

sentences.zh: 帝南討漢陽，假勰中軍大將軍，加鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When the emperor campaigned south against Hanyang he made Xie acting Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army and gave him one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor campaigned south against Hanyang he made Xie acting Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army and gave him one set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 勰以寵授頻煩，乃面陳曰：「臣聞兼親疏而兩，並異同而建。

translations.literal: Xie because favor and appointments came again and again faced the throne and said: "Your servant hears that both kin near and far together, and both different and same together established.
translations.idiomatic: Because favor and appointments came again and again Xie faced the throne and said, "Your servant hears that both kin near and far together, and both different and same together established.

sentences.zh: 此既成文於昔，臣願誦之於後。

translations.literal: This is already written in the past; your servant wishes to recite it for the future.
translations.idiomatic: This is already written in the past; your servant wishes to recite it for the future.

sentences.zh: 陳思求而不允，愚臣不請而得。

translations.literal: Chen Si sought and was not granted; the foolish subject did not ask and obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Si sought and was not granted; the foolish subject did not ask and obtained.

sentences.zh: 豈但今古雲殊，遇否大異。

translations.literal: Not only do past and present differ like clouds; meeting fortune or misfortune differs greatly."
translations.idiomatic: Not only do past and present differ like clouds—meeting fortune or misfortune differs greatly."

sentences.zh: 」帝大笑，執勰手曰：「二曹才名相忌，吾與汝以道德相親，緣此而言，無慚前烈。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed greatly, took Xie's hand and said: "The two Caos' talent and names were jealous of each other; I and you are kin by virtue—speaking from this, I have no shame before the former worthies."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed greatly, took Xie's hand, and said, "The two Caos' talent and names were jealous of each other; you and I are kin by virtue—from this I have no shame before the former worthies."

sentences.zh: 帝親講《喪服》於清徽堂，從容謂群臣曰：「彥和、季豫等年在沖蒙，早登纓紱，失過庭之訓，並未習《禮》。

translations.literal: Each wished to have me explain Mourning Garments once.
translations.idiomatic: Each wished to have me explain Mourning Garments once.

sentences.zh: 每欲令我一解《喪服》。

translations.literal: I myself examined my understanding as shallow and floated, looked up and did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: I myself found my understanding shallow and looked up and did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 自審義解浮疏，仰而不許。

translations.literal: Recently because of sitting drunk with wine I spoke and followed—therefore I bent the court's worthies and personally lectured.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, sitting drunk with wine, I spoke and followed—therefore I bent the court's worthies and lectured in person.

sentences.zh: 頃因酒醉坐，脫爾言從，故屈朝彥，遂親傅說。

translations.literal: " Censor-in-Chief Li Biao replied: "From antiquity to the present there has never been a Son of Heaven lecturing on Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: " Censor-in-Chief Li Biao replied, "From antiquity to the present there has never been a Son of Heaven lecturing on Ritual.

sentences.zh: 」御史中尉李彪對曰：「自古及今，未有天子講《禮》。

translations.literal: Your servant received the tone and intent in person—a thousand years at one time."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant received the tone and intent in person—a moment once in a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 臣得親承音旨，千載一時。」

translations.literal: Following the campaign north of the Mian he was made Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Southern Campaign Military Affairs, Regular Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army, and Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Following the campaign north of the Mian he was made Bearer of Credentials, Supervisor of Southern Campaign Military Affairs, Regular Commander-in-Chief of the Central Army, and Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 從征沔北，除使持節、都督南征諸軍事，正中軍大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Xie thereupon personally led the great host.
translations.idiomatic: Xie thereupon personally led the great host.

sentences.zh: 勰於是親勒大眾。

translations.literal: In a moment two great birds came from the south—one toward the traveling palace, one toward the headquarters—each was caught by men.
translations.idiomatic: In a moment two great birds came from the south—one toward the traveling palace, one toward headquarters—each was caught.

sentences.zh: 須臾有二大鳥從南來，一向行宮，一向幕府，各為人所獲。

translations.literal: Xie said to the emperor: "At first one bird, seeing the banners, fell prostrate—I call it great good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said to the emperor, "At first one bird, seeing the banners, fell prostrate—I call it great good fortune."

sentences.zh: 勰言於帝曰：「始有一鳥，望旗顛仆，臣謂大吉。

sentences.zh: 齊將陳伯之屯于肥口，胡松又據梁城。

translations.literal: Qi general Chen Bozhi camped at Feikou; Hu Song also held Liangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi general Chen Bozhi held Feikou; Hu Song held Liangcheng.

sentences.zh: 勰部分將士，頻戰破之。

translations.literal: Xie disposed his officers and soldiers; in repeated battles he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Xie arrayed his commanders and broke them battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 淮南平，征勰還朝。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, Xie was summoned back to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, the court recalled him.

sentences.zh: 初，勰之定壽春，獲齊汝陰太守王果、豫州中從事庾稷等數人。

translations.literal: At first, when Xie secured Shouyang, he captured several men including Qi Governor of Ruyin Wang Guo and Attendant of Yuzhou Yu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: When he first took Shouyang he had captured Qi officials among them Wang Guo, governor of Ruyin, and Yu Ji, attendant of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 勰傾衿禮之，常參坐席。

translations.literal: Xie treated them with open courtesy and often had them at his table.
translations.idiomatic: Xie received them with open courtesy and kept them at his table.

sentences.zh: 果承間求還江外，勰衿而許之。

translations.literal: Guo seized an opening to ask return beyond the river; Xie with sympathy granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo found a moment to ask leave to return south of the Yangtze; Xie granted it from sympathy.

sentences.zh: 果又謝曰：「果等今還，仰負慈澤，請聽仁駕振旅，反跡江外。

translations.literal: Guo again thanked him, saying: "We who return now bear your gracious favor on our backs; please allow your benevolent host to shake the army and turn our tracks beyond the river."
translations.idiomatic: Guo thanked him again: "We who go home now carry your grace on our backs. Grant your noble host leave to march and turn our footsteps back across the river."

sentences.zh: 」至此乃還。

translations.literal: Only then did they return.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did they depart.

sentences.zh: 其為遠人所懷如此。

translations.literal: Such was how the distant held him in regard.
translations.idiomatic: So deep was the regard he won from men far away.

sentences.zh: 勰至京師，頻表辭大司馬、領司徒及所增邑，乞還中山，有詔不許。

translations.literal: When Xie reached the capital he repeatedly memorialized to resign as Grand Marshal and Minister of Works and the added fiefs, begging return to Zhongshan; an edict would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, he repeatedly asked to lay down grand marshal, minister of works, and the added fiefs and retire to Zhongshan; the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 乃除錄尚書，侍中、司徒如故，固辭不免。

translations.literal: He was made Director of the Secretariat; Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of Works as before; he firmly refused but could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: They made him director of the secretariat while keeping his other posts; he refused until he could refuse no more.

sentences.zh: 時咸陽王禧以驕矜，頗有不法，北海王詳陰言於帝；

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Xianyang Xi was arrogant and had many unlawful acts; Prince of Beihai Xiang spoke of it privately to the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xianyang Xi had grown proud and lawless; Prince of Beihai Xiang whispered as much to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 又言勰大得人情，不宜久在宰輔，勸帝遵遺敕。

translations.literal: He also said Xie had won great popular favor and ought not long remain at the head of government, urging the emperor to follow the late charge.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Xie had won the people's hearts and should not long head the government, urging the emperor to honor his father's last wish.

sentences.zh: 禧等又出領軍於烈為恆州，烈深以為忿。

translations.literal: Xi and the others also sent out Commander of the Palace Guard Yu Lie as Governor of Hengzhou; Lie was deeply resentful.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and his party also posted Commander of the Palace Guard Yu Lie to Hengzhou, and Lie burned with resentment.

sentences.zh: 烈子忠常在左右，密令忠言於帝，宜早自覽政。

translations.literal: Lie's son Zhong was constantly at the emperor's side; he secretly had Zhong speak to the emperor that he ought early to take government into his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: Lie's son Zhong was always at the emperor's ear; Lie secretly had him urge the young ruler to take the reins himself.

sentences.zh: 時將礿祭，王公並齋于廟東坊。

translations.literal: When the time came for the suburban sacrifice, princes and nobles all fasted in the east wing of the temple.
translations.idiomatic: When the season came for the suburban sacrifice, princes and nobles fasted together in the temple's east wing.

sentences.zh: 帝遣于烈將壯士六十人召禧、勰、詳等引見。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yu Lie with sixty stalwart guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yu Lie with sixty picked guards to summon Xi, Xie, Xiang, and the rest to audience.

sentences.zh: 帝謂勰曰：「頃來南北務殷，不容仰遂沖操。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Xie: "Of late north and south affairs have been pressing; I could not honor your lofty withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: He told Xie, "North and south have both been on fire; I could not grant the lofty retreat you sought.

sentences.zh: 恪是何人，而敢久違先敕？

translations.literal: What sort of man is Ke that he dared long defy the former charge?
translations.idiomatic: What is Ke, that he dared so long to defy my father's command?

sentences.zh: 今遂叔父高蹈之意。

translations.literal: Now I grant my uncle's wish to walk apart from power."
translations.idiomatic: Now I grant my uncle the high road he has long desired."

sentences.zh: 」詔乃為勰造宅，務從簡素，以遂其心。

translations.literal: An edict then built a residence for Xie, kept deliberately plain, to satisfy his heart.
translations.idiomatic: An edict built him a house deliberately plain, to satisfy his heart.

sentences.zh: 勰因是作《蠅賦》以喻懷。

translations.literal: Xie thereupon wrote "Rhapsody on the Fly" to voice his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Xie answered with a "Rhapsody on the Fly" to voice what he felt.

sentences.zh: 又以勰為太師，勰遂固辭。

translations.literal: He was again made Grand Preceptor; Xie firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: They named him grand preceptor; he refused again.

sentences.zh: 詔侍中敦喻，帝又為書於勰，崇家人之敬，勰不得已而應命。

translations.literal: An edict had the attendant-in-ordinary urge him earnestly; the emperor again wrote Xie a letter of familial respect; Xie could not refuse and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The attendant-in-ordinary was sent to press him; the emperor wrote again with familial deference; at last Xie yielded.

sentences.zh: 帝前後頻幸勰第。

translations.literal: Before and after, the emperor repeatedly visited Xie's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again the emperor came to his gate.

sentences.zh: 及京兆、廣平王暴虐不法，制宿衛隊主率羽林、武賁幽守諸王於其第，勰上表切諫，帝不納。

translations.literal: When the princes of Jingzhao and Guangping were violent and lawless, an order had squad leaders of the palace guard lead armored guards to confine the princes in their residences; Xie memorialized in sharp remonstrance; the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Jingzhao and Guangping turned brutal and lawless, the throne ordered squad leaders of the guard to pen them in their houses with armored men. Xie remonstrated in the sharpest terms; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 時議定律令，勰與高陽王雍、八坐、朝士有才學者，五日一集，參論軌制應否之宜。

translations.literal: At the time they were deliberating law codes; Xie with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, the eight ministers, and court scholars of talent met every five days to discuss whether the statutes should stand or fall.
translations.idiomatic: While the realm debated new law codes, Xie met every five days with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, the eight ministers, and the ablest scholars to weigh what should stand or fall.

sentences.zh: 凡所裁決，時彥歸仰。

translations.literal: Whatever they decided, men of the age looked up to them.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever they decided, the age looked up to them.

sentences.zh: 又加侍中。

translations.literal: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 勰敦尚文史，撰自古帝王賢達至於魏世子孫，族從為三十卷，名曰《要略》。

translations.literal: Xie honored letters and history; he compiled from ancient emperors and worthies down to Wei imperial sons and clansmen thirty scrolls titled Essentials in Brief.
translations.idiomatic: Xie loved letters and history and compiled thirty scrolls, from ancient emperors and sages down to Wei princes and kin, titled Essentials in Brief.

sentences.zh: 性仁孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was benevolent and filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was benevolent and filial.

sentences.zh: 言于朝廷，以其舅潘僧固為長樂太守。

translations.literal: Speaking at court, he had his maternal uncle Pan Senggu made Governor of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: At court he secured his maternal uncle Pan Senggu the governorship of Changle.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉構逆，僧固見逼。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu plotted rebellion, Senggu was forced along.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rose in rebellion, Senggu was dragged into it.

sentences.zh: 尚書令高肇性既凶愎，又肇兄女入為夫人。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Gao Zhao was by nature fierce and obstinate; moreover Zhao's elder brother's daughter had entered as consort.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Gao Zhao was fierce and obstinate by nature, and his elder brother's daughter had lately entered the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 順皇后崩，帝欲以為後，勰固執以為不可。

translations.literal: When Empress Shun died the emperor wished to make her empress; Xie firmly held it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Shun died the emperor wished to raise her to empress; Xie held the move impossible and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 肇於是屢譖勰，因僧固之同愉逆，肇誣勰與愉通，南招蠻賊。

translations.literal: Zhao then slandered Xie again and again; through Senggu's tie to Yu's rebellion Zhao accused Xie of communicating with Yu and summoning southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao slandered him without cease, and through Senggu's link to Yu's plot accused Xie of conspiring with Yu and calling southern rebels.

sentences.zh: 勰國郎中令魏偃、前防閣高祖珍希肇提攜，構成事。

translations.literal: Xie's Bureau Director Wei Yan and former gate officer Gao Zuzhen hoped for Zhao's patronage and fabricated the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's bureau director Wei Yan and former gate officer Gao Zuzhen, hungry for Zhao's favor, fabricated the case.

sentences.zh: 肇初令侍中元暉以奏，暉不從。

translations.literal: At first Zhao had Attendant-in-Ordinary Yuan Hui present the memorial; Hui would not.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao first ordered Attendant-in-ordinary Yuan Hui to present the accusation; Hui refused.

sentences.zh: 又令左衛元珍言之。

translations.literal: He then had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Left Guard Yuan Zhen speak of it.

sentences.zh: 帝訪暉，明勰無此。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Hui; Hui made clear Xie had done none of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Hui, who made clear that Xie had done none of this.

sentences.zh: 帝更以問肇，肇以魏偃、祖珍為證，乃信之。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Zhao again; Zhao took Wei Yan and Zuzhen as proof, and then believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Zhao again; Zhao produced Wei Yan and Zuzhen as witnesses, and the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 永平元年九月，召勰及高陽王雍、廣陽王嘉、清河王懌、廣平王懷及高肇等人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Yongping, Xie was summoned with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Prince of Guangyang Jia, Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Guangping Huai, and Gao Zhao and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongping 1, Xie was summoned with Prince of Gaoyang Yong, Prince of Guangyang Jia, Prince of Qinghe Yi, Prince of Guangping Huai, Gao Zhao, and others.

sentences.zh: 時勰妃方產，固辭不得已，意甚憂懼，與妃訣而登車。

translations.literal: At the time Xie's consort was in childbirth; he firmly refused but could not; his mind was full of dread; he took leave of his consort and mounted the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was in labor; he tried to refuse and could not, sick with dread. He took leave of her and climbed into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 入東掖門，度一小橋，牛傷，人挽而入。

translations.literal: Entering the east side gate, crossing a small bridge, the ox was hurt; men pulled and entered.
translations.idiomatic: At the east side gate, crossing a little bridge, the ox was injured; men hauled the carriage through.

sentences.zh: 宴於禁中，夜皆醉，各就別所消息。

translations.literal: They feasted in the forbidden precinct; at night all were drunk; each went to a separate place to rest.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted inside the palace until all were drunk, then each went to a separate room to sleep.

sentences.zh: 俄而元珍將武士齎毒酒至。

translations.literal: Soon Yuan Zhen came with guards bearing poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yuan Zhen came with guards bearing poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 勰曰：「一見至尊，死無恨也。

translations.literal: Xie said: "Once I see the August One, I die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Xie said, "Let me see the Son of Heaven once more and I die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」珍曰：「至尊何可復見！

translations.literal: Zhen said: "How can the August One be seen again!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "The Son of Heaven will not be seen again."

sentences.zh: 」武士以刀環築勰二下，勰大言稱冤。

translations.literal: Guards struck Xie twice with the ring of the blade; Xie cried out that he was wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Guards struck him twice with the flat of the blade; Xie cried that he was wronged.

sentences.zh: 武士又以刀築勰，乃飲毒酒，武士就殺之。

translations.literal: Guards again struck Xie with the blade; then he drank the poison; guards then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They struck him again, then he drank; the guards finished him.

sentences.zh: 向晨，以褥裹屍，輿從屏門出，載屍歸第，雲因飲而薨。

translations.literal: Toward dawn the corpse was wrapped in a quilt, carried out through the screen gate, and the body returned to his residence; it was said he had died from drink.
translations.idiomatic: Toward dawn they wrapped the corpse in quilts, carried it out through the screen gate, and sent it home, saying he had died from drink.

sentences.zh: 勰妃李氏，司空沖之女也，號哭曰：「高肇枉理殺人，天道有靈，汝還當惡死。

translations.literal: Xie's consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed: "Gao Zhao killed a man by perverting justice; Heaven has a spirit—you will yet die a vile death."
translations.idiomatic: His consort Lady Li, daughter of Minister of Works Chong, wailed, "Gao Zhao murdered him by twisting the law. Heaven has eyes—you will yet die foully."

sentences.zh: 」及肇以罪見殺，還於此屋，論者知有報應焉。

translations.literal: When Zhao was executed for crime he returned to this very house; commentators knew there was retribution.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao was executed for his crimes he was brought back to this very house; men said Heaven had answered her.

sentences.zh: 帝為舉哀於東堂。

translations.literal: The emperor held mourning for him in the eastern hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him in the eastern hall.

sentences.zh: 勰既有大功于國，無罪見害，行路士女皆流涕曰：「高肇小人，枉殺如此賢王！

translations.literal: Xie had great merit for the state yet was killed without crime; men and women on the road all wept and said: "Gao Zhao, that petty man, wrongly killed so worthy a prince!"
translations.idiomatic: Xie had served the state with great merit and died innocent; men and women in the streets wept and said, "That petty man Gao Zhao murdered a prince so worthy as this!"

sentences.zh: 」在朝貴戚莫不喪氣。

translations.literal: Nobles at court all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The great at court lost heart.

sentences.zh: 景明、報德寺僧鳴鐘欲飯，忽聞勰薨，二寺一千餘人皆嗟痛，為之不食，但飲水而齋。

translations.literal: At Jingming and Baode monasteries the monks were about to ring for the meal when they suddenly heard of Xie's death; more than a thousand in the two monasteries all sighed in pain, would not eat, and drank only water in fast.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jingming and Baode monasteries the monks were ringing for the midday meal when word came of Xie's death; more than a thousand monks in both houses groaned, would not eat, and drank only water in mourning.

sentences.zh: 追贈假黃鉞、使持節、都督中外諸軍事、司徒公、太師。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the golden axe, commissioner with credentials, commander of all armies within and without, Minister of Works, Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously they gave him the golden axe, credentials as commissioner, command of all armies at home and abroad, minister of works, and grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 給鑒輅九旒，武賁班劍百人，前後部羽葆鼓吹，轀輬車。

translations.literal: He was given the imperial canopy with nine tassels, a hundred guards with halberds and swords, feathered banners and drums before and behind, and the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: They granted the imperial canopy with nine tassels, a hundred guards with halberds and swords, feathered banners and drums before and behind, and the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 有司奏太常卿劉芳議勰諡，保大定功曰武，善問周達曰宣，宜諡武宣王。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple Liu Fang's discussion of Xie's posthumous name: preserving greatness and fixing merit is Wu, good inquiry and thorough penetration is Xuan; the posthumous name should be Prince Wu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry reported Director Liu Fang's judgment on his posthumous name: "Preserving greatness and fixing merit" yields Wu; "good inquiry and thorough penetration" yields Xuan. He should be Prince Wu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 及莊帝即位，追號文穆皇帝，妃李氏為文穆皇后，遷神主於太廟，稱肅祖。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Wen Mu; his consort Lady Li was Empress Wen Mu; the spirit tablet was moved to the ancestral temple and called Ancestor Su.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne he was posthumously titled Emperor Wen Mu and Lady Li Empress Wen Mu; his tablet entered the ancestral temple as Ancestor Su.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝時，去其神主。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Jiemin his spirit tablet was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin his spirit tablet was removed.

sentences.zh: 嫡子劭，字子訥，襲封。

translations.literal: His eldest son Shao, styled Zinuo, succeeded to the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Shao, styled Zinuo, succeeded to the fief.

sentences.zh: 劭善武藝，少有氣節。

translations.literal: Shao was skilled in martial arts and in youth had spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was skilled in arms and in youth had mettle.

sentences.zh: 明帝初，梁將寇邊，劭表上粟九千斛、資絹六百匹、國吏二百人以充軍用。

translations.literal: Early in Mingdi, when Liang generals raided the border, Shao memorialized nine thousand dan of grain, six hundred bolts of silk and goods, and two hundred household officials of the fief to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Mingdi, when Liang generals raided the border, Shao offered nine thousand dan of grain, six hundred bolts of silk and goods, and two hundred household officials of the fief for the army.

sentences.zh: 靈太后嘉其至意，不許。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling praised his utmost intent and would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling praised his devotion and would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 累遷青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，靈太后失德，四方紛擾，劭遂有異志。

translations.literal: Late in Xiaochang, when Empress Dowager Ling lost virtue and the four quarters were in turmoil, Shao then harbored a different intent.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Xiaochang, when the empress dowager lost her virtue and the realm boiled, Shao nursed designs of his own.

sentences.zh: 為安豐王延明所啟，征入為御史中尉。

translations.literal: Prince of Anfeng Yanming reported him; he was summoned in as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Anfeng Yanming denounced him; he was summoned in as imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 莊帝即位，尊為無上王。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang ascended the throne, Shao was honored as Prince Without Superior.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Shao was honored as Prince Without Superior.

sentences.zh: 尋遇害河陰。

translations.literal: Soon he met disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he met disaster at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 追諡曰孝宣皇帝，妻李氏為文恭皇后。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Xiao Xuan; his wife Lady Li was Empress Wen Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was titled Emperor Xiao Xuan; his wife Lady Li was Empress Wen Gong.

sentences.zh: 子韶，字世胄，好學，美容儀。

translations.literal: His son Shao, styled Shizhou, loved learning and had a handsome bearing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shao, styled Shizhou, loved learning and was handsome of bearing.

sentences.zh: 初，爾硃榮將入洛，父劭恐，以韶寄所親榮陽太守鄭仲明。

translations.literal: At first, when Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, his father Shao in fear placed Shao with his trusted friend Governor of Rongyang Zheng Zhongming.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong was about to enter Luoyang, his father Shao in fear placed the boy with his trusted friend Zheng Zhongming, governor of Rongyang.

sentences.zh: 仲明尋為城人所殺。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongming was killed by men of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhongming was killed by men of the city.

sentences.zh: 韶因亂，與乳母相失，遂與仲明兄子僧副避難。

translations.literal: Shao in the turmoil lost his wet nurse and with Zhongming's nephew Sengfu fled for refuge.
translations.idiomatic: In the turmoil Shao lost his wet nurse and fled with Zhongming's nephew Sengfu.

sentences.zh: 路中為賊逼，僧副恐不免，因令韶下馬。

translations.literal: On the road they were pressed by bandits; Sengfu feared they could not escape and had Shao dismount.
translations.idiomatic: On the road bandits closed in; Sengfu feared they could not escape and made Shao dismount.

sentences.zh: 僧副謂客曰：「窮鳥投人，尚或矜湣，況諸王如何棄乎？

translations.literal: Sengfu said to the travelers: "A bird at the end of flight still finds pity when it casts itself on man—how can you abandon a prince of the blood?"
translations.idiomatic: Sengfu told the travelers, "A bird at the end of its flight still wins pity when it casts itself on a man—how can you abandon a prince of the blood?"
