sentences.zh: 」僧副舉刃逼之，客乃退。

translations.literal: Sengfu raised the blade to press them; the travelers then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Sengfu raised his blade and pressed them; they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 韶逢一老母姓程，哀之，隱於私家。

translations.literal: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng who pitied him and hid him in a private house.
translations.idiomatic: Shao met an old woman surnamed Cheng who pitied him and hid him in her house.

sentences.zh: 居十餘日，莊帝訪而獲焉，襲封彭城王。

translations.literal: After more than ten days Emperor Zhuang found him by inquiry; he succeeded to Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days Emperor Zhuang found him by inquiry; he succeeded as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 齊神武后以孝武帝后配之，魏室奇寶多隨後入韶家。

translations.literal: After Qi Shenwu made Emperor Xiaowu's consort his wife, many of Wei's rare treasures followed her into Shao's house.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi Shenwu gave him Emperor Xiaowu's consort as wife, many of Wei's rare treasures followed her into Shao's house.

sentences.zh: 有二玉缽相盛，轉而不可出。

translations.literal: There were two jade bowls nested so they could turn but not be separated.
translations.idiomatic: There were two nested jade bowls that could turn but never be pulled apart.

sentences.zh: 馬腦榼容三升，玉縫之。

translations.literal: An agate case held three sheng, seamed in jade.
translations.idiomatic: An agate case held three sheng, its seams traced in jade.

sentences.zh: 皆稱西域鬼作也。

translations.literal: All were said to be the work of Western Region demons.
translations.idiomatic: Men said they were the work of demons from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 歷位太尉、侍中、錄尚書事、司州牧、特進、太傅。

translations.literal: He held posts as Grand Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat, Governor of Sizhou, Special Grandee, and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand commandant, attendant-in-ordinary, director of the secretariat, governor of Sizhou, special grandee, and grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 十年，太史奏云：「今年當除舊佈新。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the imperial astronomers memorialized: "This year the old should be removed and the new spread."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the astronomers reported, "This year the old must be swept away and the new spread."

sentences.zh: 」文宣謂韶曰：「漢光武何故中興？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen Xuan said to Shao: "Why did Han Guangwu revive the dynasty?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen Xuan asked Shao, "Why did Han's Guangwu restore the dynasty?"

sentences.zh: 」韶曰：「為誅諸劉不盡。

translations.literal: Shao said: "Because he did not kill all the Liu to the last man."
translations.idiomatic: Shao said, "Because he did not kill every Liu to the last man."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃誅諸元以厭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed the various Yuan to appease it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he killed the Yuan to appease the omen.

sentences.zh: 遂以五月誅元世哲、景武等二十五家，餘十九家並禁止之。

translations.literal: Thereupon in the fifth month he executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; the remaining nineteen households were all placed under prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he executed Yuan Shizhe, Jingwu, and twenty-five other households; nineteen more households were placed under prohibition.

sentences.zh: 韶幽於京畿地牢，絕食，啖衣袖而死。

translations.literal: Shao was confined in the capital's dungeon, starved, and died eating his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was shut in the capital dungeon, starved, and died gnawing his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 及七月，大誅元氏，自昭成已下並無遺焉。

translations.literal: By the seventh month there was a great slaughter of the Yuan clan; from Zhaocheng down none were left.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month the Yuan were slaughtered wholesale; from Zhaocheng's line down, none were spared.

sentences.zh: 或父祖為王，或身常貴顯，或兄弟強壯，皆斬東市。

translations.literal: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had themselves long been eminent, some had strong brothers—all were beheaded at the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: Some had fathers or grandfathers who had been kings, some had long held high rank, some had strong brothers in their prime—all were beheaded at the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 其嬰兒投於空中，承之以槊。

translations.literal: Infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.
translations.idiomatic: Infants were tossed into the air and caught on spears.

sentences.zh: 前後死者凡七百二十一人，悉投屍漳水。

translations.literal: Before and after, seven hundred twenty-one died in all; all corpses were cast into the Zhang River.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred twenty-one died in all; every corpse was cast into the Zhang River.

sentences.zh: 剖魚者多得爪甲，都下為之久不食魚。

translations.literal: Those who cut open fish often found fingernails; for a long time the capital would not eat fish.
translations.idiomatic: Men who gutted fish often found fingernails; for a long season the capital would not touch fish.

sentences.zh: 世哲從弟黃頭，使與諸囚自金凰台各乘紙鴟以飛，黃頭獨能至紫陌乃墜，仍付御史獄，畢義雲餓殺之。

translations.literal: Shizhe's cousin Huangtou was made with other prisoners to ride paper kites from the Golden Phoenix Terrace and fly; Huangtou alone reached Zimo Lane before falling; he was handed to the censor's prison and Bi Yiyun starved him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhe's cousin Huangtou was set with other prisoners to ride paper kites from the Golden Phoenix Terrace; Huangtou alone reached Zimo Lane before he fell, was sent to the censor's prison, and Bi Yiyun starved him to death.

sentences.zh: 北海王詳字季豫，美姿容，善舉止。

translations.literal: Prince of Beihai Xiang, styled Jiyu, had a handsome countenance and graceful bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Beihai Xiang, styled Jiyu, was handsome of face and graceful in bearing.

sentences.zh: 太和九年封，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he was enfeoffed and made attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe 9 he was enfeoffed and made attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 孝文自洛北巡，詳常與侍中彭城王勰並在輿輦，陪侍左右。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen toured north from Luoyang, Xiang was often with Attendant-in-Ordinary Prince of Pengcheng Xie in the carriage, attending left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen toured north from Luoyang, Xiang often rode beside Prince of Pengcheng Xie in the imperial carriage, attending left and right.

sentences.zh: 至文成射銘所，帝停駕，詔諸弟及侍臣皆試射遠近。

translations.literal: At the place where Emperor Wencheng shot the inscription, the emperor halted the carriage and ordered the younger princes and attending ministers all to try shooting near and far.
translations.idiomatic: At the spot where Emperor Wencheng had shot his inscription, the emperor halted and ordered younger princes and attending ministers to try their skill at near and far targets.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆去一二十步，唯詳箭及之。

translations.literal: All others were twenty or thirty paces off; only Xiang's arrow reached it.
translations.idiomatic: Others stood twenty or thirty paces back; only Xiang's arrow reached the mark.

sentences.zh: 帝拊掌欣笑，遂詔勒銘，親自為制。

translations.literal: The emperor clapped his hands and laughed with delight; he then ordered the inscription cut and personally composed the text.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor clapped and laughed with delight, then ordered the inscription carved and wrote the text himself.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，詳行中領軍，留守。

translations.literal: When the carriage campaigned south, Xiang served as acting commander of the palace guard and remained to defend.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern campaign Xiang served as acting commander of the palace guard and remained behind to defend.

sentences.zh: 孝文臨崩，顧命詳為司空輔政。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen was near death he entrusted Xiang as Minister of Works to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: At his deathbed Xiaowen entrusted government to Xiang as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 宣武覽政，為中大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: When Xuandi took government, he was made Grand General and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuandi took the reins, Xiang was made grand general and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 咸陽王禧之謀反，詳表求解任，制不許。

translations.literal: When Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion, Xiang memorialized asking to resign his duties; the order would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Xianyang Xi plotted rebellion, Xiang asked to resign; the throne would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 除太尉、領司徒、侍中，錄尚書事如故。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Commandant, holding Minister of Works and Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Secretariat as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand commandant while retaining minister of works, attendant-in-ordinary, and director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 詳之拜命，其夜暴風震電，拔其廷中桐，樹大十圍，倒立本處。

translations.literal: The night Xiang received the appointment, a violent wind with thunder and lightning uprooted the paulownia in his court, a tree ten arm-spans around, which stood inverted in its place.
translations.idiomatic: The night he received the appointment a storm wind with thunder uprooted the paulownia in his court, ten arm-spans around, and left it standing upside down in its hole.

sentences.zh: 初，宣武之覽政，詳聞彭城王勰有震主之慮，而欲奪其司徒，大懼物議，故為大將軍，至是乃居之。

translations.literal: At first, when Xuandi took government, Xiang heard that Prince of Pengcheng Xie had the worry of overshadowing the ruler and wished to seize his post as Minister of Works; he greatly feared public opinion and therefore took Grand General; only now did he hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi first took power, Xiang had heard that Prince of Pengcheng Xie might overshadow the throne and had wanted his post as minister of works; fearing public talk, he took grand general instead—only now did he hold it.

sentences.zh: 天威如此，識者知其不終。

translations.literal: Heaven's authority was thus; those who knew saw he would not end well.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had spoken; those who understood knew he would not end well.

sentences.zh: 既以季父崇寵，位望兼極，貪冒無厭，公私營販。

translations.literal: Already favored as the emperor's younger uncle, his rank and repute at the summit, he was greedy without end and traded in public and private.
translations.idiomatic: Favored as the emperor's younger uncle, rank and repute at their height, he was greedy without end and trafficked in public and private gain.

sentences.zh: 又於東掖門外規占第宅，至有喪柩在室，請延至葬而不見許，輿櫬巷次，行路哀嗟。

translations.literal: He also staked out a residence outside the east side gate; there were even mourning coffins in the rooms; he asked to delay until the burial and was not granted it; the bier blocked the lane and passersby sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: He staked out a mansion outside the east side gate; mourning coffins still stood in the rooms. He begged delay until the burial and was refused; biers blocked the lane and passersby sighed.

sentences.zh: 詳母高太妃頗助威虐，怨<鄉向>嗷然。

translations.literal: Xiang's mother Grand Consort Gao greatly aided his violence; resentment in the neighborhood was loud.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Grand Consort Gao, fed his violence; the neighborhood seethed with complaint.

sentences.zh: 妃宋王劉昶女，不見答禮。

translations.literal: His consort was daughter of Song Prince Liu Chang; she was not answered with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: His consort was a daughter of Song Prince Liu Chang; he never treated her with the courtesy owed a wife.

sentences.zh: 寵妾范氏，愛等伉儷。

translations.literal: His favored concubine Lady Fan was loved as an equal partner.
translations.idiomatic: His favored concubine Lady Fan he loved as an equal partner.

sentences.zh: 及死葬訖，猶毀隧視之。

translations.literal: After her death and burial he still destroyed the tomb passage to look in.
translations.idiomatic: After her death and burial he still broke open the tomb passage to look upon her.

sentences.zh: 又烝于安定王燮妃高氏，即茹皓妻姊。

translations.literal: He also had illicit relations with the consort of Prince of Anding Xie, Lady Gao—elder sister of Ru Hao's wife.
translations.idiomatic: He also lay with the consort of Prince of Anding Xie, Lady Gao, elder sister to Ru Hao's wife.

sentences.zh: 詳既素附於皓，又緣淫好，往來綢密。

translations.literal: Xiang had long been attached to Hao; he also joined through licentious fondness, coming and going in close intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had long clung to Ru Hao and, through shared appetite for vice, came and went in close intimacy.

sentences.zh: 詳雖貪侈，宣武禮敬尚隆。

translations.literal: Though Xiang was greedy and extravagant, Xuandi's ritual respect was still lofty.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xiang was greedy and extravagant, the emperor's ritual respect still ran high.

sentences.zh: 常別住華林圓西隅，與都亭宮館相接。

translations.literal: He often lived separately in the western corner of the Hualin Park, adjoining the capital pavilion palaces.
translations.idiomatic: He often lived apart in the western corner of Hualin Park, adjoining the capital pavilion palaces.

sentences.zh: 帝每潛幸其所，肆飲終日，與高太妃相見，呼為阿母，伏而上酒，禮若家人。

translations.literal: The emperor often stole to his place, drinking all day, meeting Grand Consort Gao; he called her Foster Mother, crawled to offer wine, with ritual like family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often stole to his house and drank the day through, meeting Grand Consort Gao, calling her Foster Mother, crawling to offer wine with the ease of kin.

sentences.zh: 臨出，高每拜送，舉觴祝言：「願官家千萬年壽，歲一入妾母子舍也。

translations.literal: On leaving, Gao always bowed in send-off, raising the cup and praying: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years; once a year enter the house of me and my son."
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Gao always bowed him out, raising her cup: "May Your Majesty live ten thousand years and once a year enter the house of me and my son."

sentences.zh: 」初，宣武之親政，詳與咸陽王禧、彭城王勰並被召入，共乘犢車，防衛嚴固。

translations.literal: At first, when Xuandi took government in person, Xiang with Prince of Xianyang Xi and Prince of Pengcheng Xie were all summoned in, riding together in a calf cart under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuandi first took government in person, Xiang rode with Prince of Xianyang Xi and Prince of Pengcheng Xie in a calf cart under strict guard.

sentences.zh: 高時惶迫，以為必死，亦乘車傍路哭送至金墉。

translations.literal: Gao was then in panic, thinking they would surely die; she also rode by the roadside weeping and escorted them to Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was then in panic, sure they would die; she rode by the roadside weeping and followed them to Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 及詳得免，高云：「自今以後，不願富貴。

translations.literal: When Xiang was spared, Gao said: "From now on I do not wish wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang was spared, Gao said, "From now on I want no more wealth.

sentences.zh: 但令母子相保，共汝掃市作活也。

translations.literal: Only let mother and son preserve each other; with you we will sweep the market and live by labor."
translations.idiomatic: Only let mother and son keep each other; with you we will sweep the market and live by labor."

sentences.zh: 」至此，貴寵崇盛，不復言有禍敗之理。

translations.literal: By now favor and glory were lofty and grand; they no longer spoke of the logic of ruin.
translations.idiomatic: By then favor and glory had mounted too high for talk of ruin.

sentences.zh: 後為高肇所譖，雲詳與皓等謀逆。

translations.literal: Later he was slandered by Gao Zhao, who said Xiang with Hao and others plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Zhao slandered him, saying Xiang with Hao and others plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時詳在南第。

translations.literal: At the time Xiang was at the southern residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xiang was at the southern residence.

sentences.zh: 帝召中尉崔亮入禁，糾詳貪淫，及茹皓、劉胄、常季賢、陳掃靜等專恣之狀。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Imperial Censor Cui Liang into the forbidden precinct to investigate Xiang's greed and licentiousness, and the arbitrary acts of Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Imperial Censor Cui Liang into the palace to investigate Xiang's greed and lust, and the arrogance of Ru Hao, Liu Zhou, Chang Jixian, Chen Saojing, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 夜即收禁南台。

translations.literal: That night he was seized and confined at the southern terrace.
translations.idiomatic: That night he was seized and confined at the southern terrace.

sentences.zh: 又武賁百人，圍守詳第。

translations.literal: A hundred armored guards also surrounded and guarded Xiang's residence.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred armored guards also surrounded his residence.

sentences.zh: 夜中慮其驚懼奔越，遣左右郭翼開金墉門馳出喻之，示以中尉彈狀。

translations.literal: In the night, fearing he would panic and flee, he sent his attendant Guo Yi to open the Jincheng gate and gallop out to explain, showing the censor's impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing panic and flight in the night, the emperor sent his attendant Guo Yi to open the Jincheng gate and gallop out with the censor's impeachment.

sentences.zh: 詳母高見翼，頓首號泣，不能自勝。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Gao saw Yi and beat her head, wailing, unable to master herself.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort Gao saw Yi and beat her head, wailing beyond control.

sentences.zh: 詳言：「審如中尉所糾，何憂也？

translations.literal: Xiang said: "If it is truly as the censor impeaches, what is there to worry?
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "If it is truly as the censor charges, what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 人奉我珍異貨物，我實受之，果為取受，吾何憂乎？

translations.literal: Men presented me rare and precious goods; I truly received them; if that counts as taking bribes, why should I worry?"
translations.idiomatic: Men gave me rare treasures and I took them. If that is bribery, why should I worry?"

sentences.zh: 」至明，皓等皆賜死。

translations.literal: By daylight Hao and the rest were all granted death.
translations.idiomatic: By daylight Hao and the rest were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 引高陽王雍等五王入議詳罪。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaoyang Yong and five other princes were led in to deliberate Xiang's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Gaoyang Yong and five other princes were brought in to judge Xiang's crime.

sentences.zh: 單車防守還華林館。

translations.literal: He was guarded back to the Hualin residence in a single carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He was taken back to the Hualin residence in a single carriage under guard.

sentences.zh: 母妻相與哭，入所居，小奴弱婢數人隨從。

translations.literal: Mother and wife wept together and entered where he lived; a few young male slaves and weak maidservants followed.
translations.idiomatic: Mother and wife wept together and entered his rooms with a few young slaves and weak maids.

sentences.zh: 防援甚嚴。

translations.literal: The guard was very strict.
translations.idiomatic: The guard was very strict.

sentences.zh: 徙就太府寺，免為庶人。

translations.literal: He was moved to the Ministry of the Imperial Treasury and reduced to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the Ministry of the Imperial Treasury and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 別營坊館于洛陽縣東北隅，如法禁衛，限以終身，名曰思善堂，將徙詳居之。

translations.literal: A separate lodge was built in the northeast corner of Luoyang county by law's confinement, limited for life, named Hall of Recalling Goodness, and Xiang was to be moved there.
translations.idiomatic: A separate lodge was built in Luoyang's northeast corner, guarded for life, named Hall of Recalling Goodness, and Xiang was to be moved there.

sentences.zh: 會其家奴陰結党輩，欲劫出，密抄名字，潛托侍婢通於詳。

translations.literal: Then his household slaves secretly joined a faction, planning to seize him out; they secretly copied names and quietly entrusted a serving maid to pass word to Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Then his household slaves secretly banded to seize him out, copied names in secret, and had a serving maid pass word to Xiang.

sentences.zh: 詳始得執省，而門防主司遙見，突入，就詳手中覽得，呈奏。

translations.literal: Xiang had just taken it to examine when the gate guard's chief clerk saw from afar, burst in, took it from Xiang's hand, and presented it in memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had just taken the note to read when the gate guard's chief clerk saw from afar, burst in, snatched it from his hand, and memorialized the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝密令害之。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly ordered him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered him killed.

sentences.zh: 詳自至太府，令其母妻還居南宅，五日一來。

translations.literal: From the time Xiang reached the treasury he had his mother and wife return to the southern residence, coming once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he reached the treasury he sent mother and wife back to the southern residence, to visit once every five days.

sentences.zh: 此夜，母妻不來，死于奴婢手中。

translations.literal: That night mother and wife did not come; he died at the hands of slaves and maids.
translations.idiomatic: That night mother and wife did not come; he died at the hands of slaves and maids.

sentences.zh: 詔喪還南宅，諸王皇宗，悉令奔赴。

translations.literal: An edict returned the mourning to the southern residence; all princes of the imperial clan were ordered to hurry to attend.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent his body back to the southern residence; every prince of the blood was ordered to attend.

sentences.zh: 賵物一依廣陵故事。

translations.literal: Funeral goods all followed the Guangling precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral goods followed the Guangling precedent in all things.

sentences.zh: 詳之初禁，乃以淫高事告母。

translations.literal: When Xiang was first confined he told his mother of the affair with Gao.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang was first confined he told his mother of the affair with Lady Gao.

sentences.zh: 母大怒，詈之曰：「汝自有妻妾侍婢，少盛如花，何共高麗婢奸，令致此罪！

translations.literal: His mother was greatly angry and cursed him: "You have your own wives and serving maids, young and blooming as flowers—why lie with a Goryeo slave girl and bring this crime!
translations.idiomatic: His mother raged and cursed him: "You have wives and maids young as flowers—why lie with a Goryeo slave and bring this ruin upon us!

sentences.zh: 我得高麗婢，當啖其肉。

translations.literal: If I get that Goryeo slave I will eat her flesh."
translations.idiomatic: If I lay hands on that Goryeo girl I will eat her flesh."

sentences.zh: 」乃杖詳背及兩腳百餘下。

translations.literal: She then beat Xiang's back and both legs more than a hundred times.
translations.idiomatic: She beat his back and both legs more than a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 自行杖，力疲，乃使奴代。

translations.literal: She wielded the staff herself until strength failed; then she had a slave take her place.
translations.idiomatic: She wielded the staff herself until her strength failed, then had a slave take her place.

sentences.zh: 高氏素嚴，詳每有微罪，常加責罰，以絮裹杖。

translations.literal: Lady Gao was by nature severe; for Xiang's small faults she often added punishment, wrapping the staff in cotton.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao was severe by nature; for Xiang's small faults she often punished him, wrapping the staff in cotton.

sentences.zh: 至是，去絮，皆至創膿。

translations.literal: By now the cotton was removed; all reached festering sores.
translations.idiomatic: Now the cotton was stripped away; every blow brought festering sores.

sentences.zh: 又杖其妃劉數十，云：「新婦大家女，門戶匹敵，何所畏而不檢校夫婿！

translations.literal: She also beat his consort Liu dozens of times, saying: "New wife of a great house, families matched in standing—what did you fear that you did not check your husband!"
translations.idiomatic: She also beat his consort Liu dozens of times, crying, "New wife of a great house, families matched in standing—what did you fear that you never checked your husband!"

sentences.zh: 」劉笑而受罰，卒無所言。

translations.literal: Liu smiled and accepted the punishment; in the end she said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu smiled and took the blows; in the end she said nothing.

sentences.zh: 詳貪淫之失，雖聞遠近，而死之日，罪無定名，遠近歎怪之。

translations.literal: Though Xiang's greedy and licentious faults were heard far and near, on the day of his death his crimes had no fixed name; near and far sighed in wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Though his greed and lust were known far and wide, on the day he died his crimes had no fixed name; men near and far marveled.

sentences.zh: 永平元年十月，詔追復王爵，諡曰平王。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Yongping an edict restored his princely rank; posthumous name Prince Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongping 1 an edict restored his princely rank; posthumously he was Prince Ping.

sentences.zh: 子顥襲。

translations.literal: His son Hao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 顥字子明，少慷慨，有壯氣。

translations.literal: Hao, styled Ziming, in youth was generous and had bold spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, styled Ziming, was generous in youth and full of bold spirit.

sentences.zh: 為徐州刺史，尋為御史彈劾，除名。

translations.literal: He was Governor of Xuzhou; soon impeached by the censor and removed from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Xuzhou, then was impeached by the censor and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後賊帥宿勤明遠、叱幹騏驎等寇亂豳、華等州，乃復顥王爵，兼左僕射、西道行台以討明遠。

translations.literal: Later bandit chiefs Su Qinmingyuan and Chigan Qilin and others raided Bin and Hua and other prefectures; Hao's princely rank was restored and he was made Left Vice Minister and Western Route Commissioner to attack Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when bandit chiefs Su Qinmingyuan and Chigan Qilin raided Bin and Hua, his princely rank was restored and he was made left vice minister and western route commissioner to attack Mingyuan.

sentences.zh: 頻破賊，解豳、華之圍。

translations.literal: He repeatedly broke the bandits and relieved the sieges of Bin and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the bandits again and again and lifted the sieges of Bin and Hua.

sentences.zh: 後蕭寶夤等大敗於平涼，顥亦奔還京師。

translations.literal: Later Xiao Baoyin and others were greatly defeated at Pingliang; Hao also fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiao Baoyin and others were routed at Pingliang; Hao also fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 武泰初，為相州刺史，以禦葛榮。

translations.literal: Early in Wutai he was Governor of Xiangzhou to resist Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wutai he was governor of Xiangzhou to resist Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 屬爾硃榮入洛，推莊帝，授顥太傅。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and set up Emperor Zhuang, Hao was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang and set up Emperor Zhuang, Hao was made grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 顥以葛榮南侵，爾硃縱害，遂盤桓顧望，圖自安之策。

translations.literal: Hao, because Ge Rong invaded south and Erzhu committed outrage, then lingered and looked about, plotting a policy for his own safety.
translations.idiomatic: With Ge Rong pressing south and Erzhu committing outrage, Hao lingered and looked about, plotting how to save himself.

sentences.zh: 事不諧，遂與子冠受奔梁。

translations.literal: When affairs did not succeed he with his son Guanshou fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan failed he fled to Liang with his son Guanshou.

sentences.zh: 梁武以為魏主，假之兵將，令其北入。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang made him ruler of Wei and lent him troops and generals, ordering him north.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang made him ruler of Wei, lent him troops and generals, and ordered him north.

sentences.zh: 永安二年四月，于梁國城南登壇燔燎，年號孝基元年。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of Yong'an, south of Liang's capital he ascended the altar and burned the fire; era name Xiaoji year 1.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yong'an 2, south of the Liang capital, he ascended the altar and lit the sacred fire; his era was Xiaoji 1.

sentences.zh: 莊帝詔濟陰王暉業於考城拒之，為顥所禽。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang ordered Prince of Jiyin Huiye to resist him at Kaocheng; Huiye was captured by Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang ordered Prince of Jiyin Huiye to resist him at Kaocheng; Huiye was captured.

sentences.zh: 莊帝北幸，顥遂入洛，改稱建武元年。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang went north in favor; Hao then entered Luoyang and changed the era to Jianwu 1.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang went north in retreat; Hao entered Luoyang and proclaimed the era Jianwu 1.

sentences.zh: 顥以數千之眾，轉戰屢克，據有都邑，號令自己。

translations.literal: Hao with several thousand men, turning in battle repeatedly victorious, held the capital and issued orders himself.
translations.idiomatic: With a few thousand men Hao fought his way in, again and again victorious, seized the capital, and gave orders in his own name.

sentences.zh: 天下人情，想望風政。

translations.literal: Sentiment throughout the realm looked to his wind and government.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven looked to his wind and government.

sentences.zh: 自謂天之所授，頗懷驕怠。

translations.literal: He himself thought Heaven had granted it and grew quite proud and slack.
translations.idiomatic: He thought Heaven had granted the throne and grew proud and slack.

sentences.zh: 宿昔賓客近習之徒，咸見寵待，干擾政事。

translations.literal: Former guests and close attendants of long standing were all favored and interfered in government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Old guests and close attendants were all favored and meddled in government.

sentences.zh: 又日夜縱酒，不恤軍國。

translations.literal: He also drank day and night without caring for army or state.
translations.idiomatic: He drank day and night and cared nothing for army or state.

sentences.zh: 所統南兵，陵竊市里，朝野失望。

translations.literal: The southern troops under his command plundered the markets; court and countryside lost hope.
translations.idiomatic: The southern troops under his command plundered the markets; court and countryside lost hope.

sentences.zh: 時又酷儉，公私不安。

translations.literal: At the time he was also harsh in frugality; public and private were unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh in frugality as well; public and private life both frayed.

sentences.zh: 莊帝與爾硃榮還師討顥，顥自于河梁拒戰。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhuang with Erzhu Rong returned with troops to attack Hao; Hao himself resisted at Heqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang returned with Erzhu Rong to attack him; Hao met them at Heqiao.

sentences.zh: 冠受戰敗被禽。

translations.literal: Guanshou was defeated in battle and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Guanshou was defeated and captured.

sentences.zh: 顥自轘轅出至臨潁，為臨潁縣卒所斬。

translations.literal: Hao himself went out by Zhuanxu to Linying and was beheaded by a soldier of Linying county.
translations.idiomatic: Hao fled by Zhuanxu toward Linying and was beheaded by a soldier of Linying county.

sentences.zh: 初，顥入洛，其日暴風，欲入閶闔門，馬大驚不進，令人執轡乃入。

translations.literal: At first, when Hao entered Luoyang, that day there was a violent wind; he wished to enter the Changle gate; the horse was greatly startled and would not advance; men held the reins and only then entered.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered Luoyang that day a violent wind rose; at the Changle gate his horse panicked and would not advance until men seized the reins.

sentences.zh: 有恆農楊曇華告人曰：「顥必無成，假服袞冕，不過六十日。

translations.literal: There was Hengnong Yang Yanhua who told others: "Hao will surely not succeed; though he borrows imperial robes, it will not pass sixty days."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yanhua of Hengnong told others, "Hao will never succeed; though he borrows imperial robes, he will not pass sixty days."

sentences.zh: 」又諫議大夫元昭業曰：「昔更始自洛陽而西，初發，馬驚奔，觸北宮鐵柱，三馬皆死，而更始卒不成帝位。

translations.literal: Remonstrating Censor Yuan Zhaoye also said: "Formerly Gengshi from Luoyang went west; at the first setting out the horses startled and ran, striking the northern palace's iron pillar; three horses all died, and Gengshi in the end did not complete the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Yuan Zhaoye also said, "When Gengshi left Luoyang for the west, his horses bolted at the start and struck the northern palace's iron pillar; three horses died, and Gengshi never finished as emperor.

sentences.zh: 以古譬今，其兆一也。

translations.literal: Comparing ancient to present, the omen is one."
translations.idiomatic: The omen is the same."

sentences.zh: 」至七月果敗。

translations.literal: By the seventh month he indeed was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: By the seventh month he was indeed defeated.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，贈太師、大司馬。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaowu he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made grand preceptor and grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 顥弟頊，莊帝初，封東海王，位中書監。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Xuan, at the start of Emperor Zhuang, was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai and made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Xuan, at the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign, was enfeoffed Prince of Donghai and made director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 及顥入洛，成敗未分，便以意氣自得，為時人笑。

translations.literal: When Hao entered Luoyang and success or failure was not yet divided, he was self-satisfied from spirit; men of the time laughed.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao entered Luoyang and the outcome was still in doubt, Xuan swaggered with self-satisfaction; men of the time laughed.

sentences.zh: 顥敗，潛竄，為人執送，斬於都市。

translations.literal: When Hao was defeated he hid in secret flight; a man seized and delivered him; he was beheaded in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao fell he fled in hiding; a man seized him and delivered him; he was beheaded in the market.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Early in Xiaowu he was posthumously given Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 孝文七男：林廢後生廢太子恂；

translations.literal: Xiaowen's seven sons: after Deposed Empress Lin, Deposed Crown Prince Xun;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen had seven sons: by Deposed Empress Lin, Deposed Crown Prince Xun;

sentences.zh: 文昭皇后生宣武皇帝、廣平武穆王懷；

translations.literal: by Empress Wen Zhao, Emperor Xuandi and Prince of Guangping Wu Mu Huai;
translations.idiomatic: by Empress Wen Zhao, Emperor Xuandi and Prince of Guangping Wu Mu Huai;

sentences.zh: 袁貴人生京兆王愉；

translations.literal: by Lady Yuan, Prince of Jingzhao Yu;
translations.idiomatic: by Lady Yuan, Prince of Jingzhao Yu;

sentences.zh: 羅夫人生清河文獻王懌、汝南王悅；

translations.literal: by Lady Luo, Prince of Qinghe Wen Xian Yi and Prince of Runan Yue;
translations.idiomatic: by Lady Luo, Prince of Qinghe Wen Xian Yi and Prince of Runan Yue;

sentences.zh: 鄭充華生皇子恌，未封，早夭。

translations.literal: by Lady Zheng Chonghua, the prince Tiao, not enfeoffed, died early.
translations.idiomatic: by Lady Zheng Chonghua, the prince Tiao, who was never enfeoffed and died young.

sentences.zh: 廢太子庶人恂，字元道。

translations.literal: Deposed Crown Prince the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.
translations.idiomatic: Deposed Crown Prince, the commoner Xun, styled Yuandao.

sentences.zh: 生而母死，文明太后撫視之，常置左右。

translations.literal: At birth his mother died; Empress Dowager Wenming nursed and watched him, often keeping him at her side.
translations.idiomatic: His mother died at his birth; Empress Dowager Wenming nursed him and kept him always at her side.

sentences.zh: 年四歲，太后親為立名恂，字元道。

translations.literal: At four years the empress dowager personally established his name Xun, styled Yuandao.
translations.idiomatic: At four the empress dowager herself gave him the name Xun and the style Yuandao.

sentences.zh: 於是大赦。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the court proclaimed a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年七月癸丑，立恂為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, day guichou, of the seventeenth year of Taihe, Xun was established as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou of the seventh month, Taihe 17, Xun was established as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 及冠恂於廟，孝文臨光極東堂，引恂入見，誡以冠義曰：「字汝元道，所寄不輕，汝當尋名求義，以順吾旨。

translations.literal: At the capping in the temple, Xiaowen at the eastern hall of Guangji summoned Xun in to see him and admonished him on the capping rite, saying: "I style you Yuandao; what is entrusted is not light—you should seek the meaning in the name and follow my intent."
translations.idiomatic: At his capping in the temple Xiaowen received him at the eastern hall of Guangji and taught him the rite: "I style you Yuandao; what is entrusted is not light. Seek the meaning in the name and follow my intent."

sentences.zh: 」二十年，改字宣道。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year his style was changed to Xuandao.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year his style was changed to Xuandao.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，詔恂詣代都，其進止儀體，帝皆為定。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict sent Xun to the capital at Dai; his comings and goings, ritual and bearing, the emperor all fixed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, an edict sent Xun to the old capital at Dai; the emperor fixed every detail of his journey, ritual, and bearing.

sentences.zh: 及恂入辭，帝曰：「今汝不應向代。

translations.literal: When Xun entered to take leave, the emperor said: "Now you ought not go toward Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun came to take leave the emperor said, "You ought not go to Dai now.

sentences.zh: 但太師薨於恆壞，朕既居皇極之重，不容輕赴舅氏之喪，欲使汝展哀舅氏，拜汝母墓，一寫為子之情。

translations.literal: But the Grand Preceptor died at Heng; I already bear the heavy weight of the imperial apex and cannot lightly go to my maternal uncle's mourning; I wish you to show mourning for your uncle, bow at your mother's tomb, and write out once the feeling of a son.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor died at Heng. I bear the weight of the throne and cannot lightly attend my uncle's mourning. Go show mourning for your uncle, bow at your mother's tomb, and once write out a son's feeling.

sentences.zh: 山陵北海，汝至彼，太師事畢後日，宜一拜山陵。

translations.literal: At the northern hills and tombs, when you arrive there, after the Grand Preceptor's affairs are finished, on another day you should once bow at the hills and tombs.
translations.idiomatic: At the northern hills and tombs, when the Grand Preceptor's rites are finished, on another day bow once at the tombs.

sentences.zh: 拜訖，汝族祖南安可一就問訊。

translations.literal: When the bowing is done, your clan ancestor Prince of Nan'an may be visited once for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When that is done, you may once visit your clan ancestor Prince of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 在途當溫讀經籍，今日親見吾也。

translations.literal: On the road you should warmly read the classics; today you see me in person."
translations.idiomatic: On the road read the classics with care; today you see me face to face."

sentences.zh: 」後帝每歲征幸，恂常留守，主執廟祀。

translations.literal: Afterward each year when the emperor campaigned, Xun often remained to defend and presided over temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever the emperor campaigned, Xun often remained behind to guard the capital and preside over temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 恂不好書學，體貌肥大，深忌河、洛暑熱，意每追樂北方。

translations.literal: Xun did not love letters and learning; his body was large and fat; he deeply hated the heat of the Yellow and Luo rivers and in mind often yearned for the pleasures of the north.
translations.idiomatic: Xun did not love books; he was large and heavy of body; he hated the heat of the Luo valley and longed in his heart for the north.

sentences.zh: 中庶子高道悅數苦言致諫，恂甚銜之。

translations.literal: Junior mentor Gao Daoyue repeatedly spoke in bitter remonstrance; Xun deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Junior mentor Gao Daoyue remonstrated again and again; Xun deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 孝文幸崧嶽，恂留守金墉，謀欲召牧馬，輕騎奔代，手刃道悅於禁中。

translations.literal: When Xiaowen visited Song Mountain, Xun remained at Jincheng, plotting to summon the horse herds and with light cavalry flee to Dai, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowen visited Song Mountain, Xun remained at Jincheng, plotted to summon the horse herds and flee to Dai with light cavalry, and with his own hand killed Daoyue in the palace.

sentences.zh: 領軍元徽勒門防遏，夜得寧靜。

translations.literal: Commander of the Palace Guard Yuan Hui restrained the gate guards and held them back; by night all was quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Commander of the Palace Guard Yuan Hui held the gate guards back; by night all was quiet.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之駭惋，外寢其事，仍至汴口而還。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he was shocked and grieved; outwardly he concealed the affair and still went to Bian Ford and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was shocked and grieved when he heard, but outwardly concealed the affair and still went to Bian Ford and returned.

sentences.zh: 引恂數罪，與咸陽王禧等親杖恂。

translations.literal: He summoned Xun and counted his crimes; with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others he personally beat Xun with staves.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Xun, counted his crimes, and with Prince of Xianyang Xi and others personally beat him with staves.

sentences.zh: 又令禧等更代百餘下，扶曳出外，不起者月餘。

translations.literal: He also had Xi and the others take turns for more than a hundred blows; they dragged him out; for more than a month he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He had Xi and the others take turns for more than a hundred blows, then drag him out; for more than a month he could not rise.

sentences.zh: 拘於城西別館。

translations.literal: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He was confined in a separate lodge west of the city.

sentences.zh: 引見群臣於清徽堂，議廢之。

translations.literal: He summoned the ministers to audience at Qingwei Hall to deliberate deposing him.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the ministers to Qingwei Hall to deliberate deposing him.

sentences.zh: 司空、太子太傅穆亮，尚書僕射、少保李沖，並免冠稽首而謝。

translations.literal: Minister of Works and Crown Prince's Grand Tutor Mu Liang, Vice Minister of Works and Junior Guardian Li Chong, all removed caps and bowed to the ground in apology.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works and the crown prince's grand tutor Mu Liang, and Vice Minister of Works and junior guardian Li Chong, all removed their caps and bowed to the ground in apology.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「古人有言，大義滅親。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The ancients had a saying: great righteousness destroys kin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The ancients said that great righteousness destroys kin.

sentences.zh: 此小兒今日不滅，乃是國家之大禍。

translations.literal: If this boy is not destroyed today, it is the state's great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: If this boy is not destroyed today, it will be the state's great calamity.

sentences.zh: 脫待我無後，恐有永嘉之亂。

translations.literal: If you wait until I have no heir, I fear there will be chaos like the Yongjia era."
translations.idiomatic: If you wait until I have no heir, I fear chaos like the Yongjia era."

sentences.zh: 」乃廢為庶人，置之河陽；

translations.literal: He was deposed as commoner and placed at Heyang;
translations.idiomatic: He was deposed to commoner status and placed at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 服食所供，粗免饑寒而已。

translations.literal: food and clothing supplied were only enough roughly to escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Food and clothing were only enough roughly to escape hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 帝幸代，遂如長安，中尉李彪承閑密表，告恂復與左右謀逆。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Dai he then went as to Chang'an; Imperial Censor Li Biao seized an opening for a secret memorial, reporting that Xun again with his attendants plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Dai and then toward Chang'an, Imperial Censor Li Biao seized an opening for a secret memorial, reporting that Xun again plotted rebellion with his attendants.

sentences.zh: 帝在長安，使中書侍郎邢巒與咸陽王禧奉詔齎椒酒詣河陽，賜恂死。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Chang'an; he sent Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Luan with Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict with peppered wine, to Heyang and granted Xun death.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Chang'an; he sent Attendant of the Secretariat Xing Luan with Prince of Xianyang Xi, bearing an edict with peppered wine, to Heyang to grant Xun death.

sentences.zh: 時年十五餘。

translations.literal: At the time he was a little more than fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: He was a little more than fifteen.

sentences.zh: 斂以粗棺常服，瘞于河陽城。

translations.literal: He was encoffined in a coarse coffin in ordinary dress and buried in Heyang city.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in a coarse coffin in ordinary dress at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年冬，御史臺令史龍文觀坐法當死，告廷尉，稱恂前後被攝左右之日，有手書自理，不知狀。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-second year, Censorate clerk Long Wenguan sat for a crime that should die and reported to the Court of Justice that on the days when Xun was repeatedly taken by attendants left and right, there was a hand document of self-explanation whose circumstances he did not know.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-second year, censorate clerk Long Wenguan faced death for a crime and reported to the Court of Justice that on the days when Xun was repeatedly taken by attendants, there had been a handwritten plea whose circumstances he did not know.

sentences.zh: 而中尉李彪、侍御史賈尚寢不為聞。

translations.literal: But Imperial Censor Li Biao and Attending Censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: But Imperial Censor Li Biao and attending censor Jia Shang suppressed it and did not report.

sentences.zh: 賈坐系廷尉。

translations.literal: Jia sat in the Court of Justice for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jia was imprisoned in the Court of Justice for it.

sentences.zh: 時彪免歸，帝在鄴，尚書表收彪赴洛，會赦，遂不窮其本末。

translations.literal: At the time Biao was dismissed and returned home; the emperor was at Ye; the Ministry of Works memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; an amnesty came and the root and branch were not pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Biao had been dismissed and was home; the emperor was at Ye; the Ministry of Works memorialized to seize Biao and send him to Luoyang; an amnesty came and the matter was not pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 賈尚出系，暴病數日死。

translations.literal: Jia Shang left imprisonment; he suddenly fell ill and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Shang left prison, fell suddenly ill, and died within days.

sentences.zh: 初，帝將為恂娶司徒馮誕長女，以女幼，待年長，先為娉彭城劉長文、榮陽鄭懿女為左右孺子。

translations.literal: At first the emperor was about to marry Xun to the eldest daughter of Minister of Works Feng Dan; because the girl was young he waited until she was older; first he betrothed as left and right Ruzi the daughters of Pengcheng Liu Changwen and Rongyang Zheng Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor meant to marry Xun to Minister of Works Feng Dan's eldest daughter; because the girl was young he waited; first he betrothed as left and right ruzi the daughters of Liu Changwen of Pengcheng and Zheng Yi of Rongyang.

sentences.zh: 時恂年十三四，帝嘗謂郭祚、崔光、宋弁曰：「人生須自放，不可終朝讀書。

translations.literal: At the time Xun was thirteen or fourteen; the emperor once said to Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian: "A man's life must release himself; he cannot read books all morning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun was thirteen or fourteen the emperor once told Guo Zuo, Cui Guang, and Song Bian, "A man must sometimes release himself; he cannot read all morning.

sentences.zh: 我欲使恂旦出省經傳，食後還內，晡時復出，日夕而罷。

translations.literal: I wish Xun to go out in the morning to review the classics, return inside after eating, go out again at the hour of the monkey, and cease at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: I want Xun to go out in the morning to study the classics, return after the meal, go out again at the monkey hour, and cease at dusk.

sentences.zh: 卿等以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 」光曰：「孔子稱血氣未定，戒之在色。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Confucius said that when blood and qi are not settled, one is on guard against lust.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Confucius warned that when blood and qi are unsettled, one must guard against lust.

sentences.zh: 太子尚以幼年涉學之日，不宜於正晝之時，舍書禦內，又非所以安柔弱之體，固永年之命。

translations.literal: The crown prince is still in the years of first entering study; he ought not in the hours of full daylight leave books and enter the inner quarters; it is also not what secures a tender body and fixes the years of life."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is still in his first years of study; he ought not in broad daylight leave his books for the inner quarters; that is no way to secure a tender body and fix the years of life."

sentences.zh: 」帝以光言為然，乃不令恂晝入內。

translations.literal: The emperor took Guang's words as right and then did not have Xun enter inside in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took Guang's words as right and would not let Xun enter the inner quarters by day.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 京兆王愉字宣德，太和二十一年封，拜都督、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande, was enfeoffed in the twenty-first year of Taihe and made Commander-in-Chief and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jingzhao Yu, styled Xuande, was enfeoffed in Taihe 21 and made commander-in-chief and governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以彭城王中宣府長史盧陽烏兼長史，州事巨細，委之陽烏。

translations.literal: He made Prince of Pengcheng's Central Propaganda Office senior administrator Lu Yangwu concurrent senior administrator; all details of the province were entrusted to Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He made Prince of Pengcheng's senior administrator of the Central Propaganda Office Lu Yangwu concurrent senior administrator; every detail of the province was entrusted to Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，為護軍將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Xuandi he was General Who Protects the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuandi's reign he was general who protects the army.

sentences.zh: 帝留愛諸弟，愉等常出入宮掖，晨昏寢處，若家人焉。

translations.literal: The emperor kept his beloved younger brothers; Yu and the others often went in and out of the palace women's quarters, morning and evening lodging like family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kept his beloved younger brothers near; Yu and the others often entered the palace women's quarters and lodged morning and evening like family.

sentences.zh: 遷中書監。

translations.literal: He was moved to Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為納順皇后妹為妃，而不見禮答。

translations.literal: He took as consort the younger sister of Empress Shun but did not answer her with ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: He took Empress Shun's younger sister as consort but never answered her with the courtesy owed a wife.

sentences.zh: 愉在徐州納妾李氏，本姓楊，東郡人，夜聞其歌，悅之，遂被寵嬖。

translations.literal: Yu at Xuzhou took a concubine Lady Li, originally surnamed Yang of Dongjun; at night he heard her song, was pleased, and she came to be favored.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou Yu took a concubine, Lady Li, born Yang of Dongjun; hearing her sing at night he was pleased, and she won his favor.

sentences.zh: 罷州還京，欲進貴之。

translations.literal: When he left the province and returned to the capital he wished to advance her to honored status.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the province for the capital he wished to raise her to honored status.

sentences.zh: 托右中郎將趙郡李恃顯為之養父，就之禮迎，產子寶月。

translations.literal: He entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao commandery to be her adoptive father and went through the rites to welcome her; she bore the son Baoyue.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted Right Gentleman of the Palace Li Shixian of Zhao to be her adoptive father, welcomed her by rite, and she bore the son Baoyue.

sentences.zh: 順皇后召李入宮，毀擊之。

translations.literal: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace and beat and injured her.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Shun summoned Li into the palace and beat her until she was injured.

sentences.zh: 強令為尼於內，以子付妃養之。

translations.literal: She was forced to become a nun inside; the son was given to the consort to rear.
translations.idiomatic: She was forced to become a nun inside the palace; the son was given to the consort to rear.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，後父于勁以後久無所誕，乃表勸廣嬪御。

translations.literal: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long had borne no child, then memorialized urging broadening of the secondary harem.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the empress's father Yu Jin, because the empress long bore no child, memorialized urging a broader harem.

sentences.zh: 因令後歸李於愉，舊愛更甚。

translations.literal: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love was even greater.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he had the empress return Li to Yu; the old love burned hotter.

sentences.zh: 愉好文章，頗著詩賦。

translations.literal: Yu loved letters and was quite accomplished in poetry and rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Yu loved letters and was accomplished in poetry and rhapsody.

sentences.zh: 時引才人宋世景、李神俊、祖瑩、邢晏、王遵業、張始均等，共申宴喜。

translations.literal: At the time he often drew men of talent Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others to share feasts and joy.
translations.idiomatic: He often drew men of talent—Song Shijing, Li Shenjun, Zu Ying, Xing Yan, Wang Zunye, Zhang Shiqi, and others—to share feasts and joy.

sentences.zh: 招四方儒學賓客嚴懷真等數十人，館而禮之。

translations.literal: He recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four quarters such as Yan Huaiyan and lodged and honored them.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited several tens of Confucian guests from the four quarters, such as Yan Huaiyan, lodged them, and honored them.

sentences.zh: 所得穀帛，率多散施。

translations.literal: The grain and cloth he received he mostly gave away in distribution.
translations.idiomatic: The grain and cloth he received he mostly gave away.

sentences.zh: 又崇信佛道，用度常至不接。

translations.literal: He also honored and believed in the Buddhist Way; expenses often reached the point of not meeting needs.
translations.idiomatic: He also honored the Buddhist way; his expenses often outran his means.

sentences.zh: 與弟廣平王懷，頗相誇尚，競慕奢麗，貪縱不法。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Prince of Guangping Huai he quite mutually boasted and admired, competing in extravagant splendor, greedy and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: With his younger brother Prince of Guangping Huai he boasted and admired each other, competing in splendor, greedy and lawless.

sentences.zh: 於是宣武攝愉禁中推案，杖愉五十，出為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xuandi confined Yu in the palace to investigate, beat Yu fifty blows, and sent him out as Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Xuandi confined Yu in the palace to investigate, beat him fifty blows, and sent him out as governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 始愉自以職求侍要，勢劣二弟，潛懷愧恨，頗見言色。

translations.literal: At first Yu himself thought that in office he sought attendance on important matters, his power weaker than his two younger brothers, and secretly harbored shame and resentment, often showing it in words and looks.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yu had sought attendance on weighty affairs by office, found his power weaker than his two younger brothers, and secretly nursed shame and resentment, often showing it in word and face.

sentences.zh: 又以幸妾屢被頓辱，內外離抑。

translations.literal: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, inside and outside were estranged and suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Also because his favored concubine was repeatedly humiliated, he was estranged within and suppressed without.

sentences.zh: 及在州，謀逆。

translations.literal: When he was in the province he plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 愉遂殺長史羊靈引及司馬李遵，稱得清河王密疏，雲高肇謀為殺害主上。

translations.literal: Yu then killed Senior Administrator Yang Lingyin and Marshal Li Zun, claiming to have received a secret document from Prince of Qinghe saying Gao Zhao plotted to kill the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then killed Senior Administrator Yang Lingyin and Marshal Li Zun, claiming a secret document from Prince of Qinghe that Gao Zhao plotted to kill the ruler.

sentences.zh: 遂為壇於信都之南，柴燎告天，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: He then made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial position.
translations.idiomatic: He made an altar south of Xindu, burned firewood and reported to Heaven, and at once took the imperial position.

sentences.zh: 赦天下，號建平元年，立李氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He amnestied the realm, era name Jianping 1, and established Lady Li as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He amnestied the realm, proclaimed the era Jianping 1, and made Lady Li empress.

sentences.zh: 宣武詔尚書李平討愉。

translations.literal: Xuandi ordered Minister of Works Li Ping to attack Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuandi ordered Minister of Works Li Ping to attack Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉出拒王師，頻敗，遂嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then surrounded the city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu went out to resist the imperial army, was repeatedly defeated, and then held the city under siege.

sentences.zh: 愉知事窮，攜李及四子數十騎出門，諸軍追之，見執以送。

translations.literal: Yu knew affairs were exhausted; he took Li and several tens of sons on several tens of horses and went out the gate; the armies pursued and seized and sent him.
translations.idiomatic: When he knew all was lost he took Li and several sons on several tens of horses out the gate; the armies pursued, seized him, and sent him on.

sentences.zh: 詔征赴京師，申以家人之訓。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with familial teaching.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to the capital and admonished him with familial teaching.

sentences.zh: 愉每止宿亭傳，必攜李手，盡其私情。

translations.literal: Whenever Yu stopped at a post station he always took Li by the hand and exhausted private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he stopped at a post station he took Li by the hand and gave himself to private feeling.

sentences.zh: 雖鎖縶之中，飲賞自若，略無愧懼之色。

translations.literal: Though in chains he drank and feasted as before, with hardly a look of shame or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Though in chains he drank and feasted as before, with hardly a look of shame or fear.

sentences.zh: 至野王，愉語人曰：「雖主上慈深，不忍殺我，吾亦何以面見至尊！

translations.literal: At Yewang Yu said to others: "Though the ruler is deeply merciful and cannot bear to kill me, how can I face the August One!"
translations.idiomatic: At Yewang Yu told others, "Though the ruler is deeply merciful and cannot bear to kill me, how can I face the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」於是歔欷流涕，絕氣而死，年二十一。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sobbed, wept, and stopped breathing; he died at twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he sobbed, wept, and stopped breathing; he died at twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 或云高肇令人殺之。

translations.literal: Some say Gao Zhao had a man kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Some say Gao Zhao had a man kill him.

sentences.zh: 斂以小棺，瘞。

translations.literal: He was encoffined in a small coffin and buried.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in a small coffin.

sentences.zh: 諸子至洛，皆赦之。

translations.literal: The sons reached Luoyang and were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: His sons reached Luoyang and were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後靈太后令愉之四子皆附屬籍，追封愉臨洮王。

translations.literal: Later Empress Dowager Ling ordered Yu's four sons all attached to the register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu Prince of Lintao.
translations.idiomatic: Later Empress Dowager Ling had Yu's four sons attached to the register and posthumously enfeoffed Yu as Prince of Lintao.

sentences.zh: 寶月乃改葬父母，追服三年。

translations.literal: Baoyue then reburied his parents and observed mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyue then reburied his parents and observed three years of mourning.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌字宣仁，幼而敏慧，美姿貌，孝文愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Yi, styled Xuanren, in youth was clever and wise, handsome of bearing; Xiaowen loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qinghe Yi, styled Xuanren, was clever and wise in youth, handsome of bearing; Xiaowen loved him.

sentences.zh: 彭城王勰甚器異之，並曰：「此兒風神外偉，黃中內潤，若天假之年，繼二南矣。

translations.literal: Prince of Pengcheng Xie greatly prized and marked him apart, and together said: "This boy's spirit is outwardly grand, inwardly rich at the core; if Heaven grants years, he will continue the Two Souths."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie prized him greatly and said with others, "This boy's spirit is grand without and rich within; if Heaven grants him years, he will continue the Two Souths."

sentences.zh: 」博涉經史，兼綜群言，有文才，善談理。

translations.literal: He broadly traversed the classics and histories and comprehensively joined many schools; he had literary talent and was skilled in discourse on principle.
translations.idiomatic: He ranged broadly through the classics and histories, took in many schools, had literary talent, and was skilled in discourse on principle.

sentences.zh: 寬仁容裕，喜怒不形於色。

translations.literal: Broad in kindness, ample in forbearance; joy and anger did not show on his face.
translations.idiomatic: He was broad-minded and forbearing; joy and anger never showed on his face.

sentences.zh: 太和二十一年封。

translations.literal: In Taihe twenty-first year he was enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed in Taihe 21.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，拜侍中，轉尚書僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanwu's reign he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary, then transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xuanwu's reign he was made Attendant-in-Ordinary, then Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 懌才長從政，明於斷決，剖判眾務，甚有聲名。

translations.literal: Yi was talented in government, clear in judgment, dissecting and deciding the multitude of affairs; he had great renown.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had a gift for government and a clear judgment; he cut through the mass of affairs and won great renown.

sentences.zh: 司空高肇以帝舅寵任，既擅威權，謀去良宗，屢譖懌及愉等。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Gao Zhao, as the emperor's uncle-in-law, was favored and entrusted; once he monopolized authority, he plotted to remove worthy princes and repeatedly slandered Yi, Yu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhao, the emperor's uncle by marriage, held the post of Minister of Works and won favor until he monopolized power; he plotted against worthy princes and repeatedly slandered Yi, Yu, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 愉不勝其忿怒，遂舉逆冀州。

translations.literal: Yu could not bear his rage and therefore rose in rebellion in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu could not contain his fury and rose in rebellion in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 因愉之逆，又構殺勰。

translations.literal: Because of Yu's rebellion, he also framed and killed Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Using Yu's rebellion as pretext, he also framed and killed Xie.

sentences.zh: 懌恐不免。

translations.literal: Yi feared he could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Yi feared he would not escape.

sentences.zh: 肇又錄囚徒以立私惠。

translations.literal: Zhao also recorded prisoners to establish private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao also reviewed prisoners to curry private favor.

sentences.zh: 懌因侍宴，酒酣，乃謂肇曰：「天子兄弟，詎有幾人，而炎炎不息？

translations.literal: Yi, taking advantage of attendance at a feast, when the wine was deep, then said to Zhao: "The Son of Heaven's brothers—how many are there, that you blaze on without cease?
translations.idiomatic: At a feast, deep in wine, Yi said to Zhao, "How many brothers does the Son of Heaven have, that you burn on without cease?

sentences.zh: 昔王莽頭禿，亦藉渭陽之資，遂篡漢室。

translations.literal: In old times Wang Mang was bald-headed, yet by his tie through the Weiyang marriage he seized the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang was bald, yet by his kinship through the Weiyang side he seized the Han throne.

sentences.zh: 今君曲形見矣，恐復終成亂階。

translations.literal: Now your crooked form is plain to see; I fear you will again complete the steps of chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Your bent shape is plain to see now; I fear you will again make the ladder of chaos."

sentences.zh: 」又言于宣武曰：「臣聞唯器與名，不可以假人。

translations.literal: He also said to Emperor Xuanwu: "I have heard that only vessels and names may not be lent to others.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Emperor Xuanwu, "I have heard that only rank and title must never be lent away.

sentences.zh: 是故季氏旅泰山，宣尼以為深譏；

translations.literal: Therefore when the Ji clan performed the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Confucius held it deep reproach;
translations.idiomatic: When the Ji clan offered the Feng sacrifice on Mount Tai, Confucius took it as deep reproach;

sentences.zh: 仲叔軒懸，丘明以為至誡。

translations.literal: when Zhongsun hung the royal bells, Qiu Ming took it as the utmost warning.
translations.idiomatic: when Zhongsun hung the royal bells, Qiu Ming called it the utmost warning.

sentences.zh: 諒以天尊地卑，君臣道別。

translations.literal: Surely Heaven is honored and Earth is low; ruler and subject have separate ways.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is high and Earth low; ruler and subject walk separate roads.

sentences.zh: 宜杜漸防萌，無相僭越。

translations.literal: One should stop the first sprout and guard against what buds; let none overstep.
translations.idiomatic: One should choke the sprout and bar encroachment.

sentences.zh: 至於減膳錄囚，人君之事，今乃司徒行之，詎是人臣之義？

translations.literal: As for reducing meals and recording prisoners—these are a ruler's affairs; now the Minister of Works performs them—how is that the meaning of a subject?
translations.idiomatic: Reducing the royal table and reviewing prisoners belong to the ruler; now the Minister of Works does them—what part of that is a subject's duty?

sentences.zh: 且陛下修政教，解獄訟，則時雨可降，玉燭知和。

translations.literal: Moreover, if Your Majesty cultivates government and teaching and releases prisoners from litigation, then timely rain may descend and the jade candle know harmony.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty cultivates government and teaching and clears the courts, timely rain will fall and the jade candle of peace will glow.

sentences.zh: 何使明君失之于上，奸臣竊之于下？

translations.literal: Why let a bright ruler lose them above while a treacherous minister steals them below?
translations.idiomatic: Why should a bright ruler lose them above while a treacherous minister steals them below?

sentences.zh: 長亂之基，於此在矣。

translations.literal: The root of long chaos lies here."
translations.idiomatic: The root of lasting chaos is here."

sentences.zh: 」宣武笑而不應。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanwu smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 孝明熙平初，遷太尉，侍中如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's Xiping era he was transferred to Grand Commandant, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaoming's Xiping era he was made Grand Commandant while remaining Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 詔懌裁門下之事，又典經義注。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Yi to decide affairs of the Gate and Canon, and also to oversee classical commentary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Yi in charge of Gate-and-Canon affairs and classical commentary.

sentences.zh: 時有沙門惠憐者，自雲咒水飲人，能差諸病。

translations.literal: At the time there was a monk Huilian who claimed that chanting water and having people drink it could cure all illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Huilian claimed that enchanted water, drunk by the sick, could cure every illness.

sentences.zh: 病人就之者，日有千數。

translations.literal: Those who came to him with illness numbered a thousand a day.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand sufferers came to him each day.

sentences.zh: 靈太后詔給衣食。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling ordered food and clothing provided.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling ordered food and clothing supplied.

sentences.zh: 事力優重，使於城西之南，治療百姓病。

translations.literal: His support was especially heavy; he was sent to the south of the western city to treat the people's illnesses.
translations.idiomatic: His support was lavish; he was sent south of the western city to treat the people's illnesses.

sentences.zh: 懌表諫曰：「臣聞律深惑眾之科，禮絕妖淫之禁，皆所以大明居正，防遏奸邪。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized in remonstrance: "I have heard that the law sets severe penalties for deluding the masses, and ritual cuts off perverse sorcery—all to make clear the upright position and bar treacherous evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "The law sets heavy penalties for deluding the masses; ritual cuts off perverse sorcery—both to mark the upright seat and bar treachery.

sentences.zh: 昔在漢末，有張角者，亦以此術，熒惑當時。

translations.literal: In old times at the end of Han there was Zhang Jiao, who also used this art and bewitched his age.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han, Zhang Jiao used this same art and bewitched his age.

sentences.zh: 論其所行，與今不異。

translations.literal: Judging what he did, it does not differ from today.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by his acts, it does not differ from today.

sentences.zh: 遂能詃誘生人，致黃巾之禍。

translations.literal: He could entice the living and bring on the disaster of the Yellow Turbans.
translations.idiomatic: He could lure the living and bring on the Yellow Turban disaster.

sentences.zh: 天下塗炭數十年間，角之由也。

translations.literal: For decades the realm was scorched—Jiao was the cause.
translations.idiomatic: For decades the realm burned—and Jiao was the cause.

sentences.zh: 昔新垣奸，不登於明堂；

translations.literal: In old times the charlatan Xinyuan did not ascend the Bright Hall;
translations.idiomatic: The charlatan Xinyuan never reached the Bright Hall;

sentences.zh: 五利僥，終嬰於顯戮。

translations.literal: Wuli the opportunist in the end met execution before the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Wuli the opportunist in the end met public execution.

sentences.zh: 靈太后以懌孝明懿叔，德先具瞻，委以朝政，事擬周、霍。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling, because Yi was Xiaoming's worthy uncle, his virtue foremost in all eyes, entrusted him with court government, affairs comparable to the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling, seeing Yi as Xiaoming's worthy uncle and a man all eyes followed, entrusted him with government on the model of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang.

sentences.zh: 懌竭力匡輔，以天下為己任。

translations.literal: Yi strove with all his strength to support and correct, taking the realm as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Yi strove to support and correct the realm and took the empire as his charge.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉，太后之妹夫也，恃寵驕盈。

translations.literal: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's sister's husband, relied on favor and was arrogant and full.
translations.idiomatic: Commander of the Guards Yuan Cha, the empress dowager's brother-in-law, leaned on favor and swelled with pride.

sentences.zh: 懌裁之以法，每抑黜之，為叉所疾。

translations.literal: Yi restrained him by law and repeatedly suppressed and demoted him; Cha came to hate him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi restrained him by law and repeatedly suppressed and demoted him; Cha came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 叉党人通直郎宋准愛希又旨，告懌謀反。

translations.literal: A partisan of Cha's, Direct Attendant Song Zhun, eager for Cha's intent, reported that Yi plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Cha's partisan, Direct Attendant Song Zhun, eager to please him, reported that Yi plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 禁懌門下，訊問左右及朝貴，貴人分明，得雪，乃釋焉。

translations.literal: Yi was confined at the Gate; when his attendants and court nobles were questioned, the nobles spoke clearly and he was cleared, then released.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was confined at the Gate; when attendants and court nobles were questioned, they spoke clearly, he was cleared, and released.

sentences.zh: 懌以忠而獲謗，乃鳩集昔忠烈之士，為《顯忠錄》二十卷以見意焉。

translations.literal: Yi, loyal yet slandered, then gathered former loyal and stalwart men and made Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal yet slandered, Yi gathered former loyal and stalwart men and compiled Records of Manifest Loyalty in twenty scrolls to declare his intent.

sentences.zh: 正光元年七月，叉與劉騰逼孝明于顯陽殿，閉靈太后于後宮，囚懌于門下省。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhengguang, Cha and Liu Teng forced Xiaoming in the Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, and imprisoned Yi in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhengguang 1, Cha and Liu Teng seized Xiaoming in the Xianyang Hall, shut Empress Dowager Ling in the rear palace, and imprisoned Yi in the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 懌罪伏，遂害之，時年三十四。

translations.literal: Yi, his crime confessed, was then killed; he was thirty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Once his guilt was recorded, Yi was killed; he was thirty-four.

sentences.zh: 朝野貴賤，知與不知，含悲喪氣，驚振遠近。

translations.literal: Court and countryside, noble and base, knowing and not knowing, held grief and lost breath; shock shook far and near.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside, noble and base, all who knew him and all who did not, grieved and caught their breath; shock ran far and near.

sentences.zh: 夷人在京及歸，聞懌之喪，為之劈面者數百人。

translations.literal: Barbarians in the capital and those returning, hearing of Yi's death, numbered several hundred who gashed their faces for him.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians in the capital and those returning, hearing of Yi's death, numbered several hundred who gashed their faces in mourning.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷，闕自有魏諸王，召入華林別館，禁其出入。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Huai, among all princes of Wei from the beginning, was summoned into the separate lodge of the Hualin Garden and forbidden to go out or in.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Huai, among all Wei princes from the founding, was summoned to the Hualin separate lodge and forbidden to leave.

sentences.zh: 令四門博士董征授以經傳。

translations.literal: He ordered the Four Gates academician Dong Zheng to teach him the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Four Gates academician Dong Zheng to teach him the classics.

sentences.zh: 孝武崩，乃得歸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu died, he was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 汝南王悅，好讀佛經，覽書史；

translations.literal: Prince of Runan Yue loved reading Buddhist sutras and perusing histories;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Runan Yue loved Buddhist sutras and histories;

sentences.zh: 為性不倫，俶儻難測。

translations.literal: his nature was unorthodox, free and hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: his nature was unorthodox, untamed and hard to read.

sentences.zh: 悅妃閭氏，即東海公之女也。

translations.literal: Yue's consort, the Lady Yan, was daughter of the Duke of Donghai.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's consort Lady Yan was daughter of the Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 生一子，不見禮答。

translations.literal: She bore one son but received no courteous regard.
translations.idiomatic: She bore a son but won no courteous regard.

sentences.zh: 有崔延夏者，以左道與悅遊。

translations.literal: There was Cui Yanxia, who by heterodox ways kept company with Yue.
translations.idiomatic: One Cui Yanxia kept company with Yue by heterodox ways.

sentences.zh: 合服仙藥松術之屬，時輕與出采之，宿於城外小人之所。

translations.literal: Together they took immortality drugs of pine and artemisia; at times he went out lightly to gather them and lodged in commoners' dwellings outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Together they took immortality drugs of pine and artemisia; at times he went out lightly to gather them and lodged in hovels outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 遂斷酒肉粟稻，唯食麥飯。

translations.literal: He then cut off wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat porridge.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave up wine, meat, millet, and rice and ate only wheat porridge.

sentences.zh: 又絕房中，而更好男色。

translations.literal: He also ceased the bedchamber and instead favored male beauty.
translations.idiomatic: He also ceased the bedchamber and favored male beauty instead.

sentences.zh: 輕忿妃妾，至加捶撻，同之婢使。

translations.literal: He lightly resented his consorts and concubines, even beating them, treating them like maids.
translations.idiomatic: He lightly resented consorts and concubines, even beating them like maids.

sentences.zh: 悅之出也，妃住於別第，靈太后敕檢問之。

translations.literal: When Yue went out, the consort stayed at a separate residence; Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue went out, the consort stayed at a separate residence; Empress Dowager Ling ordered an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 引入，窮悅事故。

translations.literal: She was brought in and Yue's conduct was pursued to the end.
translations.idiomatic: She was brought in and Yue's conduct was pursued to the end.

sentences.zh: 妃病杖床蓐，瘡尚未愈。

translations.literal: The consort was ill on her bed with the cane; her wounds were not yet healed.
translations.idiomatic: The consort lay ill on her bed with the cane; her wounds were not yet healed.

sentences.zh: 太后因悅杖妃，乃下令禁斷。

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because Yue had caned the consort, then ordered a ban.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yue had caned the consort, the empress dowager ordered a ban.

sentences.zh: 令諸親王及三蕃，其有正妃病患百日已上，皆遣奏聞。

translations.literal: She ordered all imperial princes and the three frontier princes that if a principal consort was ill more than a hundred days, all were to report it.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered all imperial princes and the three frontier princes: if a principal consort was ill more than a hundred days, they must report it.

sentences.zh: 若有猶行捶撻，就削封位。

translations.literal: If any still beat them, their enfeoffment was to be cut on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: If any still beat them, their fief was to be cut on the spot.

sentences.zh: 及清河王懌為元叉所害，悅了無仇恨之意，乃以桑落酒候伺之，盡其私佞。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue had not the slightest hatred but instead waited on him with mulberry-leaf wine and gave his full private fawning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yi was killed by Yuan Cha, Yue felt no hatred but waited on him with mulberry-leaf wine and fawned with all his private arts.

sentences.zh: 叉大喜，以悅為侍中、太尉。

translations.literal: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Cha was greatly pleased and made Yue Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 臨拜日，就懌子亶求懌服玩之物。

translations.literal: On the day of his appointment he went to Yi's son Dan and asked for Yi's robes and curios.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of appointment he went to Yi's son Dan and demanded Yi's robes and curios.

sentences.zh: 不時稱旨，乃召亶杖之百下。

translations.literal: When they did not promptly please him, he summoned Dan and caned him a hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: When they did not promptly please him, he summoned Dan and caned him a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 亶居廬未葬，形氣羸弱，暴加威撻，殆至不濟。

translations.literal: Dan was in mourning hut, his form and breath frail and weak; sudden harsh beating nearly brought him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was still in the mourning hut, frail in body and breath; sudden harsh beating nearly killed him.

sentences.zh: 仍呼阿兒，親自循撫。

translations.literal: He then called "Little son" and personally stroked and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: He then called "Little son" and personally stroked and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 悅乃為大剉碓，置於州門，盜者便欲斬其手。
