translations.literal: Yue then made a great mortar-pestle and set it at the province gate; thieves were at once to have their hands cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then set a great mortar-pestle at the province gate; thieves were to have their hands cut off at once.

sentences.zh: 時人懼其無常，能行異事，奸偷畏之而暫息。

translations.literal: People feared his unpredictability and that he could do strange things; thieves and rogues feared him and for a time ceased.
translations.idiomatic: People feared his unpredictability and strange deeds; thieves and rogues feared him and for a time ceased.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮舉兵向洛，悅遂奔梁。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, Yue then fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong marched on Luoyang, Yue fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁武厚相資待。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 莊帝崩，遂立為魏主，號年更興。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang died, he was then set up as ruler of Wei, the era name changed to Gengxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang died, he was set up as ruler of Wei under the era name Gengxing.

sentences.zh: 節閔初，遣兵送悅，置於境上，以覬侵逼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiemin, troops were sent to escort Yue and place him on the border to watch for invasion.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiemin's reign, troops escorted Yue to the border to watch for invasion.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武既誅爾硃，以悅孝文子，宜承大業，乃令人示意。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu had killed the Erzhu clan, because Yue was Xiaowen's son and ought to inherit the great enterprise, he had a man convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan had killed the Erzhu clan, holding that Yue, as Xiaowen's son, ought to inherit the throne, he sent a man to convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 悅既至，清狂如故，動為罪失，乃止。

translations.literal: When Yue arrived, he was wild and unrestrained as before, constantly committing faults; they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue arrived, he was as wild as before and constantly erred; they dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，除大司馬、開府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiaowu he was appointed Grand Marshal and Defender-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiaowu's reign he was made Grand Marshal and Defender-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 孝武以廣陵頗有德望，以悅屬尊地近，內懷畏忌，故前後害之。

translations.literal: Xiaowu, because Guangling had considerable virtue and renown, and because Yue by kin was close in rank and near in territory, inwardly feared and was jealous; therefore he killed him before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowu, because Guangling had virtue and renown and Yue was close in kin and territory, feared and resented him inwardly and killed him in time.

sentences.zh: 贈假黃鉞、太師、司州牧，大司馬、王如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Governor of Sizhou, Grand Marshal, and prince as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the Acting Yellow Battle-Ax, Grand Preceptor, Governor of Sizhou, Grand Marshal, and his princedom as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: Posthumous name: Wén Xuān.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous title: Literary and Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 子穎，與父俱奔梁，遂卒于江左。

translations.literal: His son Ying, with his father, fled together to Liang and died on the left bank of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying fled to Liang with his father and died on the Yangtze's southern bank.

sentences.zh: 皇子恌，年七歲，景明元年薨，就斂于華林棗間堂，葬于文昭皇后陵東。

translations.literal: The imperial son Tao, seven years old, died in the first year of Jingming; he was coffined in the Jujian Hall amid the Hualin jujubes and buried east of Empress Wen Zhao's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial son Tao, seven years old, died in Jingming 1; he was coffined in the Jujian Hall amid the Hualin jujubes and buried east of Empress Wen Zhao's tomb.

sentences.zh: 後以增廣文昭後墳塋，徙窆北崗。

translations.literal: Later, to enlarge Wen Zhao's rear mound, he was moved and reburied on the northern ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Later, to enlarge Wen Zhao's rear mound, he was moved and reburied on the northern ridge.

sentences.zh: 論曰：文成五王，安豐特標令望。

translations.literal: Discussion: Among Wen Cheng's five sons, Anfeng alone bore outstanding repute.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Among Wen Cheng's five sons, only Anfeng bore outstanding repute.

sentences.zh: 延明學業該贍，加以雅談之美；

translations.literal: Yanming's learning was comprehensive, joined to the beauty of elegant discourse;
translations.idiomatic: Yanming's learning was comprehensive, joined to elegant discourse;

sentences.zh: 及于永安，運跡冠戎。

translations.literal: reaching Yong'an, his fortune's track topped the army.
translations.idiomatic: by Yong'an his fortune topped the armies.

sentences.zh: 卒致奔亡，亦其命也。

translations.literal: In the end he met flight and ruin—also his fate.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he met flight and ruin—also his fate.

sentences.zh: 獻文諸子，俱漸太和之訓，而咸陽終於逆節，廣陵斃于桑中。

translations.literal: Xianwen's sons all gradually received Taihe instruction, yet Xianyang ended in rebellious conduct and Guangling died in the mulberry grove.
translations.idiomatic: Xianwen's sons all received Taihe instruction, yet Xianyang ended in rebellion and Guangling died in the mulberry grove.

sentences.zh: 人而無儀，各宜遄死。

translations.literal: A man without propriety—each should hurry to his death.
translations.idiomatic: Men without propriety—each should hurry to his death.

sentences.zh: 高陽器術缺然，終荷棟幹，至於橈敗，實屍其闕。

translations.literal: Gaoyang's capacity and art were wanting, yet in the end he bore the pillar and beam; when the timbers broke, in truth the corpse lay in his lack.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoyang lacked capacity and art, yet in the end bore pillar and beam; when the timbers broke, the corpse lay in his lack.

sentences.zh: 武宣孝以為質，忠而樹行，及夫在安處危之操，送往事居之節，周旦匪佗之旨，霍光異姓之誠，事實兼之。

translations.literal: Wuxuan's filiality was his substance; loyalty built his conduct; as for bearing danger in safety and the constancy of seeing off the past and dwelling on what follows, the Duke of Zhou's intent that was not another's, and Huo Guang's faith of a different surname—the facts joined both.
translations.idiomatic: Wuxuan's filiality was his substance and loyalty built his conduct; bearing danger in safety, constancy in seeing off the past and dwelling on what follows—the Duke of Zhou's intent not given to another, Huo Guang's faith though of another surname—he joined both in fact.

sentences.zh: 竟而功高震主，德隆動俗。

translations.literal: Yet in the end merit high shook the ruler; virtue lofty moved custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end merit so high shook the ruler; virtue so lofty moved custom.

sentences.zh: 閑言一入，卒不全生。

translations.literal: One idle word entered, and in the end he did not keep his life whole.
translations.idiomatic: One idle word entered, and in the end he did not keep his life.

sentences.zh: 鳴呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 周成、漢昭未易遇也。

translations.literal: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were not easy to meet.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han were not easy to meet.

sentences.zh: 北海義昧鶺鴒，奢淫自喪，雖禍發青蠅，亦自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Beihai's righteousness was dim on the magpie and wagtail; luxury and excess destroyed himself—though disaster rose from the green fly, he also brought the sorrow on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Beihai's righteousness dimmed on the magpie and wagtail; luxury and excess destroyed him—though disaster rose from the green fly, he brought the sorrow on himself.

sentences.zh: 顥取若拾遺，亡不旋踵，豈守之無術，其天將覆之。

translations.literal: Hao took as if picking up lost things; ruin did not turn the heel—is it that guarding had no method, or Heaven was about to overturn?
translations.idiomatic: Hao took power as if picking up lost things; ruin came without turning the heel—was guarding without method, or was Heaven about to overturn?

sentences.zh: 庶人險暴之性，自幼而長，終以廢黜，不得其終。

translations.literal: The commoner's violent and fierce nature, from childhood growing to length, in the end was deposed and dismissed and did not obtain his end.
translations.idiomatic: The commoner's violent nature, growing from childhood to manhood, in the end was deposed and did not obtain his end.

sentences.zh: 斯乃硃、均之性，堯、舜不能訓也。

translations.literal: This is the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the nature of Zhu and Jun; Yao and Shun could not instruct it.

sentences.zh: 京兆早有令問，晚致顛覆，習於所染，可不慎乎！

translations.literal: Jingzhao early had fair renown; late he met overturn—accustomed to what stained him; can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao early won fair renown; late he met ruin—habit from what stained him. Can one not be cautious?

sentences.zh: 清河器識才譽，以懿親作輔，時鐘屯詖，始遘牆茨之逼。

translations.literal: Qinghe's capacity, insight, talent, and fame—as a close kinsman made counselor, when the bell of hardship tolled, he first met the wall-thorn's press.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe's capacity, insight, talent, and fame—as a close kinsman made counselor, when hardship tolled, he first met the wall-thorn's press.

sentences.zh: 運屬道消，晚扼凶權之手。

translations.literal: Fortune belonged to the Way's decline; late he was throttled in the hand of fierce power.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune met the Way's decline; late he was throttled by fierce power.

sentences.zh: 悲哉！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 廣平早歲驕盈，汝南性致狂逸，揆其終始，俱不足論。

translations.literal: Guangping in early years was arrogant and full; Runan by nature tended to wild excess; judging beginning and end, both scarcely merit discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Guangping in early years was arrogant and full; Runan by nature tended to wild excess; judged from beginning to end, both scarcely merit discussion.

sentences.zh: 而悅以天人所棄，卒嬰猜懼之毒，蓋地逼之尤也。

translations.literal: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, in the end met the poison of suspicion and fear—surely the extreme of being pressed by the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yue, abandoned by Heaven and men, in the end met the poison of suspicion and fear—surely the extreme of a prince pressed too near the throne.

sentences.zh: 魏自西遷之後，權移周室。

translations.literal: From the time Wei moved west, power shifted to the Zhou house.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Wei moved west, power shifted to the Zhou house.

sentences.zh: 而周文天縱寬仁，性罕猜忌；

translations.literal: Yet King Wen of Zhou was heaven-endowed, broad and kind, his nature rarely suspicious;
translations.idiomatic: Yet King Wen of Zhou was heaven-endowed, broad and kind, rarely suspicious;

sentences.zh: 元氏戚屬，並見保全，內外任使，布於列職。

translations.literal: the Yuan clan kin were all preserved; within and without they were employed and spread through the ranks of office.
translations.idiomatic: the Yuan kin were all preserved and employed within and without across the ranks of office.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐祚，無替前緒，明武纘業，亦遵先志。

translations.literal: When Xiaomin ascended, he did not replace the former thread; Mingwu continued the enterprise and also followed the former intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaomin ascended, he did not break the former thread; Mingwu continued the enterprise and followed the former intent.

sentences.zh: 雖天厭魏德，鼎命已遷，枝葉榮茂，足以愈於前代矣。

translations.literal: Though Heaven tired of Wei's virtue and the tripod mandate had shifted, branches and leaves flourished lush—enough to surpass the former age.
translations.idiomatic: Though Heaven tired of Wei's virtue and the mandate had shifted, branches and leaves flourished enough to surpass the former age.
